The company also plans to direct a [[meaningful portion of its resources|p943]] toward broad access to frontier AI.

children.title: Personnel
children.tldr: Personnel costs, mainly stock-based compensation and salaries, will grow with headcount, and the IPO will trigger additional stock-based compensation on certain RSUs.
children.summary: Personnel expenses consist mainly of [[stock-based compensation, cash compensation, benefits and payroll taxes|p944]]. Anthropic expects them to rise with headcount and to include [[additional stock-based compensation tied to this offering|p945]], including RSUs whose performance condition is met when the registration statement becomes effective.

children.title: Bartz settlement
children.tldr: The Bartz settlement line is the charge Anthropic recorded in 2025 to settle the Bartz litigation.
children.summary: This line reflects the [[charge recorded in 2025|p946]] to settle the Bartz litigation, detailed in Note 13.

children.title: Sales, Marketing, and Partnerships
children.tldr: Sales, marketing, and partnerships spending, mostly channel partner fees and advertising, will rise in dollars and swing as a share of revenue with campaigns and partner terms.
children.summary: These expenses are mainly [[fees paid to channel partners and marketing and advertising costs|p947]]. Anthropic expects them to grow in dollars and to [[fluctuate as a share of revenue|p948]] with campaign timing and changes in channel partner terms.

children.title: Other Operating and Administrative
children.tldr: Other operating and administrative costs, including donation matching and vendor services, will rise with growth, public company obligations and a significant scaling of public benefit programs.
children.summary: This line includes [[charitable donation matching, data quality vendors, IT and cloud software, payment processing, facilities, taxes and professional services|p949]]. Anthropic expects it to increase as it grows and takes on [[public company costs|p950]] such as SEC and Nasdaq compliance and D&O insurance. It may also swing as a share of revenue as the company [[significantly scales its public benefit initiatives|p950]], such as access programs and charitable matching.

children.title: Interest Income
children.tldr: Interest income comes from cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments such as Treasury and agency securities, corporate debt and commercial paper.
children.summary: Interest income is earned on [[cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments|p951]], mostly debt securities.

children.title: Change in Fair Value of Convertible Notes, Derivative Liabilities, and SAFEs
children.tldr: Convertible notes, derivatives and SAFEs are marked to fair value each period, so a rising enterprise valuation increases this expense until the notes convert or settle.
children.summary: This line records gains and losses from carrying these instruments [[at fair value each reporting period|p952]]. Because they are marked to market, [[increases in enterprise valuation drive increases in this expense|p952]], which will continue until the notes are converted, repaid or settled.

children.title: Other Income (Expense), Net
children.tldr: Other income (expense), net mainly reflects fair value changes on strategic investments and instruments, derivatives from a December 2025 acquisition, finance lease interest and currency effects.
children.summary: This line consists mainly of [[fair value changes on strategic investments and financial instruments|p953]], derivative changes tied to a [[December 2025 acquisition of a privately held company|p953]], finance lease interest and foreign exchange gains and losses.

children.title: Provision for Income Taxes
children.tldr: Income tax expense covers federal, state, local and foreign taxes, with the effective rate swayed by the valuation allowance and nondeductible derivative fair value adjustments.
children.summary: The provision covers taxes in the [[jurisdictions where Anthropic operates|p954]]. Its effective rate depends on the [[valuation allowance and nondeductible fair value adjustments|p954]], the foreign versus domestic income mix, tax credits and tax law changes.

children.title: Results of Operations
children.tldr: Revenue rose from $41 million in 2023 to $16,286 million in the first half of 2026, while net loss reached $80,748 million, driven by fair value charges.
children.summary: Revenue grew from [[$41 million in 2023 to $4,585 million in 2025|p956]], and to $16,286 million in the six months ended June 30, 2026, up from $1,163 million a year earlier. Operating loss narrowed to $693 million in the first half of 2026, and total operating expenses fell to [[104% of revenue|p959]] from 284%. Net loss still rose to $80,748 million because of a $72,388 million change in fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities and SAFEs, which the filing attributes to a [[rising enterprise valuation|p957]]. Stock-based compensation was [[$2.2 billion in the first half of 2026|p957]].

[[Operating expenses|s174]] also grew, led by compute, but more slowly than revenue. [[Interest income rose to $1,111 million|s179]]. The [[change in fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFEs|s180]] grew by $61.4 billion to $72,388 million, and [[other income (expense), net|s181]] was an $8,757 million expense tied to note purchase agreements. [[Income taxes|s182]] were not material.

Customers with $100,000 or more of TTM revenue grew from more than 600 to [[more than 6,000|p962]], and their revenue rose from $870 million to $12.0 billion, about 74% of the first-half 2026 total.

[[Sales, marketing, and partnerships|s177]] rose 2,540% to $3,168 million on channel partner fees, and [[other operating and administrative|s178]] rose 460% to $1,714 million.

children.tldr: Compute and infrastructure rose $6.6 billion, or 283%, to $8,945 million in the first half of 2026, but dropped to 55% of revenue from 201%.
children.summary: Compute costs grew from [[$2,334 million to $8,945 million|p963]] as committed compute arrived under CSP arrangements during the [[first half of 2026|p964]]. The share of revenue fell to 55% because revenue rose sharply against a [[compute base committed in advance|p965]].

children.tldr: Personnel expenses rose $2.6 billion, or 486%, to $3,152 million in the first half of 2026, mostly from a $1.9 billion stock compensation increase.
children.summary: Personnel costs grew from [[$538 million to $3,152 million|p966]], falling to 19% of revenue from 46%. The rise came from a [[$1.9 billion increase in stock-based compensation and a $510 million increase in cash compensation|p967]], both from headcount growth.

children.title: Sales, Marketing, and Partnerships
children.tldr: Sales, marketing, and partnerships rose 2,540% to $3,168 million in the first half of 2026, mainly from $2.7 billion more in channel partner fees.
children.summary: These expenses grew from [[$120 million to $3,168 million|p968]], rising to 19% of revenue from 10%. The increase was driven by a [[$2.7 billion rise in channel partner fees|p969]] and $273 million more marketing and advertising for product launches.

Drivers included increases of [[$251 million in data quality and evaluation vendors|p971]], $223 million in IT and cloud software, $222 million in payment processing, $205 million in professional services, $126 million in donation matching charges and $68 million in facilities.

children.title: Interest Income

children.summary: Interest income grew from [[$115 million to $1,111 million|p972]], driven by [[higher average cash balances and new short-term investments|p973]].

children.title: Change in Fair Value of Convertible Notes, Derivative Liabilities, and SAFEs
children.tldr: The fair value charge on convertible notes, derivatives and SAFEs grew $61.4 billion to $72,388 million in the first half of 2026 as enterprise valuation rose.
children.summary: This charge rose from [[$10,942 million to $72,388 million|p974]], mainly because the convertible promissory notes gained value as Anthropic's [[enterprise valuation increased from 2025 to 2026|p975]].

children.title: Other Income (Expense), Net
children.tldr: Other income (expense), net was an $8,757 million expense in the first half of 2026, from fair value accounting on note purchase agreements.
children.summary: Other expense rose to [[$8,757 million|p976]] from nothing a year earlier, driven by the [[initial and changing fair value of assets and liabilities under note purchase agreements|p978]] described in Note 4.

children.title: Revenue
children.tldr: Revenue rose $345 million, or 841%, to $386 million in 2024, driven by new customers after the Claude 3 model launch.
children.summary: Revenue grew from [[$41 million to $386 million|p1004]]. Consumption revenue rose about $249 million and subscriptions about $96 million, helped by the [[launch of the Claude 3 family of Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku models|p1005]]. Customers with $100,000 or more of TTM revenue grew from about 20 to [[about 200|p1005]], falling to about 57% of revenue from 90%.

children.title: Operating Expenses
children.tldr: 2024 operating expenses rose across all lines, with compute up $2.1 billion as committed capacity from 2023 deals arrived.
children.summary: In 2024, [[compute and infrastructure|s198]] rose 482% to $2,522 million, [[personnel|s199]] rose 378% to $454 million, [[sales, marketing, and partnerships|s200]] rose to $43 million and [[other operating and administrative|s201]] rose 460% to $347 million.

children.title: Compute and Infrastructure
children.tldr: Compute and infrastructure rose $2.1 billion, or 482%, to $2,522 million in 2024 as compute committed in 2023 was delivered.
children.summary: Compute costs grew from [[$433 million to $2,522 million|p1006]], reflecting [[staged delivery of compute under 2023 CSP arrangements|p1007]]. They fell to 653% of revenue from 1,056% as revenue scaled against a fixed base.

children.title: Personnel
children.tldr: Personnel expenses rose $359 million, or 378%, to $454 million in 2024 on higher cash and stock compensation from hiring.
children.summary: Personnel costs grew from [[$95 million to $454 million|p1008]], driven by a [[$164 million rise in cash compensation and $163 million in stock-based compensation|p1008]].

children.title: Sales, Marketing, and Partnerships
children.tldr: Sales, marketing, and partnerships rose $41 million to $43 million in 2024, almost entirely from launch-related marketing and advertising.
children.summary: These expenses grew from [[$2 million to $43 million|p1009]], mainly from a [[$39 million increase in marketing and advertising|p1010]].

children.title: Other Operating and Administrative
children.tldr: Other operating and administrative costs rose $285 million, or 460%, to $347 million in 2024, led by $165 million more in data quality vendors.
children.summary: These costs grew from [[$62 million to $347 million|p1011]], driven by a [[$165 million rise in data quality and evaluation vendors|p1012]], plus increases in professional services, software and facilities.

children.title: Interest Income
children.tldr: Interest income rose $37 million, or 54%, to $106 million in 2024 on a larger money market fund portfolio.
children.summary: Interest income grew from [[$69 million to $106 million|p1013]] due to [[higher average cash balances|p1014]] from money market funds.

children.title: Change in Fair Value of Convertible Notes, Derivative Liabilities, and SAFEs
children.tldr: The fair value charge on convertible notes, derivatives and SAFEs grew $4.4 billion to $5,434 million in 2024 as enterprise valuation rose.
children.summary: This charge rose from [[$1,045 million to $5,434 million|p1015]], mainly from convertible notes gaining value as [[enterprise valuation increased|p1016]].

children.title: Other Income (Expense), Net
children.tldr: Other income (expense), net was a $2 million expense in 2023 and zero in 2024, which the company considers not material.
children.summary: Other expense moved from [[$2 million to zero|p1017]] and was [[not material|p1019]].

children.title: Provision for Income Taxes
children.tldr: Income tax provision was $2 million in 2023 and $1 million in 2024, not material.
children.summary: The provision was [[$2 million and $1 million|p1020]], which the filing calls [[not material|p1022]].

children.title: Non-GAAP Financial Measures
children.tldr: Anthropic reports Adjusted Operating Income (Loss), Adjusted Operating Margin and Adjusted Net Income (Loss), excluding items it says do not reflect ongoing operations.
children.summary: Management uses non-GAAP measures for planning and [[evaluating operating performance|p1024]]. They should [[not be viewed in isolation|p1025]] from GAAP results and may differ from other companies' definitions. [[Adjusted Operating Income|s207]] turned positive at $1,618 million in the first half of 2026, and [[Adjusted Net Income|s208]] reached $2,671 million.

children.title: Adjusted Operating Income (Loss) and Adjusted Operating Margin
children.tldr: Adjusted Operating Income turned positive at $1,618 million, a 10% margin, in the first half of 2026, versus a $1,849 million loss a year earlier.
children.summary: The measure is operating loss excluding [[stock-based compensation, non-cash charitable contributions and the Bartz settlement|p1026]]. In the first half of 2026, the $693 million operating loss plus $2,185 million of stock compensation and $126 million of donation charges gave [[$1,618 million of Adjusted Operating Income|p1028]]. Adjusted Operating Margin was [[10%|p1029]], compared with (159)% a year earlier and (106)% for 2025.

children.title: Adjusted Net Income (Loss)
children.tldr: Adjusted Net Income was $2,671 million in the first half of 2026, compared with a $1,741 million adjusted loss a year earlier.
children.summary: This measure excludes from net loss [[stock compensation, donation charges, the Bartz settlement, fair value changes on convertible notes and SAFEs, and certain mark-to-market instruments|p1031]]. The first-half 2026 net loss of $80,748 million, after adding back $72,388 million of note fair value changes and $8,720 million of other mark-to-market changes, became [[$2,671 million of Adjusted Net Income|p1033]]. Adjusted net loss was $4,448 million for 2025.

children.title: Quarterly Results of Operations
children.tldr: Quarterly revenue climbed from $376 million in Q1 2025 to $11,555 million in Q2 2026, when Anthropic posted its first operating income, $974 million.
children.summary: The unaudited quarterly data is prepared [[on the same basis as the audited statements|p1035]] and may not predict future results. [[Quarterly revenue|s210]] grew every quarter, and operating income reached $974 million in the quarter ended June 30, 2026. [[As a share of revenue|s211]], total operating expenses fell from 349% to 92% over the six quarters.

children.title: Quarterly Consolidated Statements of Operations
children.tldr: Revenue rose from $376 million in Q1 2025 to $11,555 million in Q2 2026, which delivered $974 million of operating income but a $66,309 million net loss.
children.summary: Quarterly revenue grew from [[$376 million in Q1 2025 to $4,731 million in Q1 2026 and $11,555 million in Q2 2026|p1036]]. Compute costs rose to $5,558 million in Q2 2026, and operating results turned from a $1,667 million loss in Q1 2026 to [[$974 million of operating income|p1036]]. A $59,597 million fair value charge still produced a Q2 2026 net loss of $66,309 million. Stock-based compensation rose from $105 million to [[$1.3 billion per quarter|p1037]].

children.title: Quarterly Consolidated Statements of Operations, as a Percentage of Revenue
children.tldr: Compute fell from 251% of revenue in Q1 2025 to 48% in Q2 2026, and operating margin improved from (249)% to 8%.
children.summary: As a share of revenue, compute and infrastructure dropped from [[251% to 48%|p1038]] and personnel from 58% to 16% between Q1 2025 and Q2 2026. Total operating expenses fell to 92%, giving an [[8% operating margin|p1038]] in Q2 2026, though net loss was 574% of revenue. Percentages [[may not foot due to rounding|p1039]].

children.title: Quarterly Trends
children.tldr: Quarterly revenue rose from $376 million in Q1 2025 to $11.6 billion in Q2 2026, when Anthropic reached $974 million of operating income after five quarters of losses.
children.summary: Over the six quarters from March 31, 2025 to June 30, 2026, [[revenue grew every quarter|s213]] as new models and products drove usage. [[Operating expenses also rose|s214]], led by compute delivered under cloud contracts. [[Operating losses widened through 2025 and turned to operating income|s220]] in the three months ended June 30, 2026. Growing cash balances [[lifted interest income|s221]]. Rising company valuations caused large [[fair value charges on convertible notes|s222]] and [[on note purchase agreement assets and liabilities|s223]], which kept net losses large. Before those and other non-cash items, [[Adjusted Operating Income reached $2,235 million|s225]] and [[Adjusted Net Income reached $2,981 million|s226]] in the three months ended June 30, 2026.

children.title: Revenue
children.tldr: Quarterly revenue rose every quarter, from $376 million in Q1 2025 to $11.6 billion in Q2 2026, and customers paying $100,000 or more grew from about 400 to over 6,000.
children.summary: Revenue grew from [[$376 million for the three months ended March 31, 2025 to $11.6 billion for the three months ended June 30, 2026|p1040]]. Successive model and product releases drove the growth, with both consumption and subscription revenue contributing. [[Customers with $100,000 or more of trailing twelve month revenue|p1040]] grew from about 400 to more than 6,000 over the same period.

children.title: Operating Expenses
children.tldr: Every major expense line grew over the six quarters, led by compute costs that rose from $944 million to $5.6 billion a quarter.
children.summary: [[Compute and infrastructure costs|s215]] rose as committed cloud capacity came online but fell sharply as a share of revenue. [[Personnel costs|s216]] grew with headcount and stock compensation. A one-time [[$1.5 billion Bartz settlement charge|s217]] hit the September 2025 quarter. [[Sales, marketing, and partnerships spending|s218]] jumped most in the first half of 2026. [[Other operating and administrative costs|s219]] rose with scale, along with donation matching charges in late 2025.

children.title: Compute and Infrastructure
children.tldr: Quarterly compute costs rose from $944 million to $5.6 billion but fell from 251% to 48% of revenue as revenue outgrew committed capacity.
children.summary: Compute and infrastructure expenses grew from [[$944 million in the three months ended March 31, 2025 to $5.6 billion in the three months ended June 30, 2026|p1041]] as compute committed under multi-year cloud contracts was delivered. Anthropic buys compute [[12 to 18 months ahead|p1041]], so these costs are largely fixed in the near term. As a share of revenue they [[fell from 251% to 48%|p1042]].

children.title: Personnel
children.tldr: Personnel expenses rose every quarter as headcount grew, along with compensation including stock-based pay.
children.summary: Personnel expenses [[increased in each quarter|p1043]], driven by headcount growth and higher compensation, including stock-based compensation.

children.title: Bartz settlement
children.tldr: Anthropic recorded a $1.5 billion charge in the quarter ended September 30, 2025 to settle the Bartz litigation.
children.summary: A [[$1.5 billion charge to settle the Bartz litigation|p1044]] was recorded in the three months ended September 30, 2025.

children.title: Sales, Marketing, and Partnerships
children.tldr: Sales, marketing, and partnerships costs rose every quarter, most in the first two quarters of 2026, driven by channel partner fees and launch advertising.
children.summary: These expenses grew each quarter, with [[the largest increases in the three months ended March 31 and June 30, 2026|p1045]]. The main drivers were [[fees paid to channel partners and higher media spend|p1045]] supporting product launches.

children.title: Other Operating and Administrative
children.tldr: Other operating and administrative costs rose with scale, except in Q1 2026, with a Q4 2025 spike from non-cash donation matching charges.
children.summary: These costs grew on [[vendor spending for data quality and evaluation, IT and cloud software, payment fees, and professional services|p1046]]. The [[December 2025 quarter jump came mainly from non-cash donation matching charges|p1046]], and lower such charges made the March 2026 quarter the one decline.

children.title: Operating Income (Loss)
children.tldr: Operating losses widened through Q3 2025 due to compute costs and the Bartz settlement, then narrowed, reaching $1.0 billion of operating income in Q2 2026.
children.summary: The operating loss [[widened in the June and September 2025 quarters|p1047]], first from compute costs outpacing revenue and then from the Bartz settlement. It narrowed in the next two quarters, and Anthropic earned [[operating income of $1.0 billion in the three months ended June 30, 2026|p1047]]. The company [[expects results to keep fluctuating|p1047]] as incoming compute varies.

children.title: Interest Income
children.tldr: Quarterly interest income grew from $51 million to $762 million on larger cash and short-term investment balances.
children.summary: Interest income rose from [[$51 million in the three months ended March 31, 2025 to $762 million in the three months ended June 30, 2026|p1048]], mainly because of higher average cash and short-term investment balances.

children.title: Change in Fair Value of Convertible Notes, Derivative Liabilities, and SAFEs
children.tldr: Rising valuations caused fair value expense on convertible notes every quarter, peaking in Q2 2026 with the Series H financing.
children.summary: Increases in Anthropic's enterprise valuation raised the fair value of its outstanding convertible notes, creating [[expense in every quarter|p1049]]. The [[largest expense came in the three months ended June 30, 2026|p1049]], tied to the Series H financing. These charges will continue until the instruments are converted, repaid, or settled.

children.title: Other Income (Expense), Net
children.tldr: Other expense was $309 million in Q1 2026 and $8.4 billion in Q2 2026, driven by fair value accounting on note purchase agreements.
children.summary: Other income (expense), net was immaterial before 2026, then reached [[$(309) million and $(8.4) billion for the three months ended March 31 and June 30, 2026|p1050]], mainly from recognizing and remeasuring assets and liabilities under the note purchase agreements.

children.title: Provision for Income Taxes
children.tldr: Income tax provision was not material in any quarter presented.
children.summary: The [[provision for income taxes was not material|p1051]] for the quarters presented.

children.title: Quarterly Adjusted Operating Income (Loss) and Adjusted Operating Margin
children.tldr: Adjusted Operating Income reached $2,235 million, a 19% margin, in Q2 2026, versus GAAP operating income of $974 million, an 8% margin.
children.summary: Adding back stock-based compensation, non-cash charitable contributions, and the Bartz settlement, [[Adjusted Operating Income moved from $(830) million in the March 2025 quarter to $2,235 million in the June 2026 quarter|p1052]]. GAAP operating income was $974 million in that latest quarter, with stock compensation of $1,261 million. On revenue of $11,555 million, [[operating margin was 8% and Adjusted Operating Margin was 19%|p1053]], up from (249)% and (221)% in the March 2025 quarter. The [[charitable add-back relates to donation matching tied to employee equity|p1054]].

children.title: Quarterly Adjusted Net Income (Loss)
children.tldr: Despite a $66.3 billion net loss in Q2 2026, mostly from fair value charges, Adjusted Net Income was $2,981 million that quarter.
children.summary: Net losses grew to [[$(66,309) million in the three months ended June 30, 2026|p1055]], driven by a $59,597 million change in fair value of convertible notes and related instruments and $8,432 million from other mark-to-market instruments. Excluding those items, stock compensation, charitable contributions, and the Bartz settlement, [[Adjusted Net Income was $2,981 million|p1055]] that quarter, compared with $(786) million in the March 2025 quarter.

children.title: Liquidity and Capital Resources
children.tldr: As of June 30, 2026, Anthropic held $112.4 billion of cash and $19.3 billion of short-term investments, but expects heavy, rising compute spending to consume significant cash for the foreseeable future.
children.summary: Anthropic has funded itself mainly through convertible notes, preferred stock, SAFEs and sales, and has financed compute largely through cloud provider deals. As of June 30, 2026, it had [[$112.4 billion of cash and cash equivalents|p1056]], $19.3 billion of short-term investments and $3.2 billion available under its credit facility. Its [[accumulated deficit of $132.9 billion|p1057]] includes $113.2 billion from fair value changes in convertible notes and derivative liabilities. The company expects [[capital expenditures to increase significantly|p1058]], with more upfront payments for data centers and leases, and warns that limited chip suppliers and partners who also compete with it create risks. It believes current resources will last [[at least the next 12 months|p1059]], and plans to fund longer term needs through operations, [[equity, debt and partner financing|p1060]]. Its [[credit facility grew to $15 billion|s228]] in September 2026, and it has [[$77 billion of undrawn note capacity|s230]]. In the first half of 2026, [[financing provided $110,774 million|s237]], mostly from preferred stock sales.

children.title: Revolving Credit Agreement
children.tldr: In September 2026 Anthropic expanded its undrawn $3.25 billion secured revolver into a $15 billion facility maturing September 4, 2031, with a $5.0 billion minimum liquidity covenant.
children.summary: Anthropic opened a [[$2.5 billion senior secured revolving credit facility|p1061]] with Morgan Stanley Senior Funding as agent in May 2025 and raised it to $3.25 billion by November 2025. As of June 30, 2026, nothing was drawn, $78 million of standby letters of credit were outstanding, and the company was in compliance with all covenants. In September 2026 an amended agreement created a [[$15 billion facility maturing September 4, 2031|p1062]]. Maturity can come earlier if large debt payments fall due and liquidity is short. The facility is [[secured by substantially all assets|p1063]], but guarantees and collateral can be released once two of Moody's, S&P and Fitch give an investment grade rating. Interest is based on the Alternate Base Rate or Term SOFR plus a margin. A [[liquidity of at least $5.0 billion|p1064]] covenant applies each quarter starting with the quarter ending December 31, 2026.

children.title: AMD Agreement
children.tldr: AMD committed to buy up to $5.0 billion of Anthropic Class N stock, released as AMD MI450 GPU deployment milestones are met, with the first expected in 2027.
children.summary: In July 2026 Anthropic signed a [[Hardware Supply Agreement|p1065]] with AMD to purchase, lease or access Helios rack systems built on AMD Instinct MI450 series GPUs. AMD agreed to [[purchase up to $5.0 billion|p1065]] of Class N common stock in increments as delivery and deployment milestones are reached. After the IPO the price will be the 30 trading day volume weighted average price of Class A stock. Draw requests must be made within 12 months after the final GPU deployment.

children.title: Convertible Notes
children.tldr: Anthropic has $6.2 billion of Amazon convertible notes outstanding and $77 billion of undrawn note capacity from Google, Amazon and Broadcom.
children.summary: Anthropic has note purchase agreements with [[Google, Amazon and Broadcom|s231]]. Obligations to issue future notes are carried as derivative liabilities until the notes are issued. The only notes outstanding are [[$6,203 million of Amazon rollover notes|s232]], which bear no interest and are limited by Amazon's 12% ownership cap. Undrawn facilities total [[$77,000 million|s233]] as of June 30, 2026. They are [[$15.0 billion from Amazon|s234]], drawn as compute milestones are met, and [[$42.0 billion from Broadcom|s235]], which can be used only to pay lease rent and carries 9.00% interest. They also include [[$20.0 billion from Google|s236]] through December 31, 2030, which shrinks if Google uses its $10.0 billion IPO purchase option.

children.title: Overview
children.tldr: Anthropic's note agreements with Google, Amazon and Broadcom leave about $6.2 billion of Amazon notes outstanding and provide new 2026 facilities for future financing.
children.summary: Anthropic has [[note purchase agreements|p1066]] with Google, Amazon and Broadcom. Google's 2023 and 2024 notes have fully converted into preferred stock, and the Google 2026 NPA offers new capacity. Under the Amazon 2023 and 2024 NPAs about [[$6.2 billion aggregate principal|p1066]] remains outstanding, and the Amazon 2026 NPA, dated April 20, 2026, adds new capacity. Obligations to issue future notes are booked as [[a derivative liability|p1066]] until the notes are issued.

children.title: Outstanding Notes
children.tldr: As of June 30, 2026, $6,203 million of interest free Amazon rollover notes were outstanding, convertible into up to 1,840,444,962 Class N shares, subject to a 12% ownership cap.
children.summary: All outstanding notes are [[interest free rollover notes held by Amazon|p1067]]. They were reissued because conversion would have pushed Amazon above 12% of Anthropic's capitalization. The Amazon 2023 NPA notes total [[$2,186 million at $2.0928 per share|p1068]] (1,044,716,970 shares) and mature March 2034. The Amazon 2024 NPA notes total $4,017 million at $5.0478 (795,727,992 shares) and mature in January, May and November 2035. The combined [[$6,203 million|p1068]] could convert into 1,840,444,962 shares before the cap. At the IPO they convert at the [[lower of the fixed price and the IPO Price|p1069]], subject to the cap. Any remainder converts quarterly afterward, also at the 10 day trailing average price if that is lower.

children.title: Note Purchase Agreements
children.tldr: Anthropic had $77,000 million of undrawn note capacity as of June 30, 2026: $20,000 million from Google, $15,000 million from Amazon and $42,000 million from Broadcom.
children.summary: As of June 30, 2026, no notes were outstanding under the [[undrawn NPA facilities|p1070]]. Available capacity was [[$20,000 million from Google|p1071]] through December 2030, which falls by up to $10.0 billion if Google buys shares alongside the IPO. Amazon offers $15,000 million available for 30 months after the offering. Broadcom offers $42,000 million for five years from the start of the draw period, and Broadcom may assign it to a financial partner. The [[total is $77,000 million|p1071]].

children.title: Amazon
children.tldr: The Amazon 2026 NPA offers $15.0 billion, available in $5.0 billion steps tied to compute milestones and settled in Class N stock at a 30 day average price.
children.summary: The [[Amazon 2026 NPA|p1074]] provides $15.0 billion, all of it unused as of June 30, 2026. Draws settle in Class N stock at the 30 day trailing volume weighted average price of Class A stock, subject to Amazon's ownership cap. No notes are expected before the IPO. Draws are possible until the earlier of [[30 months after the offering|p1076]] or the end of certain commercial agreements. They become available in $5.0 billion increments as compute capacity milestones are met. Amounts blocked by the cap become [[interest free rollover notes maturing in 10 years|p1077]], payable in cash or by set off. After certain defaults, Anthropic may have to [[repay in five equal installments|p1078]].

children.title: Broadcom
children.tldr: Broadcom's $42.0 billion note facility can only fund lease rent, carries 9.00% paid in kind interest, and converts at 90% of the 30 day average stock price.
children.summary: Anthropic may issue notes under the [[Infrastructure Partner 2026 NPA|p1079]] only to pay quarterly rent under the 2026 Lease Arrangement. The facility provides [[$42.0 billion at 9.00% per annum|p1081]]. Maturities run 60 months for the first $24.0 billion, 63 months for amounts above $24.0 billion up to $32.0 billion, and 57 months above $32.0 billion. Holders can convert at 90% of the 30 day trailing average price. If certain revenue conditions are not met, the rate becomes [[13.00% and conversion is at 85%|p1082]]. Draws run for five years once equipment is in service. They require [[revenue growth well below actual rates|p1083]], compliance with the credit facility's minimum liquidity covenant, and continued lease performance. On a change of control, holders may take [[150% of principal and interest|p1084]] in cash or convert.

children.title: Google
children.tldr: The Google 2026 NPA offers $20.0 billion through December 31, 2030, with a 14.99% ownership cap and a $10.0 billion IPO share option that would reduce it.
children.summary: The [[Google 2026 NPA|p1089]] provides $20.0 billion, unused as of June 30, 2026. For draws after the IPO, Google may take notes on mutually agreed terms or Class N stock at the 30 day average price. Requests may be made [[through December 31, 2030|p1091]] and depend on compute agreement conditions and revenue targets that Anthropic has historically exceeded. Issuances that would take Google above [[14.99% of capitalization|p1091]] become 10 year interest free rollover notes. Google also holds an [[option to buy up to $10.0 billion|p1092]] of Class N stock at the IPO price, which would reduce the note capacity by the same amount.

children.title: Cash Flows
children.tldr: Operating cash flow swung to $3,929 million of inflow in the first half of 2026, while financing brought in $110,774 million and investing used $17,181 million.
children.summary: The [[cash flow table|p1094]] shows that operating activities used $1,627 million in 2023, $5,692 million in 2024 and $2,637 million in 2025. Operations then provided $3,929 million in the six months ended June 30, 2026, versus $1,513 million used a year earlier. Investing used $3,077 million in 2025 and $17,181 million in the 2026 half year. Financing provided $2,320 million, $7,248 million and $19,960 million for 2023 through 2025, and [[$110,774 million in the first half of 2026|p1094]].

children.title: Operating Activities
children.tldr: Operating cash flow was a $3.9 billion inflow in the first half of 2026, compared with $1.5 billion used a year earlier, driven by smaller losses and working capital timing.
children.summary: Operating cash use in 2025 fell by [[$3.1 billion|p1095]] from 2024. This came from using hosting capacity paid for in earlier years and from higher payables. The gain was partly offset by the Bartz settlement payment, higher pay costs and higher receivables. Cash use in 2024 rose by [[$4.1 billion|p1096]] on larger hosting prepayments. In the six months ended June 30, 2026, operations [[provided $3.9 billion|p1097]], helped by a smaller net loss after non-cash items and by the timing of vendor payments and customer receipts.

children.title: Investing Activities
children.tldr: Investing cash use reached $17.2 billion in the first half of 2026, compared with $49 million a year earlier, mostly short term investment purchases plus server and network spending.
children.summary: Investing cash use rose by [[$3.1 billion in 2025|p1098]], driven by purchases of marketable securities and capital spending on servers, networking and infrastructure. It rose by only [[$20 million in 2024|p1099]]. In the six months ended June 30, 2026, investing used [[$17.2 billion|p1100]], compared with $49 million a year earlier. The money went mainly to commercial paper, Treasury, agency and corporate debt securities and to higher capital expenditures.

children.title: Financing Activities
children.tldr: Financing provided $110.8 billion in the first half of 2026, compared with $4.7 billion a year earlier, mostly from sales of redeemable convertible preferred stock.
children.summary: Financing inflows rose by [[$12.7 billion in 2025|p1101]] and by [[$4.9 billion in 2024|p1102]], from preferred stock sales and, in 2024, convertible notes issued for cash. In the six months ended June 30, 2026, financing provided [[$110.8 billion|p1103]], compared with $4.7 billion a year earlier, mainly from issuing redeemable convertible preferred stock.

children.title: Off-Balance Sheet Arrangements
children.tldr: Anthropic has no off balance sheet financing beyond hosting and lease commitments, equity investment funding commitments, and data center developer guaranties and cost reimbursements.
children.summary: Apart from [[hosting and lease commitments, equity method funding commitments, and developer guaranty arrangements|p1104]] for data center capacity, Anthropic has no off balance sheet financing and no relationships with unconsolidated entities or financial partnerships.

children.title: Contractual Obligations
children.tldr: Anthropic's contractual obligations are almost entirely compute and infrastructure, though the draft leaves the dollar totals and dates blank.
children.summary: The aggregate obligations are said to be [[substantially all related to compute and infrastructure|p1105]], but the dollar amounts and dates are blank in this draft. The [[obligations table|p1107]] covers operating leases, finance leases and purchase commitments, mainly cloud hosting agreements. It excludes [[convertible notes expected to settle in shares|p1108]] and compute deals with no fixed dollar commitment. It also leaves out [[leases not yet commenced|p1111]] and commitments made after the table date. The largest deals are [[Microsoft, Google, Amazon, SpaceXAI, AMD, Nscale and Lambda|s243]] compute arrangements and [[about $161.2 billion of Broadcom equipment lease rent|s244]]. Anthropic [[expects to keep signing compute agreements|p1114]] as it scales.

children.title: Infrastructure Service Arrangements
children.tldr: Anthropic has committed to hundreds of billions in compute, including $114.5 billion with Google, $110.0 billion with Amazon and up to $120.5 billion with SpaceXAI.
children.summary: Anthropic committed to spend at least [[$44.9 billion with Microsoft|p1116]] between November 2026 and May 2033. With Google it committed at least [[$114.5 billion|p1117]] from April 2026 to July 2033, plus an estimated $125.0 billion to $150.0 billion for extra TPU compute in 2028 to 2031 that is not in the table. With Amazon it committed at least [[$110.0 billion|p1118]] from May 2026 to April 2036. The SpaceXAI deals run [[up to $120.5 billion|p1119]] into 2029, about $3.1 billion a month at full capacity, and can be cancelled on 90 days' notice after early 2027. AMD spending is expected to [[exceed $20.0 billion|p1120]]. Nscale deals reach [[up to about $44.6 billion|p1121]] into 2033, and Lambda deals total [[about $41.3 billion|p1122]] into 2034.

children.title: Infrastructure Equipment Leases
children.tldr: Five year Broadcom equipment leases for TPU capacity carry about $161.2 billion of rent excluding interest and cannot be cancelled except on default.
children.summary: Anthropic's [[five year master equipment leases with Broadcom|p1123]] are finance leases for TPU compute that began coming online in 2026, with more starting in 2027. Rent totals [[about $161.2 billion excluding interest|p1123]], paid quarterly once equipment is ready for service. The leases cannot be cancelled except on default and are secured by the equipment. They are held through two special purpose subsidiaries guaranteed by Anthropic, PBC, and some rent may be funded with [[Broadcom convertible notes|p1123]].

children.title: Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures about Market Risk
children.tldr: Anthropic's market risk comes mainly from interest rates and currency exchange rates, and neither would materially affect results under the stated scenarios.
children.summary: The company's [[main market risks are interest rate and currency movements|p1124]]. A 100 basis point rate change [[would not materially affect its investment portfolio|s246]], and a 10% currency move [[would not materially affect its financial statements|s247]].

children.title: Interest Rate Risk
children.tldr: With $112.4 billion of cash and $19.3 billion of short-term investments, a 100 basis point rate change would not materially affect portfolio value.
children.summary: As of June 30, 2026, Anthropic held [[$112.4 billion of cash and cash equivalents and $19.3 billion of short-term investments|p1125]], plus $2.5 billion of restricted cash. It does not invest for trading or speculation, and because the portfolio is short term, a [[100 basis point rate change would not have a material effect|p1125]].

children.title: Foreign Currency Exchange Risk
children.tldr: Most revenue is in U.S. dollars, a 10% currency move would not be material, and Anthropic does not currently hedge.
children.summary: The [[vast majority of revenue is in U.S. dollars|p1126]], with some in euros and British pounds. A [[hypothetical 10% exchange rate change would not have a material impact|p1126]] as of June 30, 2026. The company has no hedging contracts but may add them if exposure grows.

children.title: Critical Accounting Estimates
children.tldr: Anthropic's most judgment-heavy accounting areas are stock compensation, common stock and convertible note valuation, leases, income taxes, and legal contingencies.
children.summary: Financial statements rely on [[estimates that may differ materially from actual results|p1127]]. The company identifies [[the most critical policies|p1128]] as [[stock-based compensation|s249]], [[common stock valuations|s252]], [[fair value of convertible notes and related instruments|s253]], [[leases|s254]], [[income taxes|s255]], and [[loss contingencies|s256]].

children.title: Stock-Based Compensation
children.tldr: Stock awards are expensed at grant date fair value, which depends mainly on the estimated value of Anthropic's common stock.
children.summary: Options and RSUs are [[measured at grant date fair value|p1129]], with estimated common stock value as the key input. [[Options carry $2.8 billion of unrecognized cost|s250]], while [[RSUs carry $26.6 billion|s251]] that will start being expensed with the offering.

children.title: Stock Options
children.tldr: Options are valued with the Black-Scholes-Merton model, and $2.8 billion of unrecognized option cost remains, to be recognized over about 1.2 years.
children.summary: Anthropic values options using the [[Black-Scholes-Merton model|p1130]] and expenses them straight line. Inputs include [[estimated common stock value|p1132]], [[volatility of comparable public companies|p1133]], an expected term averaging vesting and contractual periods, Treasury rates, and a zero dividend yield. As of June 30, 2026, [[$2.8 billion of unrecognized cost|p1137]] remained, over a weighted average 1.2 years.

children.title: Restricted Stock Units and Restricted Stock Awards
children.tldr: Anthropic has $26.6 billion of unrecognized RSU expense and will record a large catch-up charge when the registration statement becomes effective.
children.summary: Outstanding RSUs have [[service and performance vesting conditions|p1138]], and the performance condition is generally met when this registration statement becomes effective. Because it had not been met, [[no RSU expense had been recognized as of June 30, 2026|p1139]]. Unrecognized RSU expense totaled [[$26.6 billion, of which $2.9 billion|p1139]] relates to awards with service vesting fully or partly met, so expenses will rise sharply in the quarter the offering closes. [[RSAs vest on service only|p1140]] and are expensed straight line.

children.title: Common Stock Valuations
children.tldr: Before the IPO, the board estimated common stock value from recent financing rounds, allocated across share classes and discounted for lack of marketability.
children.summary: The board weighed [[many factors|p1141]], including [[third-party valuations|p1142]] and [[prices in financings and secondary sales|p1143]]. It [[estimated enterprise value mainly from the nearest equity round|p1152]], allocated it using a [[hybrid of contingent claims and common stock equivalent methods|p1153]], and applied a [[discount for lack of marketability|p1154]]. These steps involve [[complex, subjective assumptions|p1155]]. After the offering, [[public trading will set the value|p1156]].

children.title: Fair Value of Convertible Notes, Derivative Liabilities, and SAFEs
children.tldr: Convertible notes are carried at fair value using a scenario-based model, and assumptions about conversion caps and rollover notes require significant judgment.
children.summary: Anthropic [[elected fair value accounting for its convertible notes|p1157]] and recorded [[derivative liabilities for future notes|p1158]] under its 2023 and 2024 agreements with Amazon and Google. Fair value comes from a [[probability-weighted scenario analysis|p1159]] covering conversion, repayment, and change of control. The [[ownership cap and rollover mechanism|p1160]] requires the most judgment because it depends on uncertain future financings. [[No SAFEs have been outstanding since 2024|p1161]], so the ongoing exposure is the convertible and rollover notes.

children.title: Leases
children.tldr: Leases for facilities and compute capacity require judgment on lease identification, term, asset value, and borrowing rate, which could materially change reported amounts.
children.summary: Anthropic leases [[facilities and equipment, including compute capacity|p1163]], and lease accounting depends on estimates such as term and incremental borrowing rate. Given the portfolio's size, [[changed estimates could materially alter classification or measurement|p1164]].

children.title: Income Taxes
children.tldr: Whether Anthropic can use its deferred tax assets is a major judgment because future taxable income is uncertain, and changes could materially affect results.
children.summary: Taxes use the asset and liability method, with [[valuation allowances|p1165]] where realization is not more likely than not. As an AI company investing heavily in compute, Anthropic says its [[taxable income projections are inherently uncertain|p1166]]. [[Uncertain tax positions|p1167]], especially research and development credits, also require judgment.

children.title: Loss Contingencies
children.tldr: Anthropic accrues legal losses when probable and estimable, and these judgments have been revised in past periods.
children.summary: The company faces [[legal and regulatory claims|p1168]], some for large or indeterminate damages. It [[records a liability when a loss is probable and estimable|p1169]] and has revised such assessments in prior periods as information changed.

children.title: Recent Accounting Pronouncements
children.tldr: Recent accounting pronouncements are described in Note 1 to the consolidated financial statements.
children.summary: Adopted and pending accounting standards are covered in [[Note 1 to the consolidated financial statements|p1170]].

children.title: Business
children.tldr: Anthropic says Claude is the fastest-adopted enterprise technology in history, and more than 11,900 customers paid $100,000 or more over the trailing twelve months as of September 30, 2026.
children.summary: Anthropic describes itself as a research lab first, founded in 2021 to develop advanced AI responsibly. It says Claude's revenue grew from $0 at its first quarter 2023 launch through the [[fastest enterprise adoption|s259]] of any technology. It expects [[Powerful AI|s265]] matching top experts within a few years and positions Claude as a [[Virtual Collaborator|s276]] for knowledge workers. As of September 30, 2026, [[more than 11,900 customers|s306]] paid $100,000 or more on a trailing twelve month basis, up from more than 950 a year earlier, including every Fortune 10 company. The company builds models, platform and applications as [[one integrated stack|s293]] and treats [[safety research|s317]] as core to its business. It gave [[846,840,960 Class N shares|s326]] to its Public Benefit Fund. Legal matters include the [[$1.5 billion Bartz settlement|s338]] and a dispute with the Department of War.

children.title: Overview
children.tldr: Anthropic calls Claude the fastest-adopted enterprise technology in history, with revenue rising from $0 at its first quarter 2023 launch, driven by self-reinforcing improvement and investment loops.
children.summary: Anthropic argues that intelligence can now be built at scale and that AI could change the economy more than industrialization or the internet. Founded in 2021, the company describes itself as [[first and foremost a research lab|p1172]] whose mission is the responsible development of advanced AI for humanity's long-term benefit. It says Claude has seen the [[fastest enterprise adoption of any technology|p1172]], with revenue growing from $0 at commercial launch in the first quarter of 2023. The section covers the company's [[five core advantages|s260]], its [[enterprise customer base|s261]], [[financial strengths|s262]], the [[improvement and investment loops|s263]], and how Claude is [[speeding up its own development|s264]]. Anthropic sees the gap between what Claude can do and how widely it is used as [[one of its largest growth opportunities|p1173]].

children.title: Our Core Advantages
children.tldr: Anthropic names five core advantages: mission and focus, talent and culture, integrated frontier and safety research, a fungible multi-chip compute pool, and an enterprise-focused strategy.
children.summary: Anthropic says a [[singular focus on its mission|p1174]] lets it put talent, research and compute toward the most valuable work, with safety and capability advancing together. Its mission and [[low-ego, truth-seeking culture|p1175]] help it attract and keep top researchers. Its capability and safety research are integrated, and each Claude model helps build the next, a dynamic it calls [["closing the loop"|p1176]]. The company may slow releases to manage risk and treats this as a deliberate tradeoff. It runs compute as [[one fungible pool across AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, NVIDIA GPUs, and AMD GPUs|p1177]] and has large long-term compute and infrastructure commitments running from 2031 to 2045 for most of the total. Its [[enterprise strategy|p1178]] organizes research, products and sales around enterprise use, where customer feedback is richest.

children.title: Enterprise Adoption of Claude
children.tldr: As of September 30, 2026, more than 1,900 customers generated at least $1 million of trailing revenue, and about 250 generated $10 million or more.
children.summary: As of September 30, 2026, Anthropic had [[more than 11,900 customers|p1180]] with $100,000 or more of trailing twelve month revenue, [[more than 1,900|p1181]] with $1 million or more, and [[about 250|p1182]] with $10 million or more. The company builds models, a platform and applications. In the three months ended September 30, 2026, [[over 50% of its $100,000+ customers|p1183]] used both Claude Platform and at least one first-party application, up from about 30% in the quarter ended December 31, 2025. Key products are [[Claude Platform, Claude Code, and Claude Cowork|p1185]]. Claude is sold on [[AWS, GCP, and Azure|p1189]] under direct contracts with customers, with a fee paid to each cloud provider. It is also sold through partners such as Accenture, Deloitte, Salesforce and Snowflake, and through Ode with Anthropic, a new services company for midsized firms.

children.title: Strengths of Our Financial Model
children.tldr: Revenue reached $11.6 billion in the quarter ended June 30, 2026, up from $787 million a year earlier, with an 8% operating margin versus (152)%.
children.summary: Anthropic cites [[Net Revenue Retention of about 900%|p1191]] as of September 30, 2026. Its revenue grew [[1,368% year over year|p1192]] for the three months ended June 30, 2026, while compute and infrastructure expenses grew 300%. Trailing revenue per employee was [[over $6.6 million|p1193]] as of September 30, 2026, up from $1.4 million a year earlier. Revenue was [[$11.6 billion|p1195]] for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared with $787 million a year earlier. Operating income was [[$1.0 billion at an 8% margin|p1196]], compared with a $1.2 billion loss at a (152)% margin. Adjusted Operating Income was [[$2.2 billion at a 19% margin|p1197]], compared with a $1.0 billion loss at (129)%. As of June 30, 2026, the company had raised [[$141.1 billion|p1198]] in total and held $112.4 billion of cash and cash equivalents and $19.3 billion of short-term investments. It notes that forecasting compute needs years ahead carries risk.

children.title: Our Self-Reinforcing Loops
children.tldr: Two loops reinforce each other: customer feedback improves Claude and widens deployment, while growing revenue funds the compute, research and talent that make Claude more capable.
children.summary: In the [[improvement loop|p1200]], feedback from enterprise deployments helps Anthropic improve its models, platform and applications, which leads to wider adoption and more feedback. In the [[investment loop|p1201]], revenue from growing adoption funds compute, research and talent. Better capabilities then widen the addressable market and bring in more revenue.

children.title: Claude is Accelerating Our Ability to Close the Loop
children.tldr: Claude wrote over 90% of contributions to Anthropic's codebase in September 2026, and code volume per engineer rose more than 45 times versus 2024.
children.summary: Claude now helps run experiments, produce training data, automate evaluations and safety audits, and write code for its own successors, which Anthropic calls [["closing the loop"|p1202]]. On internal benchmarks of hard, open-ended engineering problems, Claude's success rate reached [[about 90% in September 2026|p1203]], up about 50 percentage points in nine months. Average daily code contributed per engineer in the quarter ended September 30, 2026 was [[over 45 times|p1203]] the 2024 average, and over 90% of September 2026 contributions were written by Claude. From December 31, 2024 to September 30, 2026, [[headcount grew over five times|p1204]], while quarterly revenue was 86 times higher. The list-price value of internal Claude use [[grew over 250 times|p1206]] from January to September 2026 and passed monthly personnel expense, excluding stock-based compensation, in April 2026. Anthropic notes that AI building AI poses [[safety risks|p1207]] covered by its Responsible Scaling Policy.

children.title: AI is Transforming Intelligence
children.tldr: Anthropic expects "Powerful AI" matching or beating top human experts across most fields to be widely available within a few years.
children.summary: Anthropic expects [[Powerful AI|p1208]] to become widely available within a few years. It defines this as AI with [[expert-level ability|p1209]] across most professional and scientific fields, the ability to use any interface a remote worker uses, [[autonomous work over hours, days, or weeks|p1211]], coordination with humans and other AI systems, and [[control of physical equipment|p1213]]. If risks are managed well, the company says this could [[compress decades of scientific progress into years|p1214]] and improve medicine, education and energy. The section goes on to cover [[scaling laws|s266]], the [[cognitive work opportunity|s267]], [[sector-level change|s268]], and [[safety and ethics|s269]].

children.title: Scaling Laws and the Predictability of Progress
children.tldr: AI performance improves predictably with model size, data and compute, and Anthropic expects demand for frontier AI to outstrip compute supply for the foreseeable future.
children.summary: Tasks such as complex math, experiment design and large parts of software development are [[now routine for AI|p1215]]. This progress has followed [[Scaling Laws|p1216]], established in a paper whose lead authors, including Dario Amodei and Jared Kaplan, later co-founded Anthropic. The company expects capabilities to keep advancing for many years and [[demand to outstrip supply|p1217]], limited mainly by compute. It says most demand will sit at the frontier, and that labs with proprietary methods and strong talent can do better than scale alone would predict.

children.title: A Near-Term Opportunity to Transform Cognitive Work
children.tldr: Anthropic estimates knowledge work was worth more than $40 trillion globally in 2025, and cites IDC's forecast of $22.5 trillion in cumulative AI economic impact by 2031.
children.summary: Anthropic says knowledge work represented [[more than $40 trillion|p1218]] of global economic value in 2025, and its near-term opportunity is to expand that value. It cites an IDC estimate of [[$22.5 trillion cumulative global economic impact|p1218]] from AI by 2031. As historical evidence that new technologies expand markets, it notes [[IT spend grew from about $1.2 trillion in 2006 to $4.3 trillion in 2025|p1219]] while cloud spend rose from zero to $1.9 trillion. Global GDP grew from about $34 trillion in 2000 to more than $118 trillion in 2025. Over the same period, the [[ten largest public technology companies|p1219]] grew aggregate revenue from $68 billion to more than $2.5 trillion, about 38 times, or about 11 times the rate of GDP growth.

children.title: Frontier AI May Reshape Entire Sectors and Accelerate Novel Discoveries
children.tldr: Anthropic sees cybersecurity as a key near-term opportunity and expects Claude to transform software, finance, healthcare and life sciences, with robotics and science to follow.
children.summary: Claude can now [[run complex projects autonomously over hours and days|p1220]], coordinating thousands of agents, which positions it to transform software, professional services, cybersecurity, financial services, and healthcare and life sciences. Anthropic calls [[cybersecurity one of its most important near-term opportunities|p1221]], offering Claude Security, the new OSS Scanner, and [[trusted access for vetted defenders|p1223]]. It expects to reach new areas such as [[robotics, manufacturing, and logistics|p1224]]. In life sciences, where pharmaceutical spend is expected to [[exceed $2 trillion in 2026|p1225]], Claude supports drug discovery, and the Model Hardware Standard lets agents run lab equipment. The company aims to capture part of the [[new economic output|p1226]] AI creates.

children.title: The Importance of Safety and Ethical Behavior
children.tldr: AI misuse, power concentration and misaligned systems pose serious risks, and Anthropic argues safety and predictable behavior are decisive for enterprises choosing an AI partner.
children.summary: Anthropic notes that bad actors have [[already used AI in high-profile cyberattacks|p1227]] and that misuse in biology could cause greater harm. It also warns that AI could concentrate power and wealth, and that misaligned systems could cause large-scale harm through hidden autonomous actions. The company says frontier AI firms must invest in safety, and that enterprises treat [[safeguards, predictable behavior, and accountability|p1227]] as decisive when choosing an AI partner.

children.title: Our Core Advantages
children.tldr: Anthropic's five core advantages are mission and focus, talent and culture, frontier and safety research, its approach to compute, and its enterprise strategy.
children.summary: Anthropic lists [[five core advantages|p1228]] behind its frontier position: [[mission and focus|s271]], [[talent and culture|s272]], [[frontier and safety research|s273]], its [[approach to compute|s274]], and its [[enterprise strategy|s275]].

children.title: Mission and Focus
children.tldr: Anthropic is a Delaware PBC overseen by the LTBT, and it held back its Mythos model in April 2026 as a gated preview because of its cyber capabilities.
children.summary: Anthropic's founders see safety as foundational, so the company is a [[Delaware PBC with the LTBT|p1229]] mandated to advance its mission, and it publishes its safety methods and Responsible Scaling Policy. The company says it does not pursue projects for commercial gain or novelty alone. As an example, in April 2026 it released its frontier model [[Mythos as a gated research preview through Project Glasswing|p1230]] for select cybersecurity organizations rather than broadly, because of its advanced ability to find cyber vulnerabilities. It believes this clarity [[speeds up decision making|p1232]].

children.title: Talent and Culture
children.tldr: Anthropic claims the world's deepest concentration of AI research talent, with about 1% regrettable attrition in the twelve months ended September 30, 2026.
children.summary: Anthropic values [[talent density over talent mass|p1233]]. It believes it has the [[deepest concentration of AI research talent|p1234]] in the world, and its founders originated Scaling Laws, GPT-2 and GPT-3, RLHF, and mechanistic interpretability. Regrettable attrition was [[about 1%|p1234]] in the trailing twelve months ended September 30, 2026. The company describes a [[low-ego culture of open critique|p1235]] built on long-standing trust.

children.title: Frontier and Safety Research
children.tldr: Anthropic credits its model lead to co-designed research and infrastructure, evidence-based pretraining, agent-focused post-training, and safety research that it treats as a commercial benefit.
children.summary: Anthropic says its researchers have [[outperformed bigger, better funded teams|p1237]], and that Claude is recognized for real-world performance in coding, medicine, law, science and math. Model research and inference infrastructure are [[designed together from the start|p1239]], with shared planning and targets. Pretraining is [[engineered for capital efficiency|p1240]]: improvements must be shown to hold as models scale before entering a frontier run. [[Post-training targets agentic work|p1241]] such as coding, tool use and operating software. The company argues [[safety research is a commercial benefit|p1242]], because aligned models follow instructions better and resist attacks like prompt injection.

children.title: Our Approach to Compute
children.tldr: Anthropic runs a fungible compute pool across four chip families, directing capacity to its most productive use and securing compute far ahead of demand.
children.summary: Anthropic's pretraining, post-training and inference research produce [[proprietary compute multipliers|p1244]] and lower serving costs. Its [[multi-chip architecture across AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, NVIDIA GPUs, and AMD GPUs|p1245]] lets it optimize price and performance and onboard new chips quickly. Internal systems treat all accelerators as [[one unified capacity pool|p1246]] shared across customer work, research and internal use. Because of long lead times, it [[secures compute well in advance|p1247]], sometimes pays ahead of delivery, and expects significant investment for the foreseeable future.

children.title: Enterprise Strategy
children.tldr: Claude's ExploitBench score rose from 40% to 91% in about four months, and Anthropic expects cybersecurity adoption to follow coding's fast path into production.
children.summary: Anthropic builds top models for the hardest problems and [[routes everyday work to suitable models|p1248]]. Claude is used across finance, insurance, healthcare, law, education, retail and other industries. The company builds for [[production use rather than benchmarks|p1249]], since governance and security often block enterprise adoption. Customers use Claude Code and Claude Cowork for [[long-running autonomous work|p1250]] and use Claude Platform to build AI-native products, and their feedback [[shapes the roadmap|p1251]]. Coding moved from suggesting lines to fleets of agents [[within roughly a year|p1252]]. Cybersecurity is following, with ExploitBench scores rising from [[40% with Opus 4.8 to 78% with Claude Mythos 5 and 91% with Opus 5.5|p1252]] over about four months.

children.title: Claude as a Virtual Collaborator
children.tldr: Anthropic says AI has reached a point where Claude can work as a Virtual Collaborator, doing professional work that might take a skilled person hours or days.
children.summary: Anthropic believes AI systems can now act as [[genuine collaborators in professional work|p1253]], quickly finishing tasks that might take a skilled professional hours or days. It calls these systems [[Virtual Collaborators|p1254]]: AI that uses the access, connections and context an organization grants it to run multi-step workflows. The company aims to reach knowledge workers globally, a group [[estimated to exceed one billion in 2028|p1254]]. [[Claude Code|s277]] is the clearest current example, [[Claude Cowork|s278]] extends the approach to other knowledge work, and Anthropic expects Claude to [[take on open-ended tasks lasting hours, days, or weeks|s279]].

children.title: Claude Code
children.tldr: Claude Code, Anthropic's coding agent, plans, writes, tests and debugs production-grade code, and the company calls its launch as significant as the first conversational AI assistants.
children.summary: Claude Code goes beyond suggesting code by [[planning, writing, testing, and debugging|p1255]] to produce production-grade code. Anthropic believes its launch was [[comparable in impact to the first widely adopted conversational AI assistants|p1255]] for enterprise AI. In one example, NASA engineers used it to write navigation commands for the Mars Perseverance rover, the [[first AI-planned drive on Mars|p1255]]. Software developers act as internal champions, and [[non-technical teams increasingly adopt|p1256]] Claude Code and Claude Cowork for their own workflows.

children.title: Claude Cowork
children.tldr: Claude Cowork brings Claude Code's agent design to all knowledge workers, and its adoption has outpaced Claude Code's at the same point after launch.
children.summary: Claude Cowork applies [[the same agentic architecture as Claude Code|p1257]] to general knowledge work, reading files, navigating applications and running multi-step workflows on a user's desktop. Released as a research preview in January 2026, its adoption as of September 30, 2026 [[outpaced Claude Code's|p1259]] at the equivalent point after Claude Code's February 2025 preview. In September 2026 Anthropic began [[merging Claude Cowork and Claude.ai|p1259]] into one application.

children.title: Extending Virtual Collaborators
children.tldr: Each Claude model generation can sustain longer, more complex autonomous work, and Anthropic aims for millions of agents acting as a country of geniuses in a data center.
children.summary: Benchmarks show [[substantial improvements across Claude model versions|p1260]] in the length and complexity of tasks completed reliably, with recent versions advancing most. Anthropic is working toward Claude handling [[open-ended tasks lasting hours, days, or weeks|p1261]], with millions of agents running in parallel, which it calls [[a country of geniuses in a data center|p1261]].

children.title: Claude is the Partner of Choice for Enterprises
children.tldr: Enterprises from startups to the world's largest companies choose Claude for frontier models, a shared platform, ready-made applications and trust built on safety research.
children.summary: Claude's enterprise customers range from [[AI-native startups to the largest enterprises|p1262]], and they tend to [[adopt the newest models as soon as they launch|p1263]]. Anthropic offers an integrated stack: models tuned along the capability, cost and speed curve, a [[Claude Platform|s281]] exposing the same building blocks Anthropic uses, and [[first-party applications|s282]]. Research on alignment, interpretability and security gives customers [[confidence to delegate more work|p1265]]. Customers become [[deeply embedded over time|s283]], and Anthropic distributes Claude through [[its own teams, cloud providers and partners|s284]].

children.title: Claude Platform—A Composable System for Building AI Solutions
children.tldr: Claude Platform supplies composable building blocks, including tool use, memory, an Agent SDK and the Model Context Protocol, that let customers build agents for any use case.
children.summary: Anthropic argues that demanding deployments need more than a capable model, including connectors, governance and orchestration, and that [[closing these gaps|p1267]] is a main reason customers build on Claude. The platform offers model features like [[tool use, computer use, memory, and extended thinking|p1268]], plus composition tools such as the [[Agent SDK, Claude Managed Agents and MCP|p1268]]. The same pieces power coding, research or compliance agents, which lets customers [[expand to new use cases without significant integration work|p1269]].

children.title: Applications That Meet Users Where They Are
children.tldr: Anthropic's applications reach users in their work, their industry and their existing software, from Claude Code to industry versions and Microsoft 365 integration.
children.summary: Claude Code and Claude Cowork serve users [[in their work|p1271]]; versions for financial services, healthcare, life sciences, legal, education and government come with [[domain knowledge and compliance controls pre-loaded|p1272]]; and [[Claude for Microsoft 365 and Claude in Chrome|p1273]] sit inside everyday software.

children.title: A Platform Customers Build Their Businesses On
children.tldr: Customers from Fortune 500 firms to research institutes build on Claude, and partners like Salesforce and Legora carry it to millions of end users.
children.summary: Users include Fortune 500 companies such as [[American International Group and Bristol Myers Squibb|p1274]], and research institutions such as the Garvan Institute, Gladstone Institutes and UCSF. Each integration [[deepens the relationship|p1275]], and companies like [[Legora and Salesforce|p1275]] have built products on Claude reaching millions. Anthropic believes its current revenue [[does not reflect the full economic value|p1276]] Claude creates.

children.title: Diffusion: Intelligence Available Everywhere
children.tldr: Claude spreads through product-led adoption, direct and Applied AI teams, cloud partners AWS, GCP and Azure, and a partner network of over 150,000 certified practitioners.
children.summary: Adoption often starts with individuals and [[grows into organization-wide use|p1278]], which direct sales teams then build on. [[Applied AI teams|p1280]] build custom solutions for select customers. Amazon, Google and Microsoft [[host Claude natively|p1282]], while Anthropic keeps direct contracts with customers and pays each provider a fee. The Claude Partner Network, launched in March 2026 with [[an initial $100 million|p1283]], had over 150,000 certified practitioners across over 4,000 organizations as of September 30, 2026. The [[Claude Frontier Academy|p1283]], launched in October 2026 with a $100 million commitment, aims to train 10,000 engineers by the end of 2027. [[Ode with Anthropic|p1284]], a services company formed with private equity firms, targets mid-sized companies.

children.title: Unprecedented Financial Model to Support Long-Term Investments
children.tldr: Every Fortune 10 company and over half the Fortune 500 paid Anthropic $100,000 or more over the trailing twelve months, and Anthropic says its financial model supports heavy long-term investment.
children.summary: As of September 30, 2026, customers paying $100,000 or more on a trailing twelve month basis included [[every Fortune 10 company, over 50% of the Fortune 500, and over 30% of the Global 2000|p1286]], among them the 10 largest banks and nine of the 10 largest pharmaceutical companies. Anthropic believes enterprises are still early in deployment. It points to [[rapid revenue growth|s286]], [[compute efficiency|s287]], [[operating efficiency|s288]] and a [[long-term investment approach|s289]] as advantages for funding frontier AI.

children.title: Significant Revenue Growth
children.tldr: Customers paying $100,000 or more a year grew from over 950 to over 11,900 in the year to September 30, 2026, with Net Revenue Retention near 900%.
children.summary: Between September 30, 2025 and September 30, 2026, customers with $100,000 or more of trailing twelve month revenue grew [[from more than 950 to more than 11,900|p1289]]. Run-Rate Revenue is [[not GAAP revenue or a forecast|p1291]] and can include customers later cut off for policy violations. Net Revenue Retention was [[approximately 900%|p1292]] as of September 30, 2026. Claude Enterprise users without Claude Code spent under $75 a month on average, while the [[top 5% of Claude Code users spent about 20 times that|p1293]]. Claude Fable 5.1 cut typical workload costs [[about 25% versus Fable 5|p1294]], and Opus 5.5 cut cost per task about 40% versus Opus 5, with margins preserved. After Opus 4.5 launched in November 2025, quarter-over-quarter revenue growth [[rose from 48% to 132%|p1295]] between the quarters ended December 31, 2025 and March 31, 2026.

children.title: Compute Efficiency
children.tldr: Anthropic says premium enterprise pricing, a flexible multi-partner compute fleet and Claude's help optimizing inference let it get more from each dollar of compute.
children.summary: Enterprise workloads bring [[stronger retention and higher monetization than consumer AI|p1296]]. A [[single fleet spread across multiple strategic partners|p1297]] gives diversified supply and room to optimize. Claude has also [[helped write compute multipliers|p1298]] central to efficient inference.

children.title: Operating Efficiency
children.tldr: With about 5,300 employees, Anthropic earned over $6.6 million of trailing revenue per employee, and Claude wrote over 90% of its code contributions in September 2026.
children.summary: As of September 30, 2026, trailing twelve month revenue per employee was [[over $6.6 million with about 5,300 employees|p1299]]. Product-led growth and partners let revenue grow [[without being limited by sales hiring|p1300]]. Claude wrote [[over 90% of codebase contributions|p1301]] in September 2026, and daily code volume per engineer in the quarter ended September 30, 2026 was over 45 times the 2024 average.

children.title: Long-Term Investment Philosophy
children.tldr: Revenue rose 1,368% year over year in the quarter ended June 30, 2026, while operating margin moved from (152)% to 8%.
children.summary: Comparing the three months ended June 30, 2026 with the same 2025 period, [[revenue rose 1,368%|p1303]], [[compute and infrastructure expense rose 300%|p1304]] and other operating expenses rose 741%. Operating margin went [[from (152)% to 8%|p1306]] and Adjusted Operating Margin [[from (129)% to 19%|p1307]]. Anthropic has signed purchase commitments and leases whose aggregate amount is left blank in this draft, with [[substantially all spending beyond 2030 expected between 2031 and 2045|p1309]].

children.title: Our Growth Strategy
children.tldr: Anthropic plans to keep investing in talent, compute, model capability and safety, wider availability, customer growth, new markets and acquisitions.
children.summary: The strategy rests on [[seven areas of continuous investment|p1311]]. Anthropic will recruit and retain mission-aligned talent while using Claude to [[grow without growing headcount linearly|p1312]]. It intends to [[secure more compute and expand its own data centers|p1313]] while improving efficiency. It also plans to [[advance Claude's intelligence, capability and safety|s291]] and to [[drive adoption and enter new markets|s292]].

children.title: • Advance Claude’s Intelligence, Capability, and Safety. Maintaining our leadership in frontier
children.tldr: Anthropic will advance Claude's intelligence and safety together and widen access across its own apps, AWS, GCP, Azure and enterprise software.
children.summary: Anthropic plans to extend Claude's [[autonomous work across professional domains|p1314]] from software to healthcare and cybersecurity. Customers reach Claude through apps like [[Claude Code, Claude Cowork, Claude.ai, Claude Security, Claude Design and Claude Science|p1315]], cloud marketplaces and embedded integrations, which the company will expand.

children.title: • Drive Adoption Across Existing and New Customers. We intend to grow our direct go-to-
children.tldr: Anthropic will grow sales, partner and international reach, push into life sciences and physical work, and pursue deals like its April 2026 Coefficient Bio acquisition.
children.summary: Anthropic intends to grow its [[direct and Applied AI teams|p1316]], deepen cloud partnerships, invest in prosumers and expand internationally. In life sciences, where global pharmaceutical spend is [[expected to exceed $2 trillion in 2026|p1317]], it has built a molecular biology lab and hired experts, and Claude can now [[operate lab and manufacturing equipment|p1317]]. It will selectively pursue acquisitions and partnerships, such as [[acquiring Coefficient Bio in April 2026|p1320]] and launching Ode with Anthropic.

children.title: Our Models, Platform, and Applications
children.tldr: Anthropic builds models, a developer platform, and applications as one integrated stack, so improvements at any layer carry through to customers.
children.summary: Anthropic works at every layer of frontier AI: the [[Claude model family|s294]] supplies the intelligence, the [[Claude Platform|s295]] exposes it as composable building blocks, and [[first-party applications|s300]] package those blocks into ready products. The company says this [[integrated approach|p1321]] makes it a partner of choice. It opens the platform to all builders and builds its own apps, such as [[Claude Code and Claude Cowork|p1323]], to show where models are heading, designing them for expected future capabilities. Anthropic also offers [[vertical solutions|s301]] for specific industries and designs products so customers can [[interact with Claude like a colleague|p1324]] without learning how the models work.

children.title: The Claude Model Family
children.tldr: Claude comes in four model classes: Mythos (including Fable), Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku, trading off capability, cost, and speed.
children.summary: The Claude family has [[four model classes|p1325]], all supporting text, code, and multimodal inputs. [[Mythos (including Fable)|p1326]] is the most capable class. Fable is generally available with production safeguards, while Mythos goes to vetted cybersecurity and life sciences users through trusted-access programs. The class launched as Claude Mythos Preview in April 2026, Fable 5 became generally available in June 2026, and Mythos 5.1 and Fable 5.1 were released in September 2026. [[Opus|p1327]], led by Claude Opus 5.5, is the enterprise workhorse for reasoning-heavy tasks. [[Sonnet|p1328]] balances performance, cost, and speed for general use, and [[Haiku|p1329]] is the lowest-cost, fastest class for high-volume work.

children.title: The Claude Platform
children.tldr: The Claude Platform lets businesses build, manage, and deploy agentic AI applications on reliable, secure infrastructure.
