children.summary: Dario Amodei and Daniela Amodei's salaries each rose to [[$915,000|p1724]] on January 16, 2026 and to $1,380,000 on July 1, 2026. Krishna Rao's salary rose to $1,250,000 on February 1, 2026.

children.title: Long-Term Equity Incentive Program
children.tldr: In February 2026 each Amodei received 1,431,490 options and 2,374,010 RSUs, Rao received 1,122,840 options and 1,862,140 RSUs, and the Amodeis got 537,430 more RSUs in July.
children.summary: On [[February 20, 2026|p1725]], the board granted 1,431,490 options and 2,374,010 RSUs to each of Dario Amodei and Daniela Amodei, and 1,122,840 options and 1,862,140 RSUs to Krishna Rao. The options have a $17.66 exercise price and vest monthly over one year. The RSUs vest quarterly in twelfths from May 20, 2027, once the registration statement is effective. On [[July 15, 2026|p1726]], each co-founder received another 537,430 RSUs, vesting quarterly in sixteenths from August 20, 2026, subject to the same IPO condition.

children.title: Severance Benefits
children.tldr: October 2026 severance agreements give the Amodeis 24 months of salary and Rao 12 months, plus 12 months of COBRA and 12 months of vesting acceleration.
children.summary: In October 2026 each NEO signed an [[Executive Severance Agreement|p1727]]. On a termination without cause or resignation for good reason, it pays 24 months of salary for Dario Amodei and Daniela Amodei and 12 months for Krishna Rao, 12 months of COBRA premiums, and 12 months of accelerated time-based vesting. Mr. Rao's change of control acceleration continues unchanged. These changes will appear in the [[2026 pay disclosure|p1728]].

children.title: Perquisites and Other Executive Benefits
children.tldr: Anthropic paid $2.5 million in HSR antitrust filing fees for each Amodei in October 2026 and began providing security to Krishna Rao in 2026.
children.summary: In October 2026 the company paid the FTC [[$2.5 million each|s407]] in Hart-Scott-Rodino filing fees on behalf of Dario Amodei and Daniela Amodei. It also began [[security services for Mr. Rao|s408]] in 2026 after a third-party study.

children.title: HSR Filing Fees
children.tldr: In October 2026 Anthropic paid $2.5 million each in HSR filing fees to the FTC on behalf of Dario Amodei and Daniela Amodei.
children.summary: Anthropic paid the FTC [[$2.5 million each|p1729]] in Hart-Scott-Rodino filing fees owed by Dario Amodei and Daniela Amodei for acquiring and holding company securities. The board said this ensured antitrust compliance and supported retention and alignment with stockholders.

children.title: Security Services
children.tldr: In 2026 Anthropic began providing security services to CFO Krishna Rao after commissioning a third-party security study.
children.summary: In 2026 the company [[began offering security services to Mr. Rao|p1730]] and hired a security consulting firm to study his risks, viewing the cost as necessary given his role.

children.title: Grants of Plan-Based Awards in 2025
children.tldr: In 2025 only the Amodeis received grants: each got 992,500 options at $2.38 valued at $4,028,558 and 1,717,000 RSUs valued at $9,264,932.
children.summary: On June 12, 2025, Dario Amodei and Daniela Amodei each received [[992,500 options at $2.38 per share|p1732]] with a grant date fair value of $4,028,558, and 1,717,000 RSUs worth $9,264,932. Krishna Rao received no grants in 2025. The RSUs require both service and performance conditions and have [[no threshold or maximum levels|p1733]]. Values are grant date fair values, not realized value.

children.title: Outstanding Equity Awards at 2025 Year-End
children.tldr: At 2025 year end, each Amodei held 1,717,000 unvested RSUs worth $30,317,069, and Rao held 8,166,670 unvested options at $1.30.
children.summary: As of December 31, 2025, Dario Amodei and Daniela Amodei each held [[909,790 exercisable and 82,710 unexercisable options|p1735]] at $2.38, expiring June 11, 2035, plus 1,717,000 unvested RSUs valued at $30,317,069. Krishna Rao held 5,756,350 exercisable and 8,166,670 unexercisable options at $1.30, expiring May 30, 2034. Values use a [[fair market value of $17.66 per share|p1736]] at December 31, 2025.

children.title: Option Exercises and Stock Vested in 2025
children.tldr: In 2025 each Amodei had 5,058,340 shares vest worth $12,013,558, and Rao exercised 76,980 options for a $385,285 gain.
children.summary: During 2025, Dario Amodei and Daniela Amodei each had [[5,058,340 shares vest|p1738]] with a realized value of $12,013,558. Krishna Rao exercised 76,980 options, realizing $385,285. Exercise value is [[fair market value minus exercise price|p1738]], and vesting value is [[fair market value on the vesting date|p1739]].

children.title: Employment, Severance, and Change of Control Arrangements with Our NEOs
children.tldr: Rao's 2024 offer letter gave six months' salary, six months of COBRA and 1/8 option vesting on termination, and full vesting on a change of control termination.
children.summary: Krishna Rao's [[March 2, 2024 offer letter|p1740]] set at-will employment, salary, a hiring option grant and severance terms, and ended in October 2026. On a termination without cause or a good reason resignation, he would get [[six months of salary|p1741]], up to six months of COBRA and vesting of 1/8 of his options, subject to a release and other conditions. If this happened around a change of control, or his awards would be cancelled for nothing, [[all unvested equity would vest|p1742]]. That benefit continues under an October 2026 letter agreement.

children.title: Potential Payments upon Termination or Change of Control
children.tldr: Only Krishna Rao had severance rights in 2025, worth $29,067,579 on a regular termination and $134,031,467 on a change of control termination.
children.summary: In 2025 [[only Mr. Rao|p1744]] was eligible for severance. Had he been terminated on December 31, 2025, his benefits would have totaled [[$29,067,579|s414]] in a normal qualifying termination and [[$134,031,467|s415]] in connection with a change of control. The Amodeis would have received nothing.

children.title: Potential Payments upon Termination Apart from a Change of Control
children.tldr: A qualifying termination of Rao on December 31, 2025 would have paid $29,067,579, mostly $28,626,500 of accelerated options; the Amodeis would get nothing.
children.summary: If terminated without cause or for good reason on December 31, 2025, Krishna Rao would have received [[$425,000 in cash|p1746]], $28,626,500 in accelerated equity and $16,079 in health coverage, for a total of $29,067,579. The Amodeis would have received nothing. The equity value reflects [[1,750,000 option shares|p1747]] valued at $17.66 minus the $1.30 exercise price.

children.title: Potential Payments upon Termination in Connection with a Change of Control
children.tldr: A change of control termination of Rao on December 31, 2025 would have paid $134,031,467, mostly $133,590,388 of fully accelerated options.
children.summary: In a qualifying termination tied to a change of control on December 31, 2025, Krishna Rao would have received [[$425,000 in cash|p1749]], $133,590,388 in accelerated equity and $16,079 in health coverage, for a total of $134,031,467. The Amodeis would have received nothing. The equity value covers all [[8,166,670 unvested option shares|p1749]] at $17.66 minus the $1.30 exercise price.

children.title: Equity Plans
children.tldr: Anthropic is replacing its 2021 Stock Plan with a new 2026 Equity Incentive Plan and adding a 2026 Employee Stock Purchase Plan, both taking effect with the IPO.
children.summary: This section covers three equity plans. The [[2026 Equity Incentive Plan|s417]] becomes effective just before the registration statement is effective. It allows stock options, stock appreciation rights, restricted stock, RSUs and stock bonus awards, and its share reserve can grow by up to 5% each year. The [[Amended & Restated 2021 Stock Plan|s418]] will terminate at the same time and make no new grants, although existing awards stay in place under its terms. The [[2026 Employee Stock Purchase Plan|s419]] lets eligible employees buy Class A common stock at no less than 85% of fair market value, with its reserve growing by up to 1% each year.

children.title: 2026 Equity Incentive Plan
children.tldr: The 2026 Equity Incentive Plan takes effect at the IPO, absorbs leftover 2021 Plan shares, and can grow by up to 5% of outstanding economic shares each year through 2036.
children.summary: The board adopted the 2026 Plan on [[September 1, 2026|p1750]], and stockholders approved it on October 22, 2026. Its reserve includes shares still available under the 2021 Plan and shares from 2021 awards that would otherwise have returned to that plan. The reserve rises each year from fiscal 2027 through fiscal 2036 by the lesser of [[5% of outstanding economic common stock|p1752]] or an amount the board sets. The [[compensation committee|p1754]] administers the plan and may run exchange programs that reprice awards. The plan allows [[options, SARs, restricted stock, RSUs and stock bonus awards|p1756]]. Annual awards plus cash fees for a non-employee director are capped at [[$1,000,000|p1763]], or $2,000,000 in the first year of service. In a [[corporate transaction|p1767]], the administrator decides how awards are treated, which can include cancellation for no consideration. The board-replacement trigger in the [[change in control definition|p1769]] does not apply until both the Class F and Class T Sunset Times have passed.

children.title: Amended & Restated 2021 Stock Plan
children.tldr: The 2021 Stock Plan, with 3,864,826,090 Class A shares reserved, ends at the IPO; existing awards continue, and shares from awards that are forfeited or withheld move to the 2026 Plan.
children.summary: The board adopted the 2021 Plan on [[January 28, 2021|p1772]] and last amended it effective May 28, 2026. The plan will terminate just before the registration statement becomes effective, and no new awards will be granted under it. A total of [[3,864,826,090 shares|p1773]] of Class A common stock are reserved under the plan. After the IPO, shares from awards that are forfeited, withheld or repurchased will become available under the 2026 Plan. The company has granted [[stock options, restricted stock, and RSUs|p1775]] under the plan, and administration passes to the compensation committee after the offering. In a [[Corporate Transaction|p1778]], the administrator may continue, assume, substitute or cash out awards, or cancel them for no consideration.

children.title: 2026 Employee Stock Purchase Plan
children.tldr: The 2026 ESPP lets eligible employees buy Class A shares at no less than 85% of fair market value, with its reserve growing by up to 1% each year through 2036.
children.summary: The board adopted the ESPP on [[September 1, 2026|p1780]], and stockholders approved it on October 22, 2026. It has a [[Section 423 component and a non-423 component|p1781]]. The share reserve rises each year from fiscal 2027 through fiscal 2036 by the lesser of [[1% of outstanding economic common stock|p1783]] or an amount the board sets. Under the 423 component, each employee can buy no more than [[$25,000 of stock per year|p1786]], and employees holding 5% or more of the voting power cannot take part. Offerings can last up to [[27 months|p1787]]. Under the 423 component, contributions can be up to [[15% of earnings|p1788]]. The purchase price is at least [[85% of fair market value|p1789]] on the offering date or on the purchase date, whichever value is lower. If a successor company does not assume the purchase rights in a [[corporate transaction|p1792]], participants' accumulated contributions are used to buy shares before the deal closes.

children.title: Certain Relationships and Related Person Transactions
children.tldr: Since January 1, 2023, Anthropic's main related person dealings were Spark Capital's preferred stock purchases, founder tender offer sales, voting and proxy arrangements, and funding of the Long-Term Benefit Trust.
children.summary: This section lists every transaction since January 1, 2023, and every proposed one, where Anthropic is a participant, [[more than $120,000|p1797]] is involved, and a director, executive officer, holder of [[more than 5% of any voting class|p1798]], or a family member of one of these has a material interest. The main items are [[preferred stock purchases|s421]] by Spark Capital and a director's entity, [[founder sales in tender offers|s430]], [[Dario Amodei's proxy over donor fund shares|s431]], a [[new Stockholders' Agreement|s433]] with the LTBT and Founder LLC, and [[payments to the LTBT|s438]]. It also covers [[director and officer liability limits|s440]] and the audit committee's future role in [[reviewing such transactions|s441]].

children.title: Equity Financings
children.tldr: Spark Capital, linked to director Yasmin Razavi, bought preferred stock in every round from Series C through Series H, about $777 million in total.
children.summary: Entities affiliated with Spark Capital, where director Yasmin Razavi is a managing member of the general partners, bought into each of Anthropic's last six preferred rounds. Their largest purchase was $439,999,521 in the [[Series H-1 round|s422]], which raised $45.7 billion in total. Smaller Spark purchases came in [[Series G-1|s423]], [[Series F-1|s424]], [[Series E-1|s425]], [[Series D-1|s426]] and [[Series C-1|s427]]. Bodhi LLC, owned by director Vas Narasimhan and his wife, also bought $9,999,614 of Series H-1 stock.

children.title: Series H Redeemable Convertible Preferred Stock Financing
children.tldr: Anthropic raised $45,729,447,703 selling Series H-1 preferred at $589.0095 per share in May and June 2026; Spark Capital bought $439,999,521 and Bodhi LLC $9,999,614.
children.summary: From May to June 2026, Anthropic sold [[77,637,878 Series H-1 shares at $589.0095 each|p1799]], raising $45,729,447,703. Related buyers were [[Spark Capital, which bought 747,016 shares for $439,999,521|p1800]], and Bodhi LLC, owned by director Vas Narasimhan and his wife, which bought [[16,977 shares for $9,999,614|p1800]].

children.title: Series G Redeemable Convertible Preferred Stock Financing
children.tldr: Anthropic raised $23,454,545,698 selling Series G-1 preferred at $259.1364 per share in early 2026; Spark Capital bought 96,474 shares for $24,999,925.
children.summary: From January to February 2026, Anthropic sold [[90,510,425 Series G-1 shares at $259.1364 each|p1801]], for $23,454,545,698 in total. The only related buyer was [[Spark Capital, which bought 96,474 shares for $24,999,925|p1802]] through funds where director Yasmin Razavi is a managing member of the general partner.

children.title: Series F Redeemable Convertible Preferred Stock Financing
children.tldr: Anthropic raised $12,999,992,602 selling Series F-1 preferred at $140.9676 per share in August and September 2025; Spark Capital bought $61,999,947.
children.summary: From August to September 2025, Anthropic sold [[92,219,720 Series F-1 shares at $140.9676 each|p1803]], for $12,999,992,602. [[Spark Capital bought 439,817 shares for $61,999,947|p1804]] through its Spark V funds, linked to director Yasmin Razavi.

children.title: Series E Redeemable Convertible Preferred Stock Financing
children.tldr: Anthropic raised $3,567,668,210 selling Series E-1 preferred at $56.0865 per share in early 2025; Spark Capital bought $99,999,930.
children.summary: From January to March 2025, Anthropic sold [[63,610,106 Series E-1 shares at $56.0865 each|p1805]], for $3,567,668,210. [[Spark Capital bought 1,782,959 shares for $99,999,930|p1806]] through its Spark V funds, linked to director Yasmin Razavi.

children.title: Series D Redeemable Convertible Preferred Stock Financing
children.tldr: Anthropic raised $1,199,540,154 selling Series D preferred at $30.0045 per share in 2024; Spark Capital bought $74,999,968.
children.summary: From January to May 2024, Anthropic sold [[39,978,675 Series D-1 and D-3 shares at $30.0045 each|p1807]], for $1,199,540,154, and converted a $1,000,000 SAFE into 33,328 shares. [[Spark Capital bought 2,499,624 Series D-1 shares for $74,999,968|p1808]] through its Spark IV funds, linked to director Yasmin Razavi.

children.title: Series C Redeemable Convertible Preferred Stock Financing
children.tldr: Anthropic raised $445,337,400 selling Series C preferred at $11.2261 per share in 2023; Spark Capital bought $74,999,991.
children.summary: From March to June 2023, Anthropic sold [[39,669,823 Series C-1 and C-2 shares at $11.2261 each|p1809]], for $445,337,400, and converted a $1,000,000 SAFE into 89,078 shares. [[Spark Capital bought 6,680,859 Series C-1 shares for $74,999,991|p1810]] through its Spark IV funds, linked to director Yasmin Razavi.

children.title: Right of First Refusal
children.tldr: Anthropic's right to buy shares stockholders propose to sell, which binds Dario and Daniela Amodei and Spark Capital entities, ends when the offering closes.
children.summary: Under its equity plans and a [[right of first refusal and co-sale agreement dated May 28, 2026|p1811]], Anthropic or its assignees may buy shares that stockholders propose to sell to others. Dario Amodei, Daniela Amodei and Spark Capital entities are parties, and the right [[terminates when the offering is completed|p1811]].

children.title: Voting Agreement
children.tldr: A May 28, 2026 voting agreement on director elections, involving Spark Capital entities and Dario and Daniela Amodei, terminates at the offering.
children.summary: Under an [[amended and restated voting agreement dated May 28, 2026|p1812]], certain holders, including Spark Capital entities and Dario and Daniela Amodei, agreed to vote their shares on matters such as director elections. The agreement [[ends when the offering is completed|p1812]], leaving no Class A or Class N holder with special board election rights under it.

children.title: Tender Offers
children.tldr: Founders and executives sold Class A shares in two tender offers: $4.66 billion at $25.9136 per share in April 2026 and $156.7 million at $5.61 in June 2025.
children.summary: In April 2026, Anthropic facilitated a stockholder syndicate's tender offer at [[$25.9136 per share|p1813]], in which 179,883,540 Class A shares were tendered for $4,661,437,298. Sellers included Dario Amodei, Daniela Amodei, executive Krishna Rao and Daniela Amodei's spouse Holden Karnofsky. In June 2025, Anthropic ran its own tender offer at [[$5.61 per share|p1814]] for 27,942,000 shares and $156,716,898 in total, in which Dario and Daniela Amodei sold shares.

children.title: Irrevocable Proxy Agreements
children.tldr: Dario Amodei holds irrevocable proxies to vote, at his sole discretion, Anthropic shares owned by two donor advised funds, excluding shares his own family donated.
children.summary: Anthropic has [[irrevocable proxy agreements|p1815]] with Daffy Charitable Fund and Dechomai Asset Trust, which can receive donated Anthropic shares and each hold less than 5% of any voting class. [[Dario Amodei is the proxyholder|p1816]] and may vote their shares at his sole discretion, except shares donated by him, his family or affiliates. The board may designate other proxyholders.

children.title: Employment Arrangements with Immediate Family Members of Our Executive Officers
children.tldr: Holden Karnofsky, Daniela Amodei's spouse, has worked at Anthropic since January 2025, earning $430,213 cash in 2025 plus options and RSUs.
children.summary: Holden Karnofsky, spouse of Chairperson Daniela Amodei, was [[paid $430,213 in total cash compensation in 2025|p1817]]; the 2026 figure is left blank in the filing. He also received options on 179,500 Class A shares and RSUs covering 761,700 shares, which Anthropic says was [[in line with comparable employees|p1817]].

children.title: Stockholders’ Agreement
children.tldr: At the offering, Anthropic will sign a Stockholders' Agreement with the LTBT and Founder LLC covering board composition, notice rights, and expense and indemnity protections.
children.summary: Just before the offering closes, Anthropic will enter a [[Stockholders' Agreement with the LTBT and the Founder LLC|p1818]] dealing with board composition. Both parties agree to [[vote to carry out the board provisions|s434]], the LTBT gets [[advance notice of major actions|s435]], and Anthropic will [[cover their expenses and indemnify them|s436]]. Anthropic is also [[paying the Founder LLC's legal fees|s437]] for structuring the governance arrangements.

children.title: Voting Agreement
children.tldr: The Founder LLC and LTBT will vote their shares to carry out the board composition and director nomination and removal rules.
children.summary: Under the Stockholders' Agreement, the Founder LLC and the LTBT agree to [[vote their shares and take other actions|p1819]] that give effect to the board composition, nomination and removal provisions described elsewhere in the filing.

children.title: Notice Rights
children.tldr: While Class T stock exists, Anthropic must give the LTBT advance notice before major actions, including transferring control of an AI model above board capability thresholds.
children.summary: As long as Class T stock is outstanding, Anthropic must give the LTBT [[advance written notice|p1820]], which can be waived, before a liquidation, a transfer of control of an AI model exceeding board set capability thresholds, a sale of 50% or more of its voting power or economic interests, or a bankruptcy filing.

children.title: Expense Reimbursement and Indemnification
children.tldr: Anthropic will pay the Founder LLC's and LTBT's reasonable expenses, including legal fees, tied to their stock ownership and governance roles, and indemnify them.
children.summary: Anthropic will [[reimburse or advance reasonable out of pocket expenses|p1821]], including legal fees, that the Founder LLC and LTBT incur in connection with their share ownership and governance rights. It will also sign agreements to [[indemnify both entities and their related persons|p1821]] to the fullest extent the law permits.

children.title: Reimbursement of Legal Fees
children.tldr: Anthropic is paying the Founder LLC's legal fees for structuring its pre-IPO governance; the expected amount is left blank in the filing.
children.summary: Anthropic has paid or will pay the [[Founder LLC's legal fees|p1822]] for structuring and negotiating its governance arrangements before the offering; the expected total is not yet filled in.

children.title: Transactions with the LTBT
children.tldr: Anthropic funds the LTBT, paying $8,425,213 in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, after $2,716,750 in 2023, $0 in 2024 and $906,089 in 2025.
children.summary: Anthropic funds the LTBT, which holds all Class T stock, to support its operations and trustee pay. It paid [[$2,716,750, $0 and $906,089|p1823]] in 2023, 2024 and 2025, and [[$8,425,213 in the nine months ended September 30, 2026|p1823]]. The LTBT is consolidated on Anthropic's balance sheet as a variable interest entity.

children.title: Other Transactions
children.tldr: Apart from those described and equity awards to officers and directors, Anthropic reports no other related person transactions above $120,000 since January 1, 2023.
children.summary: Executives and some directors hold [[stock options and RSUs|p1824]] described under Executive Compensation. Otherwise, Anthropic states it has had [[no other related person transactions over $120,000|p1825]] since January 1, 2023, and believes the terms above were comparable to dealings with unrelated parties.

children.title: Limitation of Liability and Indemnification of Officers and Directors
children.tldr: New charter and bylaws will limit directors' and officers' personal liability as far as Delaware law allows and require indemnification and expense advances, backed by insurance.
children.summary: Anthropic's new charter will [[shield directors and certain officers from monetary damages|p1826]] for fiduciary breaches, except for disloyalty, bad faith, unlawful dividends, improper personal benefit, and, for officers, claims brought by the company. The bylaws will require [[indemnification and advance payment of expenses|p1833]], and [[individual indemnification agreements|p1834]] may go further. These terms [[may discourage stockholder suits|p1835]], and failing to balance public benefit duties will not by itself count as bad faith or disloyalty. Anthropic carries [[directors' and officers' insurance|p1836]], though the SEC views indemnification for Securities Act liabilities as [[unenforceable|p1839]].

children.title: Policies and Procedures for Related Person Transactions
children.tldr: After the offering, the audit committee will review and approve or reject related person transactions over $120,000.
children.summary: After the offering, the [[audit committee will review and approve or disapprove|p1840]] transactions over $120,000 in which a director, executive officer, director nominee, holder of more than 5% of any voting class, or a family member has a material interest.

children.title: Principal and Selling Stockholders
children.tldr: The Founder LLC's single Class F share will carry a fixed 50.1% of voting power after the offering; each co-founder holds roughly 230 to 245 million Class A shares.
children.summary: The table shows ownership as of September 30, 2026, before and after the offering, for executives, directors, holders of over 5%, and [[selling stockholders|p1846]]; percentages and offered share counts are left blank. [[Dario Amodei beneficially owns 245,259,100 Class A shares|p1854]], including 4,621,120 shares under voting proxies, and Daniela Amodei 241,408,940. All executives and directors together hold 496,360,810. The [[LTBT holds the one Class T share|p1855]], and the Founder LLC holds the one Class F share, which carries [[a fixed 50.1% of voting power|p1856]], limiting Class A holders to 49.9%. Co-founders Tom Brown, Jack Clark, Jared Kaplan, Sam McCandlish and Christopher Olah are [[selling stockholders|p1856]], and the seven co-founders will [[decide the Class F vote by one vote each|p1857]].

children.title: Description of Capital Stock
children.tldr: Anthropic will have five common stock classes plus preferred stock, with Class F holding a fixed 50.1% of voting power and only Class A and Class N sharing in dividends.
children.summary: After the offering, Anthropic will be authorized to issue [[460,000,000,002 shares|s444]], split among Class A, Class N, Class T, Class F, Class E and preferred stock. Class A carries one vote per share, Class N carries none, and the [[Class F share held by the Founder LLC|s476]] carries 50.1% of voting power. Only Class A and Class N share in dividends and liquidation. No preferred stock will be outstanding, but the board may [[issue it with 80% director approval|s454]] and, before the Class F Sunset Time, the Founder LLC's consent. Class F votes as a [[majority of Continuing Founders|s477]] directs, and changes to Class F or LTBT rights require supermajorities. Certain holders, plus Google and Broadcom, have [[registration rights|s457]]. Delaware law and the new charter and bylaws contain [[anti-takeover provisions|s463]]. The company has applied to list Class A stock on the [[Nasdaq Global Select Market under "ANT"|s480]].

children.title: General
children.tldr: After the offering, Anthropic will be authorized to issue 460,000,000,002 shares across five classes of common stock plus preferred stock, with sharply different voting and economic rights.
children.summary: This section summarizes the capital stock terms in the charter and bylaws that take effect just before the offering. Authorized stock will total [[460,000,000,002 shares|p1858]] at $0.00001 par value: [[300,000,000,000 Class A shares|p1859]], [[100,000,000,000 Class N shares|p1860]], [[one Class T share|p1861]], [[one Class F share|p1862]], [[30,000,000,000 Class E shares|p1863]] and [[30,000,000,000 preferred shares|p1864]]. On a pro forma basis as of September 30, 2026, one Class T share and one Class F share were outstanding, and [[no Class E or preferred shares|p1865]] were outstanding. A summary table shows that Class A has one vote per share, Class N has none, and [[Class F carries 50.1% of voting power|p1867]]. Only Class A and Class N share in dividends and liquidation. Classes T, F and E receive only par value on liquidation and are [[redeemable for no consideration|p1870]] when certain events occur.

children.title: Common Stock
children.tldr: Anthropic has four common stock classes: Participating Common Stock (Class A and Class N), Class T for the LTBT, Class F for the Founder LLC, and Class E for employees.
children.summary: The company's common stock falls into four classes. [[Participating Common Stock|p1872]] is split into Class A and Class N. [[Class T goes to the LTBT|p1873]], [[Class F to the Founder LLC|p1874]], and [[Class E to employees other than the co-founders|p1875]]. The classes differ in [[voting rights|s446]], [[conversion and transfer|s447]], [[redemption|s448]] and [[dividend rights|s449]]. They are also governed by [[sunset provisions|s453]], which set out when the Class T and Class F control features end.

children.title: Voting Rights
children.tldr: Class F will carry 50.1% of total voting power, Class A gets one vote per share, and Class N gets no vote except where the law requires one.
children.summary: Class A holders get [[one vote per share|p1876]] on general matters, including the election of directors other than the Class T directors. Class N holders [[cannot vote|p1877]] except where Delaware law requires a separate series vote. The Class T holder votes only on specific charter matters, most importantly [[electing a majority of the board|p1878]]. The Class F holder controls [[50.1% of total voting power|p1879]] on general matters, voted under the Founder LLC Agreement. Class E holders vote only on limited matters, such as the [[Specified Class T Director|p1880]] when the NGC disagrees with the LTBT, changes to the LTBT, and Class T redemption.

children.title: Conversion and Transferability
children.tldr: Only Class A and Class N shares can be freely transferred, and Class N converts to Class A when sold publicly or to an unaffiliated holder of at most 9.99%.
children.summary: Class A shares are [[transferable|p1881]], subject to the law and lock-ups. Class N shares, held mainly by strategic business partners, convert into Class A when they are sold in a registered offering or on the open market, or when they go to an unaffiliated third party that will own [[no more than 9.99%|p1882]] of any class afterward. Class T can be transferred only with the approval of the [[Trust Amendment Threshold|p1883]]. Class F can be transferred only in a [[board approved reorganization of the Founder LLC|p1884]] that leaves its members unchanged. Class E is [[not transferable|p1885]].

children.title: Redemption
children.tldr: Class A and Class N are not redeemable, while Class T, Class F and Class E can be redeemed for no consideration under detailed approval thresholds and triggering events.
children.summary: Class A and Class N [[cannot be redeemed|p1886]]. Class T can be redeemed for nothing with the approval of [[80% of the board and 80% of the Trustees|p1889]]. Without Trustee support, redemption requires stockholder votes. Until the third anniversary, it needs [[unanimous Continuing Founders, a Class E majority and a Class A majority|p1891]]. At any time, it can pass with [[66 2/3% of founders, 75% of Class E votes and a Class A majority|p1892]]. Once Class F is gone, it needs [[85% of outstanding Class A|p1893]]. Class F is redeemed on a Supermajority founder decision, on dissolution of the Founder LLC, or at the end of the Class F Transition Period, which starts after [[fewer than three Continuing Founders for 90 days|p1894]]. Departing employees lose [[half their Class E shares each year|p1895]], and they lose all of them on death, incapacity, termination for cause or joining a competitor.

children.title: Dividend Rights
children.tldr: Only Class A and Class N holders may receive dividends, and only when and as the board decides; Classes T, F and E get none.
children.summary: Subject to any preferred stock, [[Class A and Class N holders share in dividends|p1896]] that the board chooses to declare. Class T, Class F and Class E receive no dividends.

children.title: No Preemptive or Similar Rights
children.tldr: Common stock carries no preemptive rights and no sinking fund, and the only redemptions are the no consideration redemptions of Classes T, F and E.
children.summary: No class of common stock has [[preemptive rights or sinking fund provisions|p1897]]. The only redemption features are the no consideration redemptions of Class T, Class F and Class E described earlier.

children.title: Right to Receive Liquidation Distributions
children.tldr: In a liquidation, Class A and Class N share the remaining assets ratably, while Classes T, F and E receive only $0.00001 par value per share.
children.summary: After debts and any preferences are paid, liquidation proceeds go [[ratably to Class A, Class N|p1898]] and any participating preferred stock. Holders of Class T, Class F and Class E receive only par value of $0.00001 per share.

children.title: Fully Paid and Non-Assessable
children.tldr: Anthropic's counsel will opine that the Class A shares sold in the offering will be fully paid and non-assessable.
children.summary: The company's legal counsel will give an opinion that the Class A shares issued in the offering are [[fully paid and non-assessable|p1899]].

children.title: Sunset Provisions
children.tldr: LTBT control ends only when the Trust Amendment Threshold approves eliminating Class T, while founder control ends when Class F is redeemed or fewer than three founders remain.
children.summary: The Class T Sunset Time occurs only when Class T is redeemed or eliminated with the approval of the [[Trust Amendment Threshold|p1901]]. It never happens automatically through the passage of time, and once triggered it [[cannot be delayed or waived|p1904]]. The Class F Sunset Time comes when Class F is redeemed, or when the [[Class F Transition Period|p1900]] ends after fewer than three Continuing Founders remain for 90 days. A founder is removed on resignation, death, incapacity, or cause, or when holdings fall below [[2% of their offering date Class A stake|p1902]]. Successors admitted after a death or incapacity count toward the three founders [[until the tenth anniversary|p1906]]. Before the sunsets, the LTBT elects a board majority and Class F holds 50.1% of the vote. If only Class F remains, the Founder LLC [[controls all director elections|p1908]].

children.title: Preferred Stock
children.tldr: No preferred stock will be outstanding, but the board can issue it with 80% board approval and, before the Class F Sunset Time, the Founder LLC's consent.
children.summary: No preferred stock will be outstanding after the offering. With approval from [[80% of the authorized directors|p1909]], the board may issue preferred stock in series and set its terms without a stockholder vote. Before the Class F Sunset Time, however, it needs the Founder LLC's consent. Preferred shares with voting rights would dilute Class A voting power, while [[Class F stays fixed at 50.1%|p1909]]. Issuing preferred stock could also delay a change in control. The company has [[no current plan|p1909]] to issue any.

children.title: Options
children.tldr: Anthropic had options outstanding under its 2021 Plan to buy Class A shares as of September 30, 2026; the filing leaves the count and exercise price blank.
children.summary: As of September 30, 2026, there were [[options outstanding under the 2021 Plan|p1910]] to buy Class A shares. The filing leaves the share count and the weighted average exercise price blank.

children.title: RSUs
children.tldr: As of September 30, 2026, Class A shares were issuable on settlement of RSUs under the 2021 Plan; the filing leaves the number blank.
children.summary: As of September 30, 2026, Class A shares were [[issuable upon RSU vesting and settlement|p1911]] under the 2021 Plan. The filing leaves the number blank.

children.title: Registration Rights
children.tldr: Certain holders have registration rights under the IRA that expire within two years of the offering, and Google and Broadcom hold separate registration rights.
children.summary: Certain Class A holders, including holders of shares from converted Class N stock, have registration rights under the [[IRA|p1912]]. Google and Broadcom have separate agreements tied to their note purchase agreements. The IRA rights expire at the earliest of the [[second anniversary of the offering|p1912]], the point when a holder can sell all its shares under Rule 144 within three months, or termination of the IRA. Anthropic pays registration expenses other than underwriting fees, and lock-ups still apply. The rights cover [[demand registrations|s458]], [[piggyback registrations|s459]] and [[Form S-3 registrations|s460]], along with the separate rights of [[Google|s461]] and [[Broadcom|s462]].

children.title: Demand Registration Rights
children.tldr: Starting six months after the offering, holders of 60% of IRA registrable shares can demand up to two registrations of at least $200,000,000 each.
children.summary: Beginning [[six months after the offering|p1913]], holders of at least 60% of IRA registrable shares may request a registration. Each request must cover at least [[$200,000,000|p1913]] net of underwriting fees, and Anthropic must complete [[only two such registrations|p1913]]. The company may defer a registration for up to 120 days, no more than twice in 12 months, if it would be seriously detrimental. It is also not required to act around its own offerings, for example until 180 days after this offering.

children.title: Piggyback Registration Rights
children.tldr: IRA holders can add their shares to most future Anthropic registrations, and underwriter cutbacks cannot reduce them below 20% of the offering.
children.summary: When Anthropic registers Class A stock, IRA holders get notice and may [[include their shares|p1914]]. This does not apply to employee plan, Rule 145 or debt conversion registrations, and it is subject to the rights of Google and Broadcom. If underwriters cut back an offering, registrable shares cannot fall [[below 20% of the total|p1914]]. Co-founder shares are excluded if any other selling holder's shares are cut.

children.title: S-3 Registration Rights
children.tldr: Holders of 60% of IRA registrable shares can request unlimited Form S-3 registrations of at least $2,000,000, capped at two per 12 months.
children.summary: Once Anthropic is eligible for Form S-3, holders of 60% of IRA registrable shares may request registrations of at least [[$2,000,000|p1915]]. They may make unlimited requests, but Anthropic need not complete more than [[two in any 12 months|p1915]]. It may defer a registration once a year for up to 120 days, and it is not required to act within 180 days after a registration subject to piggyback rights.

children.title: Registration Rights of Google
children.tldr: Google can make one resale demand within a year of the offering, and Anthropic must register Google's quarterly share purchases on Form S-3 within 60 days.
children.summary: The Google RRA, signed in [[May 2026|p1916]] alongside the Google 2026 NPA, covers Google's shares that are not covered by the IRA. Google may make [[a single demand|p1916]] in the year after the registration statement takes effect. Once Anthropic is eligible for Form S-3, it must register shares from each quarterly closing [[within 60 days|p1916]]. Google's rights end on [[February 7, 2033|p1916]], or 12 months after the final quarterly closing if that comes earlier.

children.title: Registration Rights of Broadcom
children.tldr: Broadcom's June 2026 registration rights cover shares from future convertible notes, with one demand per $5.0 billion of notes, though no notes have been issued yet.
children.summary: The Infrastructure Partner RRA, signed in [[June 2026|p1917]], covers Class A shares from Class N stock issued when Broadcom's notes convert. Broadcom may assign the agreement to a financial partner with Anthropic's consent. Once Anthropic is eligible for Form S-3, it must file a shelf registration within 60 days. The holder gets [[one demand per $5.0 billion of notes|p1917]] with a $500,000,000 minimum and up to three underwritten offerings a year. Co-founder shares are cut first, and the holder has most favored treatment on later registration rights. The agreement ends nine months after the latest note maturity, and [[no notes have been issued|p1917]] so far.

children.title: Anti-Takeover Provisions
children.tldr: Delaware law and Anthropic's new charter and bylaws contain provisions that could delay or discourage a takeover and push would-be acquirers to negotiate with the board first.
children.summary: Anthropic says [[certain provisions of Delaware law|p1918]], its amended and restated certificate of incorporation and its bylaws may delay, defer or discourage someone from gaining control of the company. The company believes the benefit of being able to negotiate with an unsolicited bidder outweighs the cost of discouraging offers. The protections fall into two groups: [[Section 203 of the Delaware corporate law|s464]], which applies only later, and a set of [[charter and bylaw provisions|s465]] covering voting structure, board elections, meetings, amendments, preferred stock and court forum.

children.title: Delaware Law
children.tldr: Anthropic opts out of Delaware's Section 203 until the later of the Class F and Class T Sunset Times, after which its three-year limit on deals with 15% holders applies.
children.summary: Anthropic has [[elected not to be governed by Section 203|p1919]] until the later of the Class F Sunset Time and the Class T Sunset Time, after which it will be. Section 203 bars a business combination with an interested stockholder for three years unless [[the board approved it beforehand|p1920]], the holder reached [[at least 85% of voting stock|p1921]] in the transaction, or the board and [[two-thirds of the other outstanding voting stock|p1922]] approve it at a meeting. An [[interested stockholder|p1923]] generally owns 15% or more of the voting power.

children.title: Amended and Restated Certificate of Incorporation and Amended and Restated Bylaws Provisions
children.tldr: The new charter and bylaws include multi-class stock, board, meeting, amendment, preferred stock and forum provisions that could deter hostile takeovers or delay changes in control.
children.summary: Anthropic's charter and bylaws, effective just before the offering, contain [[provisions that could deter hostile takeovers|p1924]]. They include a [[multi-class stock structure|s466]] giving control to the LTBT and the Founder LLC, a future [[classified board|s467]], limits on [[filling board vacancies|s468]], [[advance notice rules|s469]], restrictions on who can call [[special meetings|s470]] and act by [[written consent|s472]], higher [[amendment thresholds|s473]] after the Class F Sunset Time, and authority to issue [[30,000,000,000 shares of preferred stock|s474]]. Exclusive forum rules also send most internal disputes to Delaware courts.

children.title: Multi-Class Common Stock
children.tldr: The LTBT and Founder LLC are expected to elect the whole board, and the Founder LLC to decide stockholder votes, leaving Class A holders generally unable to affect outcomes.
children.summary: Under the multi-class structure, the [[LTBT and the Founder LLC|p1925]] are expected to elect all directors, and the Founder LLC can decide every stockholder vote for the foreseeable future, including mergers or a sale of the company. Such deals also need board approval, and the LTBT elects a majority of the board. [[Class A holders generally cannot affect outcomes|p1925]] unless a majority of the Continuing Founders cannot agree, in which case Class F votes in proportion to Class A votes cast.

children.title: Classified Board
children.tldr: All directors are elected annually until the Class F Sunset Time, after which the board becomes classified into three staggered classes with three-year terms.
children.summary: Before the Class F Sunset Time, [[all directors will be elected for annual terms|p1926]]. After it, the board will [[shift to three classes of approximately equal size|p1927]] with staggered three-year terms, so only one class is elected each year. If Class T stock is still outstanding, Class T directors will be spread proportionately across the classes.

children.title: Board Vacancies
children.tldr: Vacancy rules and an 80% board approval requirement for board size before the Class T Sunset Time stop a stockholder from packing the board with its own nominees.
children.summary: Before the Class T Sunset Time, [[only the Class T holder can fill Class T director vacancies|p1928]]. Before the Class F Sunset Time, other vacancies can be filled by the board on the Founder LLC's written recommendation or by Class A and Class F holders voting together. Afterward, only the board fills them. Setting board size requires [[approval of 80% of authorized directors|p1928]] before the Class T Sunset Time, and the number must be odd until the earlier sunset. After the Class T Sunset Time, a majority suffices. The company says this [[prevents a stockholder from packing the board|p1928]].

children.title: Advance Notice Requirements for Stockholder Proposals and Director Nominations
children.tldr: Most stockholders must follow advance notice rules to raise business or nominate directors, and the NGC gets 30 days' notice of LTBT and Founder LLC nominations and removals.
children.summary: The bylaws set [[advance notice procedures|p1929]] for stockholders bringing business or director nominations, except Class T and Class F holders using their own nomination procedures. The nominating committee (NGC) also gets [[30 days' prior written notice|p1929]] of director nominations or removals by the LTBT or Founder LLC and of changes to LTBT Trustees, which it may waive. Anthropic expects these rules may discourage proxy contests by would-be acquirers.

children.title: Special Meetings of Stockholders
children.tldr: Only the board, its chair, the CEO, the President and, depending on timing, non-Class T directors, the secretary or the Founder LLC can call special stockholder meetings.
children.summary: Special meetings may be called only by [[the board, the chair, the CEO or the President|p1930]]. After the Class F Sunset Time, a majority of non-Class T directors may also call one. Before that time, the secretary may call one for Class E votes, and [[the Founder LLC|p1930]] may call one as the Class F holder.

children.title: No Cumulative Voting
children.tldr: Anthropic's charter does not allow cumulative voting in director elections.
children.summary: Delaware law denies cumulative voting unless the charter allows it, and Anthropic's charter [[does not provide for cumulative voting|p1931]].

children.title: Action by Written Consent
children.tldr: Written consent is limited to director matters, certain class protections and board-approved matters before the sunsets, and is eliminated once both the Class F and Class T Sunset Times occur.
children.summary: Before the sunsets, stockholders may act by written consent only for [[director nominations, elections and removals|p1932]], certain Class F, Class T and Class E protective provisions, and single-class matters the board first approves. After one sunset, only the remaining Class F or Class T holder may use written consent. [[After both sunsets|p1932]], all stockholder action must take place at a meeting. Class E holders can never act by written consent.

children.title: Amendment of Certificate of Incorporation and Bylaws Provisions
children.tldr: Certain charter and bylaw provisions can be amended by a Class A and Class F majority before the Class F Sunset Time, and by 66 2/3% of Class A afterward.
children.summary: Before the Class F Sunset Time, [[a majority of Class A and Class F voting power together|p1933]] can amend certain charter and bylaw provisions. After it, the threshold rises to [[66 2/3% of Class A voting power|p1933]].

children.title: Issuance of Undesignated Preferred Stock
children.tldr: With 80% board approval, Anthropic can issue up to 30,000,000,000 shares of preferred stock without stockholder action, though the Founder LLC must consent before the Class F Sunset Time.
children.summary: If [[80% of authorized directors approve|p1934]], the board can issue up to [[30,000,000,000 shares of undesignated preferred stock|p1934]] with rights it sets, without a stockholder vote. Before the Class F Sunset Time, it needs the [[Founder LLC's consent|p1934]]. Unissued preferred stock could be used to make a takeover harder.

children.title: Exclusive Forum
children.tldr: Most internal corporate disputes must go to the Delaware Court of Chancery, Securities Act claims to federal courts, and Exchange Act derivative suits to the District of Delaware.
children.summary: Unless Anthropic agrees otherwise, the [[Delaware Court of Chancery|p1935]] is the exclusive forum for derivative suits, fiduciary duty claims, Delaware corporate law claims, charter and bylaw disputes and internal affairs claims. [[Federal district courts|p1936]] are the exclusive forum for Securities Act claims, and the [[District of Delaware|p1936]] for Exchange Act derivative actions. Other Exchange Act claims may go to any competent federal court. Stockholders cannot waive compliance with federal securities laws.

children.title: Founder LLC Agreement
children.tldr: The seven co-founders' Founder LLC holds Class F stock and votes by majority of Continuing Founders; Class F and Class E are redeemed after a 450-day transition if founders dwindle.
children.summary: The co-founders will enter the [[Founder LLC Agreement|p1937]]. The Founder LLC holds the Class F stock and generally votes as [[a majority of the Continuing Founders|p1938]] decide, starting with all seven co-founders. Successors may be admitted until the tenth anniversary of the offering. If there are [[fewer than three Continuing Founders for 90 consecutive days|p1939]], a 450-day Class F Transition Period begins, after which Class F and Class E stock is redeemed for no consideration. A founder is removed on events including resignation, death, removal for cause, or [[holding less than 2% of their offering-date Class A shares|p1941]]. If founders cannot agree, Class F [[votes proportionately with Class A|p1942]]. Founders vote their own [[Class A shares freely|p1943]].

children.title: Class F Common Stock Voting Mechanics
children.tldr: Class F votes follow a Continuing Founder majority on general matters, but changes to Class F or LTBT rights need a Supermajority or Trust Amendment Supermajority or Class F votes against.
children.summary: On [[general stockholder matters|p1945]], Class F votes as a majority of Continuing Founders instruct, or proportionately with Class A if they abstain or disagree. Amendments to Class F rights need a [[Supermajority|p1946]], meaning all but one Continuing Founder, or unanimity if fewer than three. Otherwise Class F votes against. Amendments to LTBT or Class T rights need a [[Trust Amendment Supermajority|p1946]]: 66 2/3% of founders plus 75% of Class E votes cast and a Class A majority, or, until the third anniversary of the offering, unanimous founders plus Class E and Class A majorities. The Founder LLC will also support amendments approved by [[80% of directors and 80% of Trustees|p1946]].

children.title: Transfer Agent and Registrar
children.tldr: Computershare Trust Company, N.A. will be the transfer agent and registrar for the Class A common stock.
children.summary: Upon completion of the offering, [[Computershare Trust Company, N.A.|p1947]] of 150 Royall Street, Canton, MA 02021, will be the transfer agent and registrar for the Class A common stock.

children.title: Limitations of Liability and Indemnification
children.tldr: Liability limits and indemnification for officers and directors are described in the related person transactions section.
children.summary: This topic is covered in [[the section on related person transactions|p1948]], under limitation of liability and indemnification of officers and directors.

children.title: Listing
children.tldr: Anthropic has applied to list its Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol "ANT".
children.summary: Anthropic has [[applied to list its Class A common stock|p1949]] on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol "ANT".

children.title: Shares Eligible for Future Sale
children.tldr: Restricted shares held by existing holders reach the public market in staged releases, ending no later than 365 days after the prospectus date.
children.summary: Because of lock-up and market standoff agreements and Rules 144 and 701, Anthropic's restricted shares become sellable on a [[staggered schedule|p1950]]. Some shares held by non-founder directors, officers, employees and consultants can be sold on the [[first trading day after the prospectus|p1951]]. Further tranches follow at set intervals, many tied to earnings releases, including the [[FY26 Earnings Release Date|p1953]]. The 180-day lock-up fully ends at the earlier of the [[Q1 Earnings Release Date|p1958]] for the quarter ending March 31, 2027 or the 180th day. The extended 365-day lock-up fully ends at the earlier of the [[Q3 Earnings Release Date|p1965]] or the 365th day. Share counts and percentages are left blank in this draft. The section also covers [[lock-up terms|s482]], [[Class N stock|s483]], [[Rule 144|s484]], [[registration rights|s486]] and [[Form S-8 filings|s487]].

children.title: Lock-Up and Market Standoff Agreements
children.tldr: Directors, officers and most stockholders face lock-ups of about 180 days, while the seven co-founders and certain stockholders are locked up for about 365 days.
children.summary: All directors and officers and substantially all stockholders are bound by [[lock-up or market standoff agreements|p1966]]. Non-founder directors, officers and certain employees, plus certain stockholders, are restricted until the earlier of the second full trading day after the [[Q1 Earnings Release Date|p1967]] or the 180th day after the prospectus. Certain other stockholders and Anthropic's [[seven co-founders|p1970]] are restricted until the earlier of the second full trading day after the Q3 Earnings Release Date or the 365th day. These restrictions have [[timed automatic expirations|p1971]] and [[a number of exceptions|p1972]].

children.title: Class N Common Stock
children.tldr: Unlisted Class N shares convert to Class A on a qualifying transfer, and more Class N shares will come from preferred stock and note conversions, NPA draws and donation matching.
children.summary: Class N common stock is [[not listed or registered|p1974]] and converts automatically into Class A common stock on a qualifying transfer. After the offering, Class N will include shares from the [[Preferred Stock Conversion|p1976]] and from [[convertible promissory notes|p1977]] converted within ownership caps. Notes that could not convert because of the caps will [[convert at later intervals|p1978]]. More shares may come from new notes or [[NPA draws, donation matching and private placements|p1979]]. Some Class N holders also have [[registration rights|p1981]] that could make large block sales easier.

children.title: Rule 144
children.tldr: Under Rule 144, affiliates may sell up to the greater of 1% of outstanding shares or average weekly trading volume in any three months once lock-ups expire.
children.summary: Non-affiliates who have held shares for [[at least six months|p1982]] may sell them under Rule 144, subject only to the public information requirement, and face no conditions after one year. Affiliates may sell, within any three-month period, no more than the greater of [[1% of outstanding shares|p1984]] or the [[average weekly trading volume|p1985]] over the prior four weeks. They must also follow [[manner of sale and notice rules|p1986]].

children.title: Rule 701
children.tldr: Rule 701 lets holders of compensatory shares sell under Rule 144 with fewer conditions, but only starting 90 days after the prospectus date.
children.summary: Non-affiliates who received shares under a written compensatory plan may sell under Rule 144 [[without most of its conditions|p1987]], and affiliates may skip the holding period. All Rule 701 holders must wait [[90 days after the prospectus date|p1987]].

children.title: Registration Rights
children.tldr: Holders under the IRA and the Google RRA have registration rights that, once used, could let large numbers of shares be sold freely.
children.summary: Under the [[IRA and the Google RRA|p1988]], certain holders of Class A common stock can require registration of their shares. Once registered, those shares become [[freely tradable|p1988]], subject to Rule 144 limits for affiliates, and a large number could be sold.

children.title: Registration Statements on Form S-8
children.tldr: Anthropic will file Form S-8 registrations soon after the offering, making shares under its 2021 Plan, 2026 Plan and ESPP eligible for public sale.
children.summary: Anthropic plans to file [[Form S-8 registration statements|p1989]] covering shares under RSUs, options and reserves in its 2021 Plan, 2026 Plan and ESPP, plus resales of certain 2021 Plan shares. These take effect on filing, and the shares become [[eligible for sale|p1989]] subject to Rule 144, vesting and lock-ups.

children.title: Material U.S. Federal Income Tax Consequences to Non-U.S. Holders of Our Class A Common Stock
children.tldr: This section summarizes U.S. federal income tax rules for non-U.S. holders of Class A common stock, excludes many special categories of holders, and is not tax advice.
children.summary: The discussion covers the [[U.S. federal income tax consequences|p1990]] for non-U.S. holders who own and sell Class A common stock, based on law that may change retroactively. It leaves out state, local and foreign taxes and [[many special holders|p1991]], such as banks, dealers, [[holders of more than 5%|p1999]] and [[partnerships|p2007]]. It is [[not tax advice|p2008]]. The subsections define a [[non-U.S. holder|s489]] and cover [[distributions|s490]], [[gains on sale|s491]], [[backup withholding|s492]] and [[FATCA|s493]].

children.title: Non-U.S. Holder Defined
children.tldr: A non-U.S. holder is a beneficial owner that is not a partnership and not a U.S. citizen or resident, U.S. corporation, U.S.-taxed estate or qualifying trust.
children.summary: A non-U.S. holder is a beneficial owner that is not a [[pass-through entity|p2009]] and is not a [[U.S. citizen or resident|p2010]], a [[U.S. corporation|p2011]], an estate taxed on all income, or a [[trust under U.S. control|p2013]].

children.title: Distributions
children.tldr: Dividends paid to non-U.S. holders generally face 30% U.S. withholding unless a treaty lowers the rate or the income is effectively connected to a U.S. business.
children.summary: Distributions count as dividends to the extent of earnings and profits, and any excess is a [[return of capital|p2014]] and then gain. Dividends generally face [[30% withholding|p2015]] unless a treaty sets a lower rate, which requires an [[IRS Form W-8BEN or W-8BEN-E|p2016]]. Dividends [[effectively connected with a U.S. business|p2017]] avoid withholding with Form W-8ECI but are taxed at regular rates, and corporations may owe a 30% branch profits tax.

children.title: Gain on Disposition of Our Class A Common Stock
children.tldr: Non-U.S. holders generally owe no U.S. tax on gains from selling the stock, except for U.S. business income, 183-day presence, or USRPHC status, which Anthropic says it lacks.
children.summary: Gains on sale are generally not taxed unless they are [[effectively connected with a U.S. business|p2019]], the seller is an individual present [[183 days or more|p2020]] in the year, or the company is a [[United States real property holding corporation|p2021]]. Anthropic [[believes it is not and will not become|p2022]] a USRPHC. Effectively connected gains are taxed at graduated rates, and 183-day gains at [[30%|p2023]] unless a treaty lowers it.

children.title: Backup Withholding and Information Reporting
children.tldr: Dividends and sale proceeds may face information reporting and 24% backup withholding unless the holder certifies non-U.S. status; backup withholding is creditable, not an extra tax.
children.summary: Anthropic must [[report dividends annually|p2024]] to the IRS. Payments may face [[backup withholding at 24%|p2025]] unless the holder certifies non-U.S. status on Form W-8. Sales through a [[U.S. broker office|p2026]] are generally subject to these rules, while sales abroad through a foreign broker usually are not. Backup withholding [[is not an additional tax|p2027]] and can be refunded or credited.

children.title: FATCA
children.tldr: FATCA imposes 30% withholding on dividends paid to noncompliant foreign financial institutions and non-financial foreign entities, but proposed rules exempt sale proceeds.
children.summary: FATCA generally imposes [[30% withholding|p2028]] on dividends paid to foreign financial institutions and non-financial foreign entities that do not meet reporting or certification requirements. [[Proposed regulations|p2028]] remove withholding on gross sale proceeds. Investors should [[consult their own tax advisors|p2029]].

children.title: Underwriting
children.tldr: Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley lead 22 underwriters who will buy the Class A shares, with a 30-day option to buy more; Class A will list on Nasdaq as "ANT."
children.summary: Anthropic, the selling stockholders and the underwriters will sign an underwriting agreement, with [[Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC and Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC|p2030]] acting as representatives of a group of [[22 underwriters|p2032]]. The underwriters must take and pay for all offered shares if any are taken. They also get a [[30-day option to buy additional shares|p2034]] to cover over-allotments. Share counts and [[underwriting discounts|s495]] are still blank. Directors, officers and most holders face [[lock-ups of 180 days|s497]], while founders and some large holders face up to 365 days, with staged early releases. Class A stock is to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market as "ANT." Several underwriters' affiliates are [[lenders and arrangers|s498]] under Anthropic's credit agreement. The offering also includes [[public offerings abroad|s499]], in Australia, Canada, parts of the European Economic Area, Japan, Switzerland and the United Kingdom, and is subject to [[country-specific selling restrictions|s500]].

children.title: Paid by us
children.tldr: A table for the underwriting discounts and commissions Anthropic will pay, per share and in total, with and without full exercise of the underwriters' option; amounts are blank.
children.summary: This is a placeholder table showing the underwriting discounts and commissions Anthropic will pay per share and in total, under [[no exercise and full exercise|p2036]] of the underwriters' option. The dollar amounts have not yet been filled in.

children.title: Paid by the selling stockholders
children.tldr: Selling stockholders also pay underwriting discounts, amounts still blank, and underwriters will offer Class A shares at the cover price but may later change it.
children.summary: A blank table shows the [[per share and total|p2038]] underwriting discounts the selling stockholders will pay, with and without full exercise of the underwriters' option. Underwriters will first offer Class A shares to the public at the [[initial public offering price|p2039]] on the prospectus cover. They may sell to dealers at a discount not yet specified, may change the price and selling terms after the initial offering, and may reject any order in whole or in part.

children.title: Lock-Up and Market Standoff Agreements
children.tldr: Most holders face lock-ups of up to 180 days, some large holders and the founders up to 365 days, with staged early releases; Class A will list on Nasdaq as "ANT."
children.summary: Directors, officers and holders of substantially all of Anthropic's stock signed [[180-day market standoff agreements|p2040]]. Anthropic itself agreed not to issue or register stock until the earlier of its [[Q1 2027 earnings release or the 180th day|p2041]], with broad exceptions such as equity plans and acquisitions. Non-founder directors, officers and some employees may sell [[10% at trading start and 35% more|p2051]] after the FY26 earnings release. Certain holders above 0.5% are locked up until the earlier of the Q3 2027 earnings release or [[365 days|p2058]], with many small staged releases. Founders may sell [[up to 29%|p2067]] after the Q1 2027 release or day 180, with the rest locked for up to 365 days. Class A stock is to list on the [[Nasdaq Global Select Market as "ANT"|p2073]], and [[Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC|p2075]] may act as stabilization agent to support the price.

children.title: Other Relationships
children.tldr: Underwriters and their affiliates provide Anthropic other financial services, including roles as lenders and arrangers under its A&R Credit Agreement, and may trade its securities.
children.summary: The underwriters are full service financial firms that have provided, and may provide, services to Anthropic and its insiders for customary fees, and some are Anthropic customers. Affiliates of Morgan Stanley, Barclays, Citigroup, Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan, Wells Fargo and others hold arranger and agent roles under Anthropic's [[A&R Credit Agreement|p2081]]. [[Bernstein Institutional Services LLC|p2082]] acts as selling agent for SG Americas Securities, LLC. The underwriters may also [[trade and hold positions|p2083]] in Anthropic's securities and publish independent research on them.

children.title: Offerings Outside the United States
children.tldr: The offering includes public offerings in Australia, Canada, parts of the EEA, Japan, Switzerland and the UK, without listing there; dropped jurisdictions' shares would be reallocated.
children.summary: The offering includes [[public offerings in six international markets|p2084]], Australia, Canada, certain European Economic Area states, Japan, Switzerland and the United Kingdom, but Anthropic does not plan to list its shares on exchanges there. If any international offering is ended early, its shares would move to the other jurisdictions, so total size should not change. Shares may be sold elsewhere only through [[duly registered brokers or dealers|p2085]] or under an exemption, and the prospectus is [[not an offer where unlawful|p2086]].

children.title: Selling Restrictions
children.tldr: Outside the United States, the Class A shares can generally be sold only to professional or otherwise exempt investors, with separate retail offerings in Australia, parts of Europe and Switzerland.
children.summary: Barclays Bank PLC is not registered with the SEC, so any of its U.S. sales will go through its affiliate [[Barclays Capital Inc.|p2087]]. The section then sets out offering rules for each country. In most jurisdictions, such as [[Brazil|s503]], [[Singapore|s518]] and [[Malaysia|s511]], the shares are not registered with local regulators and may be offered only privately or to professional, qualified or wealthy investors. Separate public offerings are planned under their own prospectuses in [[Australia|s502]], in certain [[European Economic Area|s507]] countries, and in [[Switzerland|s521]]. In the [[United Kingdom|s525]], no local prospectus will be published, and the offering is directed only at defined Relevant Persons.

children.title: Argentina
children.tldr: The shares are not authorized for public offering in Argentina, so any Argentine transaction must be private.
children.summary: The Comisión Nacional de Valores has not authorized the shares for public offering under [[Law No. 17,811|p2088]]. Any sale in Argentina must therefore be [[made privately|p2088]].

children.title: Australia
children.tldr: Australian offers under this prospectus are limited to sophisticated and professional investors, while a separate Australian Prospectus covers the public offering.
children.summary: This document is not a disclosure document under the [[Corporations Act 2001|p2089]]. Offers made under it in Australia are limited to [[sophisticated or professional investors|p2090]] and others covered by section 708 exemptions. These buyers generally may not resell the shares in Australia for [[12 months after allotment|p2091]] unless an exemption applies. Other investors must apply through a [[separate Australian Prospectus|p2092]] lodged with the Australian Securities and Investments Commission. The document is [[general information only|p2093]] and does not give financial product advice.

children.title: Brazil
children.tldr: In Brazil, only Professional Investors may buy, through non-Brazilian accounts with settlement abroad, and trading on Brazilian regulated markets is prohibited.
children.summary: The offering is [[not registered with the CVM|p2094]] and will not be made as a public offering in Brazil. Only [[Brazilian Professional Investors|p2094]] may buy the shares, using a non-Brazilian account with settlement outside Brazil in foreign currency. [[Trading on Brazilian regulated markets|p2094]] is prohibited.

children.title: Chile
children.tldr: The shares are not registered in Chile and are offered there only privately to individually identified purchasers.
children.summary: The shares are [[not registered in the Securities Registry|p2095]] or supervised by the Chilean regulator. In Chile they are offered only to [[individually identified purchasers|p2095]] in a private offering under Article 4 of the Securities Market Act.

children.title: Colombia
children.tldr: The shares cannot be publicly offered in Colombia but may be privately placed with fewer than 100 specific persons.
children.summary: The shares are [[not registered with the RNVE|p2096]], so they cannot be publicly offered in Colombia. A private placement is allowed if it is addressed to [[fewer than 100 specific persons|p2096]] under Decree 2555 of 2010. The SFC has not reviewed the materials, and investors must rely on their own examination of the offering's merits and risks.

children.title: Dubai
children.tldr: In Dubai, this is an Exempt Offer under DFSA rules, open only to specified investor types; the DFSA has not reviewed or approved the prospectus.
children.summary: The prospectus covers an [[Exempt Offer|p2097]] under the Dubai Financial Services Authority's Offered Securities Rules and is meant only for the investor types those rules specify. The DFSA has [[not approved or verified|p2097]] the document. The shares [[may be illiquid|p2097]] or restricted on resale, and buyers should do their own due diligence.

children.title: European Economic Area
children.tldr: A separate European prospectus will support a retail offering in certain EEA countries; elsewhere in the EEA, shares go only to qualified investors or under other exemptions.
children.summary: Anthropic will offer shares to retail investors in certain Covered EEA Countries under a [[separate European prospectus|p2098]]. Outside that retail offering, shares may be offered in EEA states only to [[qualified investors|p2100]], to [[fewer than 150 persons|p2101]] other than qualified investors with the underwriters' consent, or under [[other Article 1(4) exemptions|p2102]] that do not require a prospectus. Financial intermediaries are deemed to represent that they are [[not buying for public resale|p2103]]. The section also defines an [[offer to the public|p2104]] and the Prospectus Regulation.

children.title: India
children.tldr: The prospectus is not registered or reviewed in India, and shares may be sold there only through private placements under Indian law.
children.summary: No Indian regulator, including the Securities and Exchange Board of India, has [[registered or reviewed|p2105]] the prospectus. Shares will not be offered to the Indian public except under [[private placement exemptions|p2105]], including those in the Companies Act, 2013. Each investor is deemed to represent that it is [[eligible to invest|p2105]] without prior approval.

children.title: Indonesia
children.tldr: The prospectus may not be distributed in Indonesia, and shares may not be publicly offered to Indonesian citizens or residents.
children.summary: The prospectus is [[not a public offering|p2106]] under Indonesia's Law Number 8 of 1995. It may not be distributed in Indonesia, and the shares may not be offered to [[Indonesian citizens or residents|p2106]] in a way that amounts to a public offering.

children.title: Israel
children.tldr: In Israel, the offer goes only to Qualified Investors and up to 35 Addressed Investors, so no Israeli prospectus is required.
children.summary: Anthropic will offer shares in Israel only to [[Qualified Investors and up to 35 Addressed Investors|p2107]], which avoids the need for a prospectus under the Israeli Securities Law. Qualified Investors may have to [[certify their status|p2108]] and confirm they are buying for investment. Addressed Investors may have to provide [[identity details|p2108]] such as a passport or Israeli ID number.

children.title: Malaysia
children.tldr: The shares are not registered in Malaysia and may be sold only to listed categories of institutional and high net worth investors through licensed dealers.
children.summary: No offering document is registered with the [[Securities Commission of Malaysia|p2109]]. Shares may be offered only to specified investors, such as buyers paying at least RM250,000 per transaction, individuals with net assets above RM3 million or annual income above RM300,000, and corporations with net assets above RM10 million. Any such distribution must be made by a [[Capital Markets Services License holder|p2109]] that deals in securities.

children.title: Mexico
children.tldr: The shares are not registered in Mexico and may be sold there only privately to institutional or qualified investors.
children.summary: The shares are [[not registered with the RNV|p2110]] and cannot be publicly offered in Mexico. They may be sold only to [[institutional or qualified investors|p2110]] under the private placement exemption in Article 8 of the Securities Market Law. The CNBV has not reviewed the prospectus.

children.title: New Zealand
children.tldr: In New Zealand, shares may be offered only to investment businesses, experienced, large or eligible investors, and government agencies.
children.summary: No New Zealand regulator has registered the document under the [[FMC Act 2013|p2111]]. Shares may be offered only to [[investment businesses|p2112]], persons meeting the [[investment activity criteria|p2113]], [[large|p2114]] persons, [[government agencies|p2115]] and [[eligible investors|p2116]] as defined in Schedule 1.

children.title: Peru
children.tldr: The shares are not registered with Peru's SMV and may be sold in Peru only through qualifying private offerings.
children.summary: The shares are [[not publicly marketed|p2117]] in Peru, and Peruvian public offering disclosure rules do not apply. They have not been registered with or reviewed by the [[SMV|p2117]] and may be sold in Peru only in a qualifying [[private offering|p2117]].

children.title: Philippines
children.tldr: The shares are not registered in the Philippines and may be sold only to qualified investors in exempt transactions by licensed persons.
children.summary: The shares are [[not registered|p2118]] with the Philippine Securities and Exchange Commission under the SRC. Offers in the Philippines are limited to [[qualified investors|p2119]] in exempt transactions, made by persons licensed to sell there.

children.title: Qatar
children.tldr: In Qatar, the offer is made only to specific recipients at their own request, and no Qatari regulator has approved it.
children.summary: The offer in Qatar is made [[exclusively to the intended recipient|p2120]], at that person's request and for personal use only. It is not a general public offer. Neither the [[Qatar Central Bank|p2120]] nor the Qatar Financial Center Regulatory Authority has approved the prospectus, and recipients may share it only on a need to know basis.

children.title: Saudi Arabia
children.tldr: The prospectus may be distributed in Saudi Arabia only to persons permitted under CMA rules, and the CMA disclaims any liability.
children.summary: Distribution in Saudi Arabia is limited to persons permitted under the CMA's rules adopted by [[resolution 3-123-2017|p2121]] dated 27 December 2017. The CMA [[disclaims liability|p2121]] for the prospectus, and buyers should do their own due diligence.

children.title: Singapore
children.tldr: In Singapore, shares may be offered only to institutional investors and accredited investors under the Securities and Futures Act.
children.summary: The prospectus is [[not registered with the Monetary Authority of Singapore|p2122]]. Shares may be offered only to institutional investors under Section 274 or [[accredited investors|p2122]] under Section 275 of the Securities and Futures Act 2001.

children.title: South Africa
children.tldr: No public offer is made in South Africa; shares go only to financial institutions or buyers acquiring at least ZAR 1,000,000 each.
children.summary: No [[offer to the public|p2123]] is made in South Africa, and the document is not a registered prospectus. Shares may be offered there only to exempt parties such as [[securities dealers|p2125]], the [[Public Investment Corporation|p2126]] and [[authorized financial service providers|p2128]], or to a single principal buyer with an acquisition cost of at least [[ZAR 1,000,000|p2132]]. The information is [[not financial advice|p2133]] under South African law.

children.title: South Korea
children.tldr: The shares are not registered in Korea and are offered there only as a private placement, with buyers required to follow Korean law.
children.summary: The shares are [[not registered under the FSCMA|p2134]] and are offered in Korea only as a private placement. Buyers must comply with Korean rules, including the [[Foreign Exchange Transaction Law|p2134]], and Korean buyers are deemed to represent that they purchased lawfully.

children.title: Switzerland
children.tldr: Swiss public offering occurs only under the BaFin-approved European prospectus; otherwise shares go to professional clients, and they will not list in Switzerland.
children.summary: The only Swiss public offering is the one made under the [[European prospectus approved by BaFin|p2135]] and filed under Article 54(2) of FinSA. The Class A stock will not be listed on a Swiss trading venue. Otherwise, shares may be offered only to [[professional clients|p2136]]. This document is [[not a FinSA prospectus|p2137]] and may not be publicly distributed in Switzerland.

children.title: Taiwan
children.tldr: The shares are not registered in Taiwan and cannot be publicly offered there, and no one in Taiwan is authorized to intermediate the sale.
