p1529: In addition, our Class T common stock may be redeemed by us for no consideration upon approval of persons comprising the above thresholds for amendments of the terms of the LTBT or the rights of our Class T common stock.
p1530: The LTBT is governed by five Trustees. The Trustees have the authority to appoint the Trustees by majority vote of the Trustees then in office and to remove the Trustees by majority vote of the total number of authorized Trustees or by the unanimous approval of the other Trustees then in office and the approval of the NGC, provided that the LTBT must provide at least 30 days’ prior written notice to our NGC before effecting any such appointment or removal. The notice period is waivable by our NGC in its discretion. Trustees may also be removed by order of the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware upon petition by a person designated by the Trust Agreement as having the power to enforce the agreement if a Trustee has engaged in disqualifying conduct and removal would best serve the purpose of the LTBT. Trustees will serve annual terms, and there is no limit to the number of terms a Trustee may serve. Trustees are selected based on their expertise in areas relevant to the LTBT’s purpose, including AI safety, national security, public policy, social enterprise, and related fields. In practice to date, the Trustees and company executives have collaborated closely on sourcing, interviewing, and selecting Trustees. Of the five authorized seats for Trustees, one is currently vacant.
p1531: Dr. Neil “Buddy” Shah has served as a Trustee and Chair of the LTBT since June 2023. Dr. Shah will also serve as an initial manager of the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund. Dr. Shah has served as Chief Executive Officer of the Clinton Health Access Initiative (“CHAI”), a global health organization focused on improving access to health services in low- and middle-income countries, since June 2022. Prior to joining CHAI, Dr. Shah served as Managing Director of GiveWell, a nonprofit organization focused on directing charitable capital to cost-effective global health and development programs, and, before that, as co-founder and Chief Executive Officer of IDinsight, a global advisory, data analytics, and research organization. He holds an A.B. in Economics from Harvard University, an M.D. with an emphasis in global health policy from Albert Einstein College of Medicine, and an M.P.A. in International Development from Harvard Kennedy School of Government.
p1532: Dr. Shah was selected to serve as a Trustee because of his expertise in global health, impact measurement, and social enterprise, and his experience evaluating the long-term societal effects of large-scale programs.
p1533: Richard Fontaine has served as a Trustee since April 2025. Mr. Fontaine has served as Chief Executive Officer of the Center for a New American Security (“CNAS”), a bipartisan national security research institution, since February 2019, having previously served as President of CNAS from 2012 to 2019 and as Senior Fellow from 2009 to 2012. Mr. Fontaine serves concurrently as Executive Director of the Trilateral Commission’s North America group, a position he has held since July 2019. Prior to joining CNAS and the Trilateral Commission, Mr. Fontaine served as foreign policy advisor to Senator John McCain, including as advisor to the McCain 2008 presidential campaign and subsequently as Minority Deputy Staff Director of the Senate Armed Services Committee. He has also served as Associate Director for Near Eastern Affairs at the National Security Council, and he has held positions at the U.S. Department of State and on the staff of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee. Mr. Fontaine holds a B.A. in International Relations from Tulane University and an M.A. in International Affairs from the Johns Hopkins School of Advanced International Studies.
p1534: Mr. Fontaine was selected to serve as a Trustee because of his extensive background in foreign policy and national security, and he will address the growing intersection between AI capabilities and geopolitical risks.
p1535: Dr. Ben S. Bernanke has served as a Trustee since June 2026. Since 2014, Dr. Bernanke has been a Distinguished Fellow in Economic Studies at the Brookings Institution, a public policy research organization. Dr. Bernanke served as Chairman of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System from February 2006 to January 2014, having been appointed to that position by Presidents George W. Bush and Barack Obama. Prior to serving as Federal Reserve Chairman, Dr. Bernanke served as chairman of the President’s Council of Economic Advisers and as a member of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. Before his government service, Dr. Bernanke was a professor of economics and public affairs at Princeton University, where he also chaired the Economics Department. Subsequent to his government service, Dr. Bernanke served as chair of the Global Advisory Board of and senior advisor to Pacific Investment Management Company, a global fixed income investment management firm. Dr. Bernanke holds an A.B. in Economics from Harvard University and a Ph.D. in Economics from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. Dr. Bernanke was awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics in 2022.
p1536: Dr. Bernanke was selected to serve as a Trustee because of his expertise in macroeconomics, financial systems, and institutional governance, and his experience overseeing large, consequential institutions during periods of systemic risk and uncertainty.
p1537: Dr. Christopher Stubbs has served as a Trustee since October 2026. Dr. Stubbs is the Samuel C. Moncher Professor of Physics and of Astronomy at Harvard University, where he has been a member of the faculty since 2003. At Harvard, he served as Senior Advisor for AI to the Faculty of Arts and Sciences from 2024 to 2026, as Dean of Science in the Faculty of Arts and Sciences from 2018 to 2024, and as Chair of the Department of Physics from 2007 to 2010. Prior to joining Harvard, he held faculty positions at the University of California, Santa Barbara and the University of Washington. As a member of the High-Z Supernova Search Team, Dr. Stubbs shared in the discovery of the accelerating expansion of the universe, work for which he and his colleagues received the Gruber Prize in Cosmology and the Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics. He also served as the inaugural project scientist of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory. Dr. Stubbs is a member of JASON, an independent group of scientists that advises the U.S. government on matters of national security. He holds a B.Sc. in physics from the University of Virginia and a Ph.D. in physics from the University of Washington.
p1538: Dr. Stubbs was selected to serve as a Trustee because of his expertise in experimental physics and the application of AI to science and education, and his experience leading scientific projects across academia, government, and the national laboratories.
p1539: We provide funding to the LTBT, which holds all of our Class T common stock, to support its operations and the compensation of its Trustees. In the years ended December 31, 2023, 2024, and 2025, we paid $2,716,750, $0, and $906,089, respectively, to the LTBT. During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, we paid $8,425,213 to the LTBT. The LTBT is accounted for as a consolidated variable interest entity (“VIE”) on our balance sheet (see Note 1 to our consolidated financial statements included elsewhere in this prospectus).
p1540: The Trust Agreement limits Trustee compensation to a reasonable cash amount fixed annually by the Trustees. Each Trustee receives annual cash compensation of $400,000 for their service as a Trustee. In addition, Dr.
p1541: Shah receives annual cash compensation of $25,000 for his service as the Chair of the LTBT. Trustee compensation will not vary with or be conditioned upon the profits or any action or inaction of our company. The policies of the LTBT prohibit a Trustee from directly purchasing or holding any of our securities.
p1542: In addition, in August 2026, we made a $450,000 charitable donation to CNAS, of which Mr. Fontaine is the Chief Executive Officer. The donation will be used to support CNAS research examining how AI is reshaping global competition, national security, international security, democratic governance, and other issues related to emerging technology and security.
p1543: We believe that our seven co-founders, Dario Amodei, Daniela Amodei, Tom Brown, Jack Clark, Jared Kaplan, Sam McCandlish, and Christopher Olah, as a group, are distinctly equipped to be stewards of our mission. Our co-founders have been instrumental in building our leadership position and establishing the mission-driven values that define our company. In addition, Dr. Amodei serves as our Chief Executive Officer and a member of our board of directors and Ms. Amodei serves as our President and Chairperson of our board of directors. Their long-term strategic vision has been critical to our success and will continue to guide our future. In our highly competitive industry, success requires visionary leadership, strong direction, and the kind of decisiveness necessary to make bold investments, pursue transformative opportunities, and compete effectively against formidable competitors, while also balancing the pecuniary interests of our stockholders with the Company Purpose and the best interests of those materially affected by our conduct.
p1544: We believe that our success depends in part on establishing a capital structure that enables our co-founders, management, and board of directors to focus on strategic initiatives that create lasting value for our stakeholders, rather than facing pressure to prioritize short-term results or purely pecuniary objectives at the expense of our long-term vision and mission. Immediately prior to the completion of this offering, we will issue a single share of Class F common stock, a special class of our common stock, to the Founder LLC, a limited liability company of which our seven co-founders will initially be the sole members and that will be managed by its members. Our Class F common stock will be entitled to an aggregate number of votes that equals 50.1% of the total voting power of our outstanding shares of capital stock as of the applicable record date with respect to matters submitted to stockholders generally, including the election of our directors other than the Class T directors.
p1545: Our Class F common stock will be voted by the Founder LLC in a manner determined in accordance with the Founder LLC Agreement. Generally, the Founder LLC will vote as determined by a majority of the members of the Founder LLC entitled to vote thereunder. Our seven co-founders will initially be the sole members. Upon the incapacity or death of any of our co-founders, a successor member may be admitted to the Founder LLC until the tenth anniversary of the completion of this offering. We refer to our seven co-founders and any successors in the Founder LLC as “Continuing Founders.”
p1546: When there have been fewer than three Continuing Founders (not including any successor member who is a “Non-Qualifying Member” as defined in the Founder LLC Agreement) for 90 consecutive calendar days, a 450- day transition period will commence (the “Class F Transition Period”). Upon completion of the Class F Transition Period, all of our Class F common stock and Class E common stock then issued and outstanding will be redeemed by us for no consideration and certain other governance changes will take effect.
p1547: Regardless of the length of time that has elapsed since the completion of this offering or the circumstances that resulted in the removal of a Continuing Founder, one or more successor members may be admitted to the Founder LLC during the Class F Transition Period as needed to ensure that there are three Continuing Founders serving until completion of the Class F Transition Period. The admission of any successor member during the Class F Transition Period will not cure the event that commenced the Class F Transition Period or extend the Class F Transition Period. For additional information, see the section titled “Description of Capital Stock.”
p1548: A Continuing Founder will be removed from the Founder LLC upon the earliest to occur of (i) such Continuing Founder’s resignation as a member of the Founder LLC; (ii) such Continuing Founder’s death or incapacity; (iii) with respect to each of our seven original co-founders, such original co-founder’s ceasing to hold (together with such original co-founder’s related holders) on any record date for a vote of our stockholders a number of shares of Class A common stock (including shares subject to options, RSUs, and other convertible securities) equal to at least 2% of the shares of Class A common stock held by such original co-founder and their related holders as of the completion of this offering; (iv) such Continuing Founder’s removal for “cause” (as defined in the Founder LLC Agreement), which includes specified competitive activities described in the Founder LLC Agreement; (v) with respect to any successor member admitted to the Founder LLC prior to the commencement of the Class F Transition Period, other than a successor member who is a member during the Class F Transition Period, the tenth anniversary of the completion of this offering; or (vi) with respect to each of our seven original co-founders, the commencement of a leave of absence approved by a Supermajority of the other Continuing Founders, which may not be approved during the Class F Transition Period or if the grant of the leave of absence would itself cause the Class F Transition Period to commence.
p1549: Each Continuing Founder will be entitled to one vote when determining how our Class F common stock will be voted. If a majority of the Continuing Founders cannot agree on how our Class F common stock will be voted, then our Class F common stock will generally be voted proportionately with the votes of our Class A common stock cast on the matter (subject to a quorum of a majority of outstanding Class A common stock). With respect to certain matters, our Class F common stock will be voted “for” the proposal only if a greater threshold of Continuing Founders agree, and if the greater threshold is not met, our Class F common stock will be voted “against” the proposal. See the section titled “Description of Capital Stock—Class F Common Stock Voting Mechanics.”
p1550: The Founder LLC Agreement will not govern the voting of any shares of our Class A common stock held by the co-founders or their related holders. Each co-founder (or their related holders) will be able to vote shares of our Class A common stock held by them in their discretion, regardless of the manner in which the Founder LLC will vote our Class F common stock.
p1551: The voting power of our Class F common stock will not be impacted by future issuances of our capital stock that may cause economic or voting dilution to stockholders, such as issuances for capital raising purposes, acquisitions, or employee compensation. This structure will allow the Founder LLC to determine the outcome of matters submitted to a vote of our stockholders generally, including the election of those directors not elected by the LTBT, certain amendments to our organizational documents, and the approval by our stockholders of any merger, consolidation, sale of substantially all our assets, or other major corporate transaction requiring stockholder approval.
p1552: Our seven co-founders co-founded Anthropic in January 2021. Each co-founder will initially be a member of the Founder LLC and a Continuing Founder for purposes of the Class F common stock structure described 13 above. Brief biographical information about each co-founder is set forth below.
p1553: Dario Amodei has served as our Chief Executive Officer and a member of our board of directors since cofounding Anthropic in January 2021. See “Management—Executive Officers” for Dr. Amodei’s full biographical information.
p1554: Daniela Amodei has served as our President and a member of our board of directors since co-founding Anthropic in January 2021. Ms. Amodei also currently serves as the Chairperson of our board of directors. See “Management—Executive Officers” for Ms. Amodei’s full biographical information.
p1555: Tom Brown co-founded Anthropic in January 2021 and serves as our Chief Compute Officer, leading the technical organization responsible for securing, scaling, and effectively using our compute resources. Prior to co-founding Anthropic, Mr. Brown led the engineering of GPT-3 at OpenAI and, along with Dario Amodei, coinvented deep RLHF, which was central to converting base LLMs into modern conversational assistants such as Claude. He holds an M.Eng. in Computer Science from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.
p1556: 13 Benjamin Mann has been an integral part of Anthropic since its founding in January 2021 and, given his role in establishing Anthropic, is often referred to as a co-founder. However, Mr. Mann is not a member of the Founder LLC nor a Continuing Founder upon the completion of this offering, and accordingly will not participate in determining how our Class F common stock is voted. Except as set forth in this paragraph, references to our “co-founders” elsewhere in this prospectus do not include Mr. Mann.
p1557: Jack Clark co-founded Anthropic in January 2021 and leads the Anthropic Institute, an effort to share research from across Anthropic with external partners and the public, working together to address the biggest questions posed by powerful AI systems. Prior to co-founding Anthropic, Mr. Clark served as Policy Director at OpenAI, where he was responsible for OpenAI’s engagement with governments and regulators on questions related to AI development. Before joining OpenAI, Mr. Clark was a technology journalist covering supercomputers, neural networks, and advanced technology, writing for publications including The Register and BusinessWeek. Mr. Clark also authors “Import AI,” a widely read newsletter on AI research developments.
p1558: Jared Kaplan co-founded Anthropic in January 2021 and serves as our Chief Science Officer. Dr. Kaplan is a theoretical physicist and AI researcher and is one of the principal authors of the neural scaling laws that have shaped modern LLM development, which identify power-law relationships governing the performance of AI systems as a function of model size, dataset size, and compute; he also helped pioneer Constitutional AI. Prior to co-founding Anthropic, Dr. Kaplan was a researcher at OpenAI and an associate professor of physics at Johns Hopkins University, where he taught courses on the foundations of deep learning. He holds a Ph.D. in Physics from Harvard University and a bachelor’s degree in Physics and Mathematics from Stanford University.
p1559: Sam McCandlish co-founded Anthropic in January 2021 and serves as our Chief Architect. Dr. McCandlish is a theoretical physicist and machine learning researcher specializing in large-scale model training and AI systems architecture. Prior to co-founding Anthropic, Dr. McCandlish made significant contributions to AI safety research at OpenAI, where he built and led a team focused on the science and scaling of machine learning; his work on scaling laws helped pave the way for large-scale advancements in AI, including the development of GPT-3. He holds a Ph.D. in Physics from Stanford University and a bachelor’s degree in Mathematics and Physics from Brandeis University.
p1560: Christopher Olah co-founded Anthropic in January 2021 and leads our interpretability research efforts. Prior to co-founding Anthropic, Mr. Olah led interpretability research at OpenAI and, before that, was a research scientist at Google Brain (now part of Google DeepMind). Mr. Olah is widely recognized as a foundational figure in the field of mechanistic interpretability. More broadly, his work has been widely cited across a range of topics in AI.
p1561: We founded Anthropic on the belief that the most transformative technology in human history demands an extraordinary level of responsibility, and that responsibility extends far beyond building safe systems. We intend to direct a meaningful portion of our resources toward ensuring that frontier AI is safe and its benefits are broadly distributed, which we refer to as our public benefit initiatives. These initiatives include the Initial Public Benefit Issuance and the future Public Benefit Issuances. In addition, our co-founders have each pledged to dedicate 80% of their personal equity in Anthropic to philanthropic causes. For additional information regarding these pledges, including related risks, see the section titled “Risk Factors—Risks Related to Ownership of our Class A Common Stock.” Separate from the co-founders’ pledges, we also maintain a donation matching program through which employees can pledge a meaningful portion of their equity awards toward charitable giving, which we match with shares of our Class N common stock. Further, certain donor-advised funds may from time to time receive donations of shares directly from us or from one or more of our stockholders, and we are party to certain irrevocable proxy agreements with such donor-advised funds, as described under “Certain Relationships and Related Person Transactions—Irrevocable Proxy Agreements.”
p1562: Our Class E common stock will not have any right to vote except on certain specified matters (or as otherwise required by law): the nomination or proposed removal of the Specified Class T Director or a change in the director designated as the Specified Class T Director (in circumstances where our NGC does not concur with the LTBT’s proposed action) and certain proposals to amend the terms of the LTBT and the rights of our Class T common stock or to redeem our Class T common stock.
p1563: When voting upon a proposal to nominate or remove the Specified Class T Director or a change in the director designated as the Specified Class T Director (in circumstances where our NGC does not concur with the LTBT’s proposed action), the requisite approval of our Class E common stock will require a majority of votes cast by our Class E common stock and quorum will require the presence, in person or by proxy, of a majority of outstanding shares of Class E common stock.
p1564: When voting on a proposal to amend the terms of the LTBT or the rights of our Class T common stock or to redeem our Class T common stock, in addition to the requisite approval of our Class A common stock as described more fully in the section titled “—Changes to the LTBT and Class T Common Stock,” the requisite approval of our Class E common stock will require:
p1565: • until the third anniversary of the completion of this offering, if our Class F common stock is acting pursuant to the unanimous approval of the Continuing Founders, a majority of the votes cast by our Class E common stock (subject to a quorum of 40% of our outstanding Class E common stock); or
p1566: • at any time when our Class F common stock remains outstanding, 75% of the votes cast by our Class E common stock (subject to a quorum of a majority of outstanding Class E common stock).
p1567: Our amended and restated certificate of incorporation, which will become effective immediately prior to the completion of this offering, will authorize Class E common stock, which will be issued to our employees as follows: (i) one share of Class E common stock for each six months of employment completed with us and (ii) one share of Class E common stock for each share of Class A common stock that such employee has pledged to donate through our donation matching program, or any similar program we may establish in the future. The timing for issuing Class E common stock will be determined after the closing of this offering. Our co-founders will not receive any shares of Class E common stock, and to the extent that a holder of Class E common stock later serves as a successor to any co-founder’s interest in the Founder LLC, they will not be able to vote any Class E common stock they hold during the period of such service.
p1568: Following an employee’s separation from employment with us other than for cause, one-half of such employee’s then-outstanding shares of Class E common stock will be automatically redeemed by us annually, and all of such employee’s shares will be automatically redeemed upon such employee’s death, incapacity, termination for cause, or commencement of service with a direct competitor. All shares of Class E common stock will also be automatically redeemed at such time as no Class F common stock remains outstanding. Any redemption of Class E common stock will be made for no consideration.
p1569: Decisions regarding our business and affairs are made by our board of directors. Immediately prior to the completion of this offering, we will enter into the Stockholders’ Agreement with the LTBT and the Founder LLC, under which they will agree to vote their shares and take other actions to give effect to the board composition, director nomination, and director removal provisions described in our governing documents. Collectively, the LTBT and the Founder LLC will have the ability to elect all members of our board of directors. Regardless of the class or classes of stock by which a director is elected, there is no limit to the number of terms a director may serve.
p1570: While the LTBT has significant influence over our board of directors through its ability to generally elect and remove a majority of the authorized members of our board of directors, neither the LTBT nor the Trustees have decision-making authority in the day-to-day management or strategy setting of the company. The LTBT’s role is to select directors who are well-equipped to make decisions in furtherance of the responsible balancing of the pecuniary interests of our stockholders, the best interests of those materially affected by our conduct, and the Company Purpose, and to support our management’s decision-making through advice and guidance. The Trustees aim to choose directors who have the necessary business skills, experience, and expertise to oversee the management of our business effectively and in a manner that responsibly balances (i) the pecuniary interests of our stockholders, (ii) the best interests of those materially affected by our conduct, and (iii) the Company Purpose.
p1571: The Founder LLC will also have significant influence over our business and affairs through its ability to vote our Class F common stock, which is entitled to an aggregate number of votes that equals 50.1% of the total voting power of our outstanding shares of capital stock as of the applicable record date with respect to matters submitted to stockholders generally. The Founder LLC will be able to elect and remove the directors who are not Class T directors and determine the outcome of all matters submitted to a vote of our stockholders generally (including the approval of any merger, sale of our company, or other significant corporate transaction requiring stockholder approval) for the foreseeable future.
p1572: We are considered a “controlled company” within the meaning of the Nasdaq Global Select Market corporate governance requirements because the LTBT, as the sole holder of our Class T common stock, generally has the power to elect a majority of the authorized members of our board of directors. As such, we are permitted to opt out of compliance with certain Nasdaq Global Select Market corporate governance requirements. Accordingly, if we elect not to comply with certain requirements, you will not have the same protections afforded to stockholders of companies that are subject to all of the Nasdaq Global Select Market corporate governance requirements. Although we qualify as a “controlled company,” we do not expect to rely on this exemption except with respect to our NGC, which will not consist entirely of independent directors. Our board of directors currently consists of a majority of independent directors and our audit and compensation committees currently consist entirely of independent directors.

p1586: Dario Amodei. Dr. Amodei has served as our Chief Executive Officer and a member of our board of directors since co-founding Anthropic in January 2021. Prior to co-founding Anthropic, Dr. Amodei served as Vice President of Research, among other positions, at OpenAI, an AI research lab, from July 2016 to December 2020. Before joining OpenAI, Dr. Amodei served as a Senior Research Scientist at Google Brain, an AI research team at Google, from October 2015 to June 2016. Dr. Amodei completed a postdoctoral fellowship at Stanford University School of Medicine. Dr. Amodei holds a Ph.D. in Biophysics from Princeton University and a B.S. in Physics from Stanford University. We believe that Dr. Amodei is qualified to serve on our board of directors because of the perspective and experience he brings from his deep expertise in the AI industry and as our Chief Executive Officer and as a co-founder.
p1587: Daniela Amodei. Ms. Amodei has served as our President and a member of our board of directors since cofounding Anthropic in January 2021. Ms. Amodei also currently serves as the Chairperson of our board of directors. Prior to co-founding Anthropic, Ms. Amodei held several positions at OpenAI, an AI research lab, including Vice President of Safety and Policy, Vice President of People, and Engineering Manager, between October 2018 and December 2020. Before joining OpenAI, Ms. Amodei was a Risk Manager, among other positions, at Stripe, a financial technology and payment processing company, from May 2013 to July 2018. Ms. Amodei holds a B.A. in English Literature from the University of California, Santa Cruz. We believe that Ms. Amodei is qualified to serve on our board of directors because of the perspective and experience she brings through her deep expertise in the AI industry and as our President and as a co-founder.
p1588: Krishna Rao. Mr. Rao has served as our Chief Financial Officer since April 2024. Prior to joining Anthropic, Mr. Rao served as Chief Financial Officer at Fanatics Commerce, an online sports merchandise and retail platform, from May 2023 to April 2024. Before that, he served as the Chief Financial Officer of Cedar, a healthcare technology company, from July 2021 to May 2023. From October 2015 to July 2021, Mr. Rao held several key positions at Airbnb, a global vacation rental and hospitality platform, including Global Head of Corporate & Business Development and Director of Financial Planning & Analysis. Prior to Airbnb, Mr. Rao was a Principal in the Private Equity Group at Blackstone, a global investment firm, from September 2011 to September 2015. Mr. Rao began his career as a strategy consultant at Bain, a global management consulting firm, from September 2005 to July 2008. Mr. Rao holds a J.D. from Yale Law School and an A.B. in Economics from Harvard College.
p1589: Reed Hastings. Mr. Hastings has served as a member of our board of directors since May 2025. Mr. Hastings co-founded Netflix, a global streaming service, and served as Netflix’s Chief Executive Officer and President from 1999 to January 2023, Executive Chairman from January 2023 to April 2025, and Chairman of the board from April 2025 to June 2026. Prior to Netflix, Mr. Hastings founded Pure Software, a software development tools company, in 1991 and served as its Chief Executive Officer until its acquisition by Rational Software in 1997. Mr. Hastings currently serves on the board of Bloomberg, a financial data and media company. Mr. Hastings holds an M.S.C.S. in Artificial Intelligence from Stanford University and a B.A. in Mathematics from Bowdoin College. We believe that Mr. Hastings is qualified to serve as a member of our board of directors because of his extensive board experience at major technology companies, his demonstrated commitment to responsible innovation and its societal impact, his deep understanding of technology’s transformative potential, and his philanthropic focus on education and AI’s impact on humanity.
p1590: Christopher Liddell. Mr. Liddell has served as a member of our board of directors since February 2026. In the private sector, Mr. Liddell has served as the Chief Financial Officer of several public companies, including Microsoft and International Paper, and served as Vice Chairman and Chief Financial Officer at General Motors. Mr. Liddell has served as a Director of Commonwealth Fusion Systems, a fusion power company, since March 2025, and as a Director of the Council on Foreign Relations, a nonpartisan U.S. think tank focused on foreign policy and international affairs, since July 2025. He has also held positions with the U.S. government from January 2017 to January 2021, including serving at the White House as the Deputy Chief of Staff, Director of Strategic Initiatives, and as a member of the American Technology Council. Mr. Liddell holds a Master of Philosophy from the University of Oxford and a Bachelor of Engineering from the University of Auckland. We believe that Mr. Liddell is qualified to serve as a member of our board of directors because of his wide range of experience from his corporate and public service career and his deep expertise in the financial management of publicly listed companies.
p1591: Vasant “Vas” Narasimhan. Dr. Narasimhan has served as a member of our board of directors since April 2026. Dr. Narasimhan has served as the Chief Executive Officer of Novartis AG, a global medicine company, since February 2018. He joined Novartis in April 2005 and has held numerous leadership roles across the organization, including Global Head of Drug Development and Chief Medical Officer from February 2016 to January 2018 and Global Head of Development from September 2014 to February 2016. Dr. Narasimhan holds an M.D. from Harvard Medical School, an M.P.P. from the Harvard Kennedy School, and a B.A. in Biology from the University of Chicago. We believe that Dr. Narasimhan is qualified to serve as a member of our board of directors because of his extensive experience leading a large global public company in a highly regulated industry and his track record of responsibly stewarding breakthrough science at scale.
p1592: Yasmin Razavi. Ms. Razavi has served as a member of our board of directors since March 2023. p1605: Our amended and restated certificate of incorporation that will become effective immediately prior to the completion of this offering will provide that prior to the Class F Sunset Time, we will not have a classified board of directors, and all directors will be elected for annual terms. Each director’s term will continue until the next annual meeting and until the election and qualification of their successor, or their earlier death, resignation, or removal.
p1606: Following the Class F Sunset Time, our board of directors will shift to having a classified board of directors consisting of three classes of approximately equal size, each serving staggered three-year terms. At such time, each of our directors would be assigned by the then-current board of directors to a class. If our Class T common stock remains outstanding, the Class T directors and the remaining directors shall be allocated among the classes so that each class includes a proportionate number of Class T directors and other directors. Upon expiration of the term of a class of directors, directors for that class would each be elected for a three-year term at the annual meeting of stockholders in the year in which that term expires. As a result, only one class of directors would be elected at each annual meeting of our stockholders, with the other classes continuing for the remainder of their respective three-year terms. Each director’s term would continue until the third annual meeting of stockholders following their election and until his or her successor has been elected and qualified, or until his or her earlier death, resignation, or removal. Any increase or decrease in the number of directors would be distributed among the three classes so that, as nearly as practicable, each class would consist of onethird of our directors.
p1607: Regardless of the class or classes of stock by which a director is elected, there is no limit to the number of terms a director may serve.
p1608: Our amended and restated certificate of incorporation that will become effective immediately prior to the completion of this offering will provide that, for so long as our Class F common stock or Class T common stock remains outstanding, our stockholders may act by written consent with respect to certain actions, including any action to elect or remove directors. Although stockholders will have the ability to take these actions by written consent, we value the perspectives of all of our stockholders and, in accordance with the listing standards of the Nasdaq Global Select Market, we expect to hold an annual meeting of stockholders and to solicit the votes of holders of our Class A common stock in respect of relevant matters to be considered at such meeting, including the election of our directors who are not Class T directors.

p1612: We are considered a “controlled company” within the meaning of the Nasdaq Global Select Market corporate governance requirements because the LTBT, as the sole holder of our Class T common stock, generally has the power to elect a majority of the authorized members of our board of directors. As a result, we may elect not to comply with certain corporate governance requirements, including:
p1613: • the requirement that a majority of our board of directors consist of independent directors;
p1614: • the requirement that our board of directors have a nominating and corporate governance committee that is comprised entirely of independent directors with a written charter addressing the committee’s purpose and responsibilities; and
p1615: • the requirement that our board of directors have a compensation committee that is comprised entirely of independent directors with a written charter addressing the committee’s purpose and responsibilities.
p1616: If we elect not to comply with certain requirements, you will not have the same protections afforded to stockholders of companies that are subject to all of the Nasdaq Global Select Market corporate governance requirements. Although we qualify as a “controlled company,” we do not expect to rely on this exemption except with respect to our NGC, which will not consist entirely of independent directors. Our board of directors currently consists of a majority of independent directors and our audit and compensation committees currently consist entirely of independent directors. In the event that we cease to be a “controlled company” and our Class A common stock continues to be listed on the Nasdaq Global Select Market, we will be required to comply with the provision that our NGC be comprised entirely of independent directors within the applicable transition period.

p1644: In connection with our novel corporate governance structure, our NGC will also have the right to receive 30 days’ prior written notice of any nomination of persons to serve as a director by the LTBT or the Founder LLC or the proposed removal of such directors, as well as appointments and removals of the Trustees of the LTBT. p1669: Annual Award. Each non-employee director automatically will be granted, on the date of each annual meeting of stockholders beginning in 2027, an award of RSUs (the “Annual Award”) with a value of $325,000 (the “Annual Award Grant Value”), which value will be converted to a number of shares of our Class A common stock in accordance with then-current standard company practices using the same methodology applied to employee equity awards pursuant to the company’s equity grant policy, as most recently approved by our board of directors or a board committee that has been designated appropriate authority (the “Conversion Methodology”). An Annual Award will vest in four equal quarterly installments on each Quarterly Vesting Date (as defined below) that occurs following the grant date of the Annual Award provided that, in any event, the Annual Award will vest in full on the day immediately before the date of our next annual meeting of stockholders that follows the grant date of the Annual Award, subject to the non-employee director continuing to be a service provider to us through the applicable vesting date. “Quarterly Vesting Date” means February 20, May 20, August 20, and November 20 of a given year.
p1670: Initial Award and Pro-Rated Annual Award. Each person who first becomes a non-employee director following the effective date of the Director Compensation Policy will be automatically granted:
p1671: • An award of RSUs with a value of $400,000, which value will be converted to a number of shares of our Class A common stock subject to such award using the Conversion Methodology (an “Initial Award”); and
p1672: • An award of RSUs with a value equal to the Annual Award Grant Value multiplied by the fraction obtained by dividing (A) the number of full months during the period beginning on the date the individual first becomes a non-employee director and ending on the one-year anniversary of the date of our then-most recent annual meeting of stockholders by (B) 12, which will be converted to a number of shares of our Class A common stock subject to such award using the Conversion Methodology (a “ProRated Annual Award”).
p1673: The grant of each Initial Award and Pro-Rated Annual Award will be made effective on the first trading date on or after the date on which such individual first becomes a non-employee director (such date, the “Initial Start Date”). If an individual is a member of our board of directors and also an employee, becoming a non-employee director due to termination of employment will not entitle the non-employee director to an Initial Award or a Pro-Rated Annual Award.
p1674: The Initial Award will vest as follows: 12.5% of the RSUs will vest on the six-month anniversary of the Vesting Commencement Date (as defined below) and the balance of the RSUs will vest in 14 successive equal quarterly installments on each Quarterly Vesting Date thereafter, subject to the non-employee director remaining a service provider to us through the applicable vesting date. “Vesting Commencement Date” means the first Quarterly Vesting Date that occurs on or following the Initial Start Date. The Pro-Rated Annual Award will vest in equal installments on each Quarterly Vesting Date that occurs between the Initial Start Date and the earlier of (i) our next annual meeting of stockholders that occurs after the Pro-Rated Annual Award’s grant date or (ii) the one-year anniversary of our most recent annual meeting of stockholders, provided that, in any event, the Pro-Rated Annual Award will vest in full on the day immediately before the date of our next annual meeting of stockholders that occurs after the Pro-Rated Annual Award’s grant date (for purposes of clarity, each such Quarterly Vesting Date and the final vest date that occurs on the date immediately before our next annual meeting of stockholders or one-year anniversary of our most recent annual meeting of stockholders, as applicable, will be counted as one installment such that, if there are two such Quarterly Vesting Dates, the ProRated Annual Award shall vest in three equal installments), subject to the non-employee director remaining a service provider to us through the applicable vesting date.

p1682: At Anthropic, we strive to build a team that is aligned with our mission and values. Executive compensation reflects our overall compensation philosophy, which prioritizes competitive pay that targets the 90th percentile of the AI development market, consistent pay for the same role, level, and location, and simplicity of plan design. In 2025, we offered a competitive mix of base salary, long-term equity incentive awards (including stock options and RSUs), and other benefits to attract and retain top talent in a competitive market environment.
p1683: Our executive compensation philosophy is to provide our executive officers with consistent cash and equity compensation for the same role, level, and location. When determining executive compensation, we review each executive’s current compensation against role- and level-specific market data. We do this bi-annually as part of our performance and compensation cycle where we review proposed market-based and promotion-based cash and equity increases for executives. We plan to continue to regularly review, and potentially adjust, our executive compensation programs to ensure they are consistent with our compensation philosophy as a public company.
p1684: In determining compensation for our senior leaders, we distinguish between our seven co-founders (among whom only Dr. Amodei and Ms. Amodei are executive officers) and our other senior leaders who are not cofounders (among whom only Mr. Rao is an executive officer). Each co-founder is paid equal compensation. As a non-co-founder senior leader, Mr. Rao received base salary and equity compensation based on market data for his role and level.
p1685: Our executive compensation program is structured to achieve the objectives described below. We regularly review our executive compensation program to assess whether it meets these objectives and adapts to evolving economic conditions.
p1686: • Competitive Pay to Attract and Retain Top Talent. We provide our executives with competitive cash and equity pay for each role, location, and level to attract mission-aligned, top executive talent.
p1687: • Internal Parity. We take internal parity into account when determining executive compensation. As co-founders, Dr. Amodei and Ms. Amodei are awarded equal compensation, including any annual cash or equity increases. As a non-co-founder senior leader, Mr. Rao is compensated based on the market data from our peer group for his role, level, and location. We review market data twice a year and make adjustments to our compensation benchmarks as needed.
p1688: • Aligning Executive Interests with Our Stockholders. We provide incentives that seek to align our executives’ interests with those of our stockholders through long-term equity awards, which vest over time.

p1691: Our executive compensation program has historically been overseen by the non-employee members of our board of directors, which, as a group, has made decisions regarding the compensation for our NEOs after considering recommendations from management, as further discussed below.
p1692: Following the completion of this offering, the compensation committee of our board of directors will oversee our executive compensation program and provide recommendations to our board of directors on compensation decisions for our executive officers. The compensation committee will work closely with its independent compensation consultant (engaged in connection with this offering, as described below) and meet regularly to make decisions on our executive compensation program. We expect that our compensation committee will review a variety of market data and information, including survey data, and consider the recommendations of its independent compensation consultant when making compensation decisions. Following the completion of this offering, the compensation committee’s responsibilities will include, among other things, reviewing and approving (or making recommendations to our board of directors, as applicable): overall compensation strategy; amounts and form of executive compensation; goals and objectives to be considered in determining the compensation of our Chief Executive Officer and other executive officers; annual and long-term incentive plans and benefit plans; board of directors compensation; whether such compensation policies and practices create risks that are reasonably likely to have a material adverse effect on the company; annual say-on-pay vote results; annual proxy and CD&A disclosure; and compensation peer group.
p1693: Our Chief Executive Officer and our other executive officers do not set their own compensation, nor are they present when our board of directors sets their individual compensation. Our President reviews and advises on compensation for the seven co-founders but does not make specific recommendations on or participate in decisions related to her compensation or our Chief Executive Officer’s compensation. Our President also provides her evaluation and makes recommendations with respect to base salary and equity awards for each other executive officer, which are considered by our board of directors as it ultimately makes its determinations. Our people team provides further analysis and feedback as requested by our board of directors with regard to the compensation of our executives.

p1703: We generally provide the same benefits to all of our employees, including our NEOs, and generally do not maintain benefit plans that cover only executive officers or provide perquisites or personal benefits to our NEOs. However, we do provide certain travel and security benefits to some of our NEOs. These benefits are described in more detail below. Our board of directors believes these benefits are reasonable and necessary, and for the benefit of our company. These benefits are intended to promote the productivity of our executives, in addition to ensuring their personal health, safety, and security. The aggregate incremental cost of providing these benefits to our NEOs is disclosed in the “All Other Compensation” column of the Summary Compensation Table.
p1704: We maintain a Travel and Expense Policy (the “Travel Policy”), which outlines guidelines and allowances for executive travel and expenses, recognizing the needs and responsibilities of our senior leadership team. The Travel Policy governs all business-related travel and expenses for our executives, except to the extent benefits are provided through a security program authorized and/or approved by our board of directors. Dr. Amodei and Ms. Amodei are entitled to certain enhanced travel benefits recommended by the security studies on which their security program is based (discussed in the section below titled “Security Services”). The Travel Policy is reviewed annually by our management team to ensure it remains appropriate and aligned with company objectives and industry standards. To the extent required by the relevant tax laws, the value of any personal use, including any personal elements of business trips, will be treated as taxable compensation to the executive, and we do not cover, reimburse, or otherwise “gross-up” any income tax due from any applicable executive on such compensation.
p1705: Except as noted in the subsection below titled “Security Services,” none of our NEOs were provided with private aviation services for personal travel in 2025.
p1706: The protection of our senior leadership is a critical priority for our company and our stockholders. In connection with our security program and our evaluation of security threats, we offer security services to certain of our NEOs and may provide security services to other NEOs in the future. Such security services may include: (i) individual protection services (including the protection of family members) and home security systems and monitoring, (ii) private aviation, and (iii) private car and driver services. These safeguards are implemented due to the variety of business-related security concerns faced by our senior leaders, and they are comparable to those provided to senior leaders of comparable high-profile companies in the technology industry.
p1707: In 2025, a leading security consulting firm conducted independent, third-party security studies regarding the personal and security risks of our Chief Executive Officer and our President. Based on these security studies, increased media attention for Anthropic, and the identification of bona fide business-related, heightened security concerns arising as a result of the respective positions of Dr. Amodei and Ms. Amodei within the company, our board of directors determined that enhanced personal security services were necessary to increase the safety and protection of Dr. Amodei and Ms. Amodei, and to avoid an impact to our business continuity if a security incident occurred. Our board of directors regularly assesses security concerns and reviews the security services provided to Dr. Amodei and Ms. Amodei and the cost of such services in light of such concerns, and other benefits to our company. The security measures for Dr. Amodei and Ms. Amodei in 2025 included (i) individual protection services (including during personal travel), which included the protection of family members, as well as enhanced home security systems and surveillance, (ii) private car and driver services for ground transportation, and (iii) in the case of Dr. Amodei, the use of private aircraft for both business and personal travel.
p1708: Given the importance of the roles of Dr. Amodei and Ms. Amodei at Anthropic, our board of directors required the security measures described above for the benefit of our company, and we view the costs of these services as necessary and appropriate. In the “All Other Compensation” column of the Summary Compensation Table, we have disclosed the aggregate incremental cost of the security benefits that may be deemed to be perquisites under current relevant disclosure rules. We did not pay expenses for personal security for any other NEOs in 2025, except in connection with business-related travel.

p1716: We have adopted an executive compensation recoupment policy intended to comply with the requirements of Rule 10D-1 under the Exchange Act and the rules of the stock exchange on which our securities are listed (“Clawback Policy”) that will be effective upon the effectiveness of the registration statement of which this prospectus forms a part. The Clawback Policy will generally require us to recover erroneously awarded incentive-based compensation that was received by covered executive officers in the event we are required to prepare an accounting restatement due to any material noncompliance with any financial reporting requirement under the securities laws (including any required accounting restatement to correct an error in previously issued financial statements that is material to the previously issued financial statements), or that would result in a material misstatement if the error were corrected in the current period or left uncorrected in the current period. The Clawback Policy generally covers incentive-based compensation received on or after the effective date of the Clawback Policy and during the three-year period prior to the date we are required to prepare the financial restatement. The amount required to be recovered is the excess of the amount of incentive-based compensation received over the amount that otherwise would have been received based on the restated financial measure.
p1717: We are dedicated to fostering high standards of ethical business conduct and adherence to applicable laws, rules, and regulations. Accordingly, we maintain our Insider Trading Policy, which we believe is appropriately designed to foster compliance with insider trading laws, rules, and regulations, and the listing standards of the Nasdaq Global Select Market that will be applicable to us. Our Insider Trading Policy applies to all of our officers, directors, and employees, as well as designated consultants, and specifically prohibits ownership of financial instruments or participation in investment strategies that hedge the economic risk of owning our equity securities, such as prepaid variable forwards, equity swaps, and collars. Directors, officers, and other employees are prohibited from maintaining company securities in a margin account or otherwise pledging company securities as collateral for a loan, provided that certain limited exceptions may be permitted. In addition, we prohibit our executive officers, directors, and employees from purchasing or selling our securities while in possession of material, non-public information or otherwise utilizing such information for their personal benefit. We maintain a quarterly blackout window where applicable individuals may not trade.
