p1750: General. Our 2026 Plan was adopted by our board of directors on September 1, 2026, and approved by our stockholders on October 22, 2026. Our 2026 Plan will become effective as of the day immediately prior to the day the registration statement of which this prospectus forms a part is effective.
p1751: Share Reserve. The maximum aggregate number of shares that may be issued under our 2026 Plan is: (i) shares of our Class A common stock; plus (ii) the number of shares of our Class A common stock equal to the total shares of Voting Common Stock available for issuance pursuant to our 2021 Plan immediately prior to the termination of our 2021 Plan on the effective date of our 2026 Plan; plus (iii) the number of shares of our Class A common stock equal to the total shares of Voting Common Stock subject to awards previously granted under our 2021 Plan that, after the effective date of our 2026 Plan, would have returned to our 2021 Plan and become available for issuance pursuant to future awards under our 2021 Plan had our 2021 Plan not terminated on the effective date of our 2026 Plan (provided that the maximum number of shares pursuant to (ii) plus (iii) is shares).
p1752: In addition, the number of shares that may be issued under our 2026 Plan will be increased on the first day of each fiscal year beginning with our 2027 fiscal year and ending on (and including) the first day of our 2036 fiscal year, in an amount equal to the lesser of: (i) 5% of the total number of shares of our common stock (including only all classes of common stock issued by the company that carry economic rights) outstanding on the last day of the calendar month prior to the date of such automatic increase (calculated on an as-converted basis); and (ii) such number of shares determined by our board of directors.
p1753: To the extent an award should expire or be forfeited or become unexercisable for any reason without having been exercised in full, or is surrendered pursuant to an exchange program, the unissued shares that were subject thereto shall continue to be available under our 2026 Plan for issuance pursuant to future awards. In addition, any shares which are retained by us to satisfy exercise or purchase price or any withholding taxes shall be treated as not issued and shall continue to be available under our 2026 Plan for issuance pursuant to future awards. Shares issued under our 2026 Plan and later forfeited to us due to the failure to vest or repurchased by us at a price no greater than the original purchase price paid to us for the shares shall again be available for future grant under our 2026 Plan. To the extent an award under our 2026 Plan is paid out in cash rather than shares, such cash payment will not reduce the number of shares available for issuance under our 2026 Plan.
p1754: Plan Administration. Our board of directors has delegated its authority to administer our 2026 Plan to our compensation committee. Subject to the provisions of our 2026 Plan, the administrator has the power to determine the terms of awards, including the recipients, the exercise price, if any, the number of shares subject to each award, the fair market value of a share of our Class A common stock, the vesting schedule applicable to the awards, together with any vesting acceleration, the form of consideration, if any, payable upon exercise of the award and the terms of the award agreement for use under our 2026 Plan. The administrator also has the authority, subject to the terms of our 2026 Plan, to amend existing awards, to prescribe rules and to construe and interpret our 2026 Plan and awards granted thereunder and to institute an exchange program by which outstanding awards are amended to provide for a lower exercise price or surrendered or cancelled in exchange for awards with a lower exercise price, a different type of award under our 2026 Plan or a different equity incentive plan, cash, or a combination thereof.
p1755: Eligibility. Employees, members of our board of directors who are not employees, and consultants (including, without limitation, employees of a staffing agency, professional employer organization, employer of record, and similar workers) are eligible to participate in our 2026 Plan.
p1756: Types of Awards. Our 2026 Plan provides for the grant of stock options, stock appreciation rights, restricted stock, restricted stock units, and stock bonus awards to our employees, directors, and consultants and the employees and consultants of our subsidiaries.
p1757: Stock Options. The administrator may grant incentive stock options (within the meaning of Section 422 of the Code) and/or nonstatutory stock options under our 2026 Plan, provided that incentive stock options may only be granted to our employees and the employees of our subsidiaries. The exercise price applicable to such options must generally be equal to at least the fair market value of our Class A common stock on the date of grant. The term of an incentive stock option may not exceed 10 years; provided, however, that an incentive stock option held by a participant who owns more than 10% of the total combined voting power of all classes of our stock, or of certain of our subsidiary corporations, may not have a term in excess of five years and must have an exercise price equal to at least 110% of the fair market value of our Class A common stock on the grant date.
p1758: The administrator will determine the methods of payment of the exercise price applicable to an option, which may include cash, shares, or other property acceptable to the administrator. Subject to the provisions of our 2026 Plan, the administrator determines the remaining terms of the options. Such terms may include, among other things, vesting upon the achievement of specific performance goals determined by the administrator and/ or continued service. After the termination of service, the participant may exercise their option, to the extent vested, for the period of time stated in their option agreement. Except in the event of a termination for cause, options generally remain outstanding to the extent exercisable for the full term of the options. In no event may an option be exercised later than the expiration of its term. The specific terms will be set forth in an award agreement.
p1759: Stock Appreciation Rights. Stock appreciation rights may be granted under our 2026 Plan. Stock appreciation rights allow the recipient to receive the appreciation in the fair market value of our Class A common stock between the date of grant and the exercise date. Subject to the provisions of our 2026 Plan, the administrator determines the terms of stock appreciation rights, including when such rights vest and become exercisable and whether to settle such awards in cash or with shares of our Class A common stock, or a combination thereof, except that the per share exercise price for the shares to be issued pursuant to the exercise of a stock appreciation right will be no less than 100% of the fair market value per share on the date of grant. The specific terms will be set forth in an award agreement.
p1760: Restricted Stock. Restricted stock may be granted under our 2026 Plan. RSAs are grants of shares of our Class A common stock that are subject to various restrictions, including restrictions on transferability and forfeiture provisions. Shares of restricted stock will vest and the restrictions on such shares will lapse, in accordance with terms and conditions established by the administrator. Such terms may include, among other things, vesting upon the achievement of specific performance goals determined by the administrator and/or continued service. The administrator, in its sole discretion, may accelerate the time at which any restrictions will lapse or be removed. Recipients of RSAs generally will have voting and dividend rights with respect to such shares upon grant without regard to vesting, unless the administrator provides otherwise. Shares of restricted stock that do not vest for any reason will be subject to our right of repurchase or forfeited by the recipient. The specific terms will be set forth in an award agreement.
p1761: Restricted Stock Units. RSUs may be granted under our 2026 Plan and may include the right to dividend equivalents, as determined in the discretion of the administrator. Each RSU granted is a bookkeeping entry representing an amount equal to the fair market value of one share of our Class A common stock. The administrator determines the terms and conditions of RSUs, including the vesting criteria, which may include achievement of specified performance criteria and/or continued service. The administrator, in its sole discretion, may accelerate the time at which any restrictions will lapse or be removed. The administrator determines, in its sole discretion, the timing of payment and whether an award will be settled in stock, cash, or a combination thereof. The specific terms will be set forth in an award agreement.
p1762: Stock Bonus Awards. Stock bonus awards may be granted under our 2026 Plan. The administrator may grant stock bonus awards in such amounts, and subject to such terms, as the administrator, in its sole discretion, will determine. A stock bonus award is an award of shares of our Class A common stock without a purchase price. All stock bonus awards may be made, but are not required to be made, pursuant to an award agreement. Payment of a stock bonus award may be made in the form of cash, shares, or a combination thereof, based on the fair market value of the shares subject to the stock bonus award on the date of payment, as determined in the sole discretion of the administrator.
p1763: Outside Director Limitations. Stock awards granted during a single fiscal year under our 2026 Plan or otherwise, taken together with any cash fees paid during such fiscal year for services on our board of directors, shall not exceed $1,000,000 in total value for any non-employee director, except with respect to the first year of service in which case any stock awards granted and cash fees paid will not exceed $2,000,000 in total value (calculating the value of any such stock awards, in each case, based on the grant date fair value of such stock awards for financial reporting purposes). Such applicable limit includes the value of any stock awards that are granted in lieu of all or a portion of any annual committee cash retainers or other similar cash-based payments. Stock awards granted to an individual while they were serving in the capacity as an employee or while they were an independent contractor but not a non-employee director will not count for purposes of the limitations described above.
p1764: Non-Transferability of Awards. Unless the administrator provides otherwise, our 2026 Plan generally does not allow for the transfer of awards other than by will or the laws of descent and distribution and only the recipient of an option or stock appreciation right may exercise such an award during their lifetime.
p1765: Certain Adjustments. In the event of a stock split, reverse stock split, stock dividend, combination, consolidation, recapitalization (including a recapitalization through a large nonrecurring cash dividend or distribution of property, including shares of a subsidiary) or reclassification of the shares, subdivision of the shares, a rights offering, a reorganization, merger, spin-off, split-up, repurchase, or exchange of common stock or other securities of the company or other significant corporate transaction, or other change affecting the common stock occurs, the administrator, in order to prevent dilution, diminution, or enlargement of the benefits or potential benefits intended to be made available under our 2026 Plan, will, in such manner as it may deem equitable, adjust the number, kind, and class of securities that may be delivered under our 2026 Plan and/or the number, class, kind, and price of securities covered by each outstanding award, and the terms and conditions of any outstanding award (including, without limitation, any applicable performance targets or criteria with respect thereto).
p1766: Dissolution or Liquidation. In the event of a proposed winding up, dissolution, or liquidation of the company, the administrator will notify participants as soon as practicable prior to the effective date of such proposed transaction and all awards will terminate immediately prior to the consummation of such proposed transaction, to the extent not previously exercised or settled.
p1767: Corporate Transaction. Our 2026 Plan provides that, in the event of certain significant corporate transactions, including: (1) a transfer of all or substantially all of our assets; (2) a merger, consolidation or other capital reorganization or business combination transaction of the company with or into another corporation, entity or person; or (3) the consummation of a transaction, or series of related transactions, in which any person becomes the beneficial owner, directly or indirectly, of more than 50% of the company’s then outstanding capital stock, each outstanding award will be treated as the administrator determines. Such determination, without the consent of any participant, may provide that such awards will be (i) continued if we are the surviving corporation; (ii) assumed by the surviving corporation or its parent; (iii) substituted by the surviving corporation or its parent for a new award; (iv) cancelled in exchange for a payment equal to the excess of the fair market value of our shares subject to such award over the exercise price or purchase price paid for such shares; (v) subject to full or partial acceleration of vesting, settlement, payment, and/or expiration as of immediately prior to the corporate transaction; (vi) subject to full or partial lapse of forfeiture, repurchase or reacquisition rights with respect to shares previously acquired pursuant to any awards as of immediately prior to the corporate transaction; (vii) in the case of outstanding options and/or stock appreciation rights, allowed to be exercised prior to the occurrence of the corporate transaction and terminated (for no consideration) upon the consummation of such corporate transaction if not exercised prior thereto; or (viii) cancelled in exchange for no consideration.
p1768: Change in Control. The administrator may provide, in an individual award agreement or in any other written agreement between a participant and us, that the stock award will be subject to additional acceleration of vesting, settlement, payment, and/or expiration in the event of a change in control.
p1769: Under our 2026 Plan, a “change in control” is generally (1) a merger, consolidation, or any other corporate reorganization in which the shares of capital stock of the company immediately before the transaction cease to represent immediately after such transaction at least a majority of the voting power of the continuing or surviving entity in substantially the same proportions immediately after such transaction as in effect before such transaction; (2) with certain limited exceptions, the consummation of the sale, transfer or other disposition of all or substantially all of our assets; (3) a change in the effective control of the company which occurs on the date that a majority of our board members are replaced during any 12-month period by directors whose appointment or election is not endorsed by a majority of the members of our board of directors prior to the date of the appointment or election; or (4) the consummation of any transaction as a result of which any person or company becomes the beneficial owner, directly or indirectly, of at least 50% of the total voting power represented by our then outstanding voting securities. No transaction shall constitute a change in control (i) as the result of the initial effectiveness of the company’s amended and restated certificate of incorporation that will become effective immediately prior to the effectiveness of the registration statement of which this prospectus forms a part, (ii) pursuant to Section (3) above until after the time at which both the Class F Sunset Time and the Class T Sunset Time have occurred, as such terms are defined in the company’s amended and restated certificate of incorporation that will become effective immediately prior to the effectiveness of the registration statement of which this prospectus forms a part, (iii) if its primary purpose is to change the jurisdiction of the company’s incorporation or to create a holding company owned in substantially the same proportions by the persons who held company securities immediately before such transactions, or (iv) if required for compliance with Section 409A of the Code, a transaction will not be a change in control unless it is also a “change in the ownership or effective control of” the company or “a change in the ownership of a substantial portion of the assets of” the company as determined under applicable Treasury regulations.
p1770: Compensation Recovery Policy. Awards granted under our 2026 Plan will be subject to reduction, cancellation, forfeiture, and/or recoupment in accordance with any compensation recovery policy as may be in effect as of the date of grant of such award, or as such policy is amended or another policy is adopted to comply with applicable laws. In addition, the administrator may impose such other compensation recovery or recoupment provisions in any award agreement as it determines necessary or appropriate.
p1771: Amendment or Termination. Our administrator has the authority to amend, alter, suspend, or terminate our 2026 Plan, provided such action does not materially impair the existing rights of any participant unless otherwise provided in our 2026 Plan or mutually agreed otherwise. Our 2026 Plan will continue in effect until terminated by the administrator, but no options that qualify as incentive stock options may be granted after 10 years from the earlier of the board or stockholder approval of our 2026 Plan. We will obtain stockholder approval of any amendment to our 2026 Plan as required by applicable law or listing requirements.
p1772: General. Our board of directors adopted our 2021 Plan on January 28, 2021 and last amended our 2021 Plan effective as of May 28, 2026. Our 2021 Plan will be terminated effective as of the day immediately prior to the day the registration statement of which this prospectus forms a part becomes effective, and no new awards will be granted under our 2021 Plan following this offering, but previously granted awards will continue to be subject to the terms and conditions of our 2021 Plan and the award agreements evidencing such awards.
p1773: Share Reserve. We have reserved for issuance pursuant to our 2021 Plan an aggregate of 3,864,826,090 shares of our Class A common stock. In general, if an award granted under our 2021 Plan (i) expires or is terminated, cancelled, or otherwise forfeited by a participant, (ii) a share subject to an award is withheld in satisfaction of the exercise price and/or tax withholding due in connection with such award, or (iii) a share previously issued pursuant to an award is forfeited or repurchased at the original purchase price paid for the share, then the number of unissued shares subject to any such award, and any such withheld, forfeited, or repurchased shares, will again become available for awards under our 2021 Plan. Following the effectiveness of our 2026 Plan, such shares will again become available for awards under our 2026 Plan.
p1774: Plan Administration. Our board of directors has administered our 2021 Plan before this offering. Our board of directors has delegated its authority to administer our 2021 Plan to our compensation committee following this offering.
p1775: Types of Awards. Our 2021 Plan provides for incentive and non-statutory stock options to purchase shares of our Class A common stock, RSAs, and RSUs. As of the date of this prospectus, we have issued stock options, restricted stock, and RSUs pursuant to our 2021 Plan.
p1776: Non-transferability of Awards. Unless the administrator provides otherwise, our 2021 Plan generally does not allow for the transfer of awards other than by will or the laws of descent and distribution and only the recipient of an option right may exercise such an award during their lifetime.
p1777: Certain Adjustments. In the event of certain corporate events or changes in our capitalization, to prevent diminution or enlargement of the benefits or potential benefits available under our 2021 Plan, the administrator will make adjustments to one or more of the number, kind, and class of securities that may be delivered under our 2021 Plan and/or the number, kind, class, and price of securities covered by each outstanding award.
p1778: Corporate Transaction. Our 2021 Plan provides that in the event of (i) a transfer of all or substantially all of our assets, (ii) a merger, consolidation, or other capital reorganization or business combination transaction of us with or into another corporation, entity, or person, or (iii) the consummation of a transaction, or series of related transactions, in which any “person” becomes the “beneficial owner,” directly or indirectly, of more than 50% of our then outstanding capital stock (each, a “Corporate Transaction”), the administrator may, in its sole and absolute discretion and without the need for the consent of any participant, take one or more of the following actions contingent upon the occurrence of that Corporate Transaction with respect to outstanding awards granted under our 2021 Plan which provide for: (A) the continuation of such awards by us (if we are the surviving corporation); (B) the assumption of such awards by the surviving corporation or its parent; (C) the substitution by the surviving corporation or its parent of new options or equity awards for such awards; (D) the cancellation of such awards in exchange for a payment to the participants equal to the excess of (1) the fair market value of the shares or units subject to such awards as of the closing date of such Corporate Transaction over (2) the exercise price or purchase price paid or to be paid for the shares or units representing shares subject to the awards, as applicable; or (E) the cancellation of any outstanding awards or an outstanding right to purchase restricted stock, in either case, for no consideration.
p1779: Amendment or Termination. Our board of directors may amend or terminate our 2021 Plan at any time. If our board of directors amends our 2021 Plan, we will ask our stockholders to approve the amendment if such approval is necessary or desirable to comply with applicable law. No further awards will be made under our 2021 Plan after this offering.
p1780: General. Our ESPP was adopted by our board of directors on September 1, 2026, and approved by our stockholders on October 22, 2026. Our ESPP will become effective as of the day immediately prior to the day the registration statement of which this prospectus forms a part is effective.
p1781: Our ESPP includes two components: a 423 component and a non-423 component. We intend the 423 component to qualify as an “employee stock purchase plan” within the meaning of Section 423 of the Code. The non-423 component authorizes grants of purchase rights that do not comply with Section 423 of the Code.
p1782: Share Reserve. The maximum aggregate number of shares that may be issued under our ESPP is shares of our Class A common stock.
p1783: In addition, the number of shares that may be issued under our ESPP will be increased on the first day of each fiscal year beginning with our 2027 fiscal year and ending on (and including) the first day of our 2036 fiscal year, in an amount equal to the lesser of: (i) 1% of the total number of shares of our common stock (including only all classes of common stock issued by the company that carry economic rights) outstanding on the last day of the calendar month prior to the date of such automatic increase (calculated on an as-converted basis); and (ii) such number of shares determined by our board of directors.
p1784: Plan Administration. Our ESPP is administered by our board of directors or a committee designated by our board of directors. Our board of directors has delegated its authority to administer our ESPP to our compensation committee.
p1785: Eligibility. Generally, all regular employees, including executive officers, employed by us or by any of our designated affiliates and specified service providers (including non-U.S. service providers) of the company or our designated affiliates may participate in our ESPP.
p1786: Employees may have to satisfy one or more of the following service requirements before participating in the 423 components of our ESPP, as determined by the administrator, including: (1) continuous service with us or one of our affiliates for at least two years (or such lesser period of time as may be determined by our board of directors), (2) being customarily employed for more than 20 hours per week (or such lesser period of time as may be determined by our board of directors), (3) being customarily employed for more than five months per calendar year (or such lesser period of time as may be determined by our board of directors), (4) is not a highly compensated employee within the meaning of Section 423(b)(4)(D) of the Code, or (5) such other criteria as our board of directors may determine to be consistent with Section 423 of the Code. No employee may purchase shares under the 423 component of our ESPP at a rate in excess of $25,000 worth of our Class A common stock based on the fair market value per share of our Class A common stock at the beginning of an offering for each year such a purchase right is outstanding. Finally, no employee will be eligible for the grant of any purchase rights under the 423 component of our ESPP if immediately after such rights are granted, such employee has voting power over 5% or more of our outstanding capital stock measured by vote or value under Section 424(d) of the Code.
p1787: Offerings. Our ESPP is implemented through offerings pursuant to which participants are granted rights to purchase shares of our Class A common stock on specified dates during such offerings. Under our ESPP, we may specify offerings with durations of not more than 27 months and may specify shorter purchase periods within each offering. Each offering will have one or more purchase dates on which shares of our Class A common stock will be purchased by participants in the offering. An offering under our ESPP may be terminated under certain circumstances. The administrator will have the discretion to structure an offering so that if the fair market value of a share of our Class A common stock on the first trading day of a new purchase period within that offering is less than or equal to the fair market value of a share of our Class A common stock on the offering date for that offering, then that offering will terminate immediately as of that first trading day, and the participants in such terminated offering will be automatically enrolled in a new offering beginning on the first trading day of such new offering.
p1788: Payroll Deductions. Participants who are employees may generally make contributions through payroll deductions (unless otherwise required by law or provided for in an offering). In the case of an offering under the 423 component, such percentage or maximum dollar amount of contributions may not exceed 15% of their earnings for the applicable offering. Contributions pursuant to the non-423 component will generally be made on an after-tax basis in a manner determined by the administrator.
p1789: Shares of our Class A common stock will be purchased for the accounts of participants in our ESPP at a price per share that is not less than the lesser of (1) 85% of the fair market value of a share of our Class A common stock on the first date of an offering, or (2) 85% of the fair market value of a share of our Class A common stock on the date of purchase.
p1790: Certain Adjustments. In the event of any change that is made in, or other events that occur with respect to, our Class A common stock subject to our ESPP or subject to any purchase right without the receipt of consideration by the company through merger, consolidation, reorganization, recapitalization, reincorporation, stock dividend, dividend in property other than cash, large nonrecurring cash dividend, stock split, liquidating dividend, combination of shares, exchange of shares, change in corporate structure, or other similar equity restructuring transaction, our board of directors will make appropriate and proportionate adjustments to: (1) the class(es) and maximum number of shares reserved under our ESPP, (2) the class(es) and maximum number of shares by which the share reserve may increase automatically each year, (3) the class(es) and number of shares subject to, and purchase price applicable to, all outstanding offerings and purchase rights, and (4) the class(es) and number of shares that are subject to purchase limits under ongoing offerings.
p1791: Dissolution or Liquidation. In the event of a dissolution or liquidation of the company, any offering then in progress will be shortened by setting a new purchase date prior to the consummation of such proposed dissolution or liquidation. The board of directors will notify each participant that the purchase date has been changed and that the participant’s purchase right will be exercised automatically on the new purchase date unless prior to such date the participant has withdrawn from the offering.
p1792: Corporate Transactions. Our ESPP provides that in the event of certain significant corporate transactions, including: (1) a transfer of all or substantially all of our assets; (2) a merger, consolidation, or other capital, reorganization or business combination transaction of the company with or into another corporation, entity, or person; or (3) the consummation of a transaction, or series of related transactions, in which any person becomes the beneficial owner, directly or indirectly, of more than 50% of our then outstanding capital stock, a successor corporation may assume, continue, or substitute each outstanding purchase right. If the successor corporation does not assume, continue, or substitute the purchase right, the participants’ accumulated contributions will be used to purchase shares prior to the corporate transaction and the purchase rights will terminate immediately after such purchase. The administrator will notify each participant that the purchase date has been changed and that the participant’s purchase right will be exercised automatically on the new purchase date unless prior to such date the participant has withdrawn from the offering.
p1793: Spin-Off. In the event of a spin-off or similar transaction, our board of directors may take actions deemed necessary or appropriate in connection with any ongoing offering, subject to compliance with applicable laws. p1826: We expect to adopt an amended and restated certificate of incorporation, which will become effective immediately prior to the completion of this offering, and which will contain provisions that limit the liability of our directors and certain officers for monetary damages to the fullest extent permitted by the DGCL. p1827: • any breach of the director’s or officer’s duty of loyalty to our company or our stockholders;

p1832: Any amendment to, or repeal of, these provisions will not eliminate or reduce the effect of these provisions in respect of any act, omission, or claim that occurred or arose prior to that amendment or repeal. If the DGCL is amended to provide for further limitations on the personal liability of directors and officers of corporations, then the personal liability of our directors and officers will be further limited to the greatest extent permitted by the DGCL.
p1833: In addition, we expect to adopt amended and restated bylaws, which will become effective immediately prior to the completion of this offering, and which will provide that we will indemnify, to the fullest extent permitted by law, any person who is or was a party or is threatened to be made a party to any action, suit, or proceeding by reason of the fact that they are or were one of our directors or officers or are or were serving at our request as a director or officer of another corporation, partnership, joint venture, trust, or other enterprise. Our amended and restated bylaws are expected to provide that we may indemnify to the fullest extent permitted by law any person who is or was a party or is threatened to be made a party to any action, suit, or proceeding by reason of the fact that they are or were one of our employees or agents or are or were serving at our request as an employee or agent of another corporation, partnership, joint venture, trust, or other enterprise. Our amended and restated bylaws will also provide that we must advance expenses incurred by or on behalf of a director or officer in advance of the final disposition of any action or proceeding, subject to limited exceptions.
p1834: Further, we have entered into or will enter into indemnification agreements with each of our directors and executive officers that may be broader than the specific indemnification provisions contained in the DGCL. These indemnification agreements require us, among other things, to indemnify our directors and executive officers against liabilities that may arise by reason of their status or service. These indemnification agreements also require us to advance all expenses incurred by the directors and executive officers in investigating or defending any such action, suit, or proceeding. We believe that these agreements are necessary to attract and retain qualified individuals to serve as directors and executive officers.
p1835: The limitation of liability and indemnification provisions that are expected to be included in our amended and restated certificate of incorporation, amended and restated bylaws, and indemnification agreements that we have entered into or will enter into with our directors and executive officers may discourage stockholders from bringing a lawsuit against our directors and executive officers for breach of their fiduciary duties. They may also reduce the likelihood of derivative litigation against our directors and executive officers, even though an action, if successful, might benefit us and other stockholders. Further, a stockholder’s investment may be adversely affected to the extent that we pay the costs of settlement and damage awards against directors and executive officers as required by these indemnification provisions. We cannot predict whether, when, or the amount of any future claims for indemnification in connection with any settlement or judgment. Under Delaware law and our amended and restated certificate of incorporation, in the absence of a conflict of interest, no failure to satisfy the balancing obligations associated with our status as a PBC shall, for purposes of the exculpation, advancement, and indemnification rights of our directors and officers, constitute an act or omission not in good faith, or a breach of the duty of loyalty.

p1871: We have four classes of authorized common stock:
p1872: • the class designated as Participating Common Stock, which is divided into two series: Class A common stock and Class N common stock;
p1873: • Class T common stock, which is a special class of common stock that is issued to the LTBT;
p1874: • Class F common stock, which is a special class of common stock that will be issued to the Founder LLC; and
p1875: • Class E common stock, which is a special class of common stock that will be issued to our employees, excluding our co-founders.
p1876: • Class A common stock. Holders of our Class A common stock are entitled to one vote for each share held on all matters submitted to a vote of stockholders generally, including the election of the directors other than the Class T directors.
p1877: • Class N common stock. Holders of our Class N common stock are not entitled to vote on any matter that is submitted to a vote of stockholders, except as otherwise required by law, such as certain amendments to our amended and restated certificate of incorporation that would adversely affect the powers, preferences, or special rights of our Class N common stock without so adversely affecting our Class A common stock, on which the DGCL entitles such holders to vote separately as a series.
p1878: • Class T common stock. The holder of our Class T common stock has no voting rights with respect to matters submitted to stockholders, except as set forth within our amended and restated certificate of incorporation with respect to the election of a majority of our board of directors, the redemption of our Class E common stock, certain amendments to the rights of our Class F common stock, or as otherwise required by law, such as certain amendments to our amended and restated certificate of incorporation that would adversely affect the powers, preferences, or special rights of our Class T common stock, on which the DGCL entitles such holders to vote separately as a class.
p1879: • Class F common stock. The holder of our Class F common stock will be entitled to an aggregate number of votes that equals 50.1% of the total voting power of our outstanding shares of capital stock as of the applicable record date on matters submitted to a vote of stockholders generally, including the election of the directors other than the Class T directors. Our Class F common stock will be voted in the manner provided by the Founder LLC Agreement. See the section titled “—Class F Common Stock Voting Mechanics.”
p1880: • Class E common stock. The holders of our Class E common stock have no voting rights with respect to matters submitted to stockholders, except as set forth within our amended and restated certificate of incorporation with respect to the proposed nomination, removal, or change in designation of the Specified Class T Director (in circumstances where our NGC does not concur with the LTBT’s proposed action), certain changes to the terms of the LTBT, the rights of our Class T common stock, the redemption of our Class T common stock, or as otherwise required by law, such as certain amendments to our amended and restated certificate of incorporation that would adversely affect the powers, preferences, or special rights of our Class E common stock, on which the DGCL entitles such holders to vote separately as a class.
p1881: • Class A common stock. Our Class A common stock will not be convertible into any other class or series of capital stock. Subject to compliance with applicable law and the restrictions described in the section titled “Shares Eligible for Future Sale—Lock-Up and Market Standoff Agreements,” our Class A common stock can be transferred.
p1882: • Class N common stock. The holders of our Class N common stock are primarily strategic business partners. Subject to compliance with applicable law and the restrictions described in the section titled “Shares Eligible for Future Sale—Lock-Up and Market Standoff Agreements,” our Class N common stock can be transferred. The shares of Class N common stock will automatically convert into an equal number of shares of Class A common stock upon a transfer effected through: (i) a registered offering or an open market sale of such shares or (ii) a transfer to a third party (A) that is not a holder of Class N common stock (or an affiliate of a holder of Class N common stock) and (B) that will not beneficially own or control more than 9.99% of the shares of any class or series of our equity securities after giving effect to the transfer.
p1883: • Class T common stock. Our Class T common stock will not be convertible into any other class or series of capital stock. Our Class T common stock is transferable only upon the approval of persons comprising the Trust Amendment Threshold. Because the persons comprising the Trust Amendment Threshold have the power to modify or terminate the LTBT and the rights of our Class T common stock entirely, there is no separate restriction on the identity of a permissible transferee of our Class T common stock.
p1884: • Class F common stock. Our Class F common stock will not be convertible into any other class or series of capital stock. Our Class F common stock is not transferable except in the case of a reorganization or redomiciliation of the Founder LLC that is approved by our board of directors and does not result in a change to the members of the Founder LLC.
p1885: • Class E common stock. Our Class E common stock will not be convertible into any other class or series of capital stock and is not transferable.
p1886: • Class A common stock. Our Class A common stock will not be redeemable at our option or at the option of the holder.
p1887: • Class N common stock. Our Class N common stock will not be redeemable at our option or at the option of the holder.
p1888: • Class T common stock. Our Class T common stock will be redeemable for no consideration:
p1889: ◦ if the Trustees are voting in favor of such redemption, upon approval of 80% of the authorized members of our board of directors and 80% of the Trustees then in office (in each case, rounded up or down to the nearest whole number (any exact 0.5 rounding up));
p1890: ◦ if our Class F common stock remains outstanding and the Trustees are not voting in favor of such redemption:
p1891: • until the third anniversary of the completion of this offering, upon approval by (i) our Class F common stock acting pursuant to the unanimous approval of the Continuing Founders, (ii) a majority of the votes cast by our Class E common stock (subject to a quorum of 40% of the outstanding Class E common stock), and (iii) a majority of the votes cast by our outstanding Class A common stock (subject to a quorum of a majority of outstanding Class A common stock); or
p1892: • at any time, upon approval by (i) our Class F common stock acting by decision of 66 2/3% of the Continuing Founders (rounded up to the nearest whole number), (ii) 75% of the votes cast by our Class E common stock (subject to a quorum of a majority of outstanding Class E common stock), and (iii) a majority of the votes cast by our Class A common stock (subject to a quorum of a majority of outstanding Class A common stock); or
p1893: ◦ if no Class F common stock remains outstanding and the Trustees are not voting in favor of such redemption, upon approval of 85% of the outstanding shares of Class A common stock.
p1894: • Class F common stock. Our Class F common stock will be redeemable for no consideration (i) at the option of the Founder LLC, acting upon Supermajority approval of the Continuing Founders, (ii) upon the dissolution of the Founder LLC, or (iii) upon completion of the Class F Transition Period, which will commence when there have been fewer than three Continuing Founders (not including any successor member who is a “Non-Qualifying Member” as defined in the Founder LLC Agreement) for 90 consecutive calendar days.
p1895: • Class E common stock. Our Class E common stock will not be redeemable at the option of the holder. Following an employee’s separation from employment with us other than for cause, one-half of such employee’s then-outstanding shares of Class E common stock will be automatically redeemed by us for no consideration annually, except that all shares of Class E common stock held by an employee will also be automatically redeemed by us for no consideration upon such employee’s death, incapacity, termination for cause, or commencement of service with a direct competitor. All shares of Class E common stock will also be automatically redeemed by us for no consideration (i) at such time as no Class F common stock remains outstanding, or (ii) upon the approval of (A) 80% of authorized members of our board of directors (rounded up or down to the nearest whole number (any exact 0.5 rounding up)), (B) the holder of our Class F common stock, and (C) the holder of our Class T common stock.
p1896: Subject to preferences that may apply to any shares of preferred stock outstanding at the time, the holders of our Class A common stock and Class N common stock are entitled to receive dividends out of funds legally available if our board of directors, in its discretion, determines to issue dividends and then only at the times and in the amounts that our board of directors may determine. Our Class T common stock, Class F common stock, and Class E common stock are not entitled to receive dividends. See the section titled “Dividend Policy” for more information.
p1897: Our common stock is not entitled to preemptive rights and is not subject to redemption or sinking fund provisions (other than those providing for the redemption of our Class T common stock, Class F common stock, and Class E common stock for no consideration described above).
p1898: If we become subject to a liquidation, dissolution, or winding-up, the assets legally available for distribution to our stockholders would be distributable ratably among the holders of our Class A common stock and Class N common stock and any participating preferred stock outstanding at that time, subject to prior satisfaction of all outstanding debt and liabilities and the preferential rights of and the payment of liquidation preferences, if any, on any outstanding shares of our capital stock. In the event of our liquidation, dissolution, or winding-up, holders of our Class T common stock, Class F common stock, and Class E common stock shall be entitled to receive par value ($0.00001) per share but shall not otherwise participate in such distributions.

p1909: After the completion of this offering, no shares of our preferred stock will be outstanding. Pursuant to our amended and restated certificate of incorporation that will become effective immediately prior to the completion of this offering, our board of directors (if 80% of the authorized members of our board of directors (rounded up or down to the nearest whole number (any exact 0.5 rounding up)) approve) will have the authority, subject to limitations set forth in such amended and restated certificate of incorporation or prescribed by Delaware law, to issue preferred stock in one or more series, to establish from time to time the number of shares to be included in each series and to fix the designation, powers, preferences, and rights of the shares of each series and any of its qualifications, limitations, or restrictions, in each case without further vote or action by our stockholders; provided that prior to the Class F Sunset Time, our board of directors shall not designate or issue any series of preferred stock without the affirmative vote or consent of the Founder LLC. Our board of directors (if 80% of the authorized members of our board of directors (rounded up or down to the nearest whole number (any exact 0.5 rounding up)) approve) can also increase or decrease the number of shares of any series of preferred stock, but not below the number of shares of that series then outstanding, without any further vote or action by our stockholders. Subject to limitations set forth in our amended and restated certificate of incorporation that will become effective immediately prior to the completion of this offering, or prescribed by Delaware law, we may authorize the issuance of preferred stock with voting or conversion rights that could adversely affect the voting power or other rights of the holders of our common stock, including the likelihood that such holders will receive dividend payments and payments upon liquidation. If we were to issue shares of preferred stock with the right to vote on matters submitted to our stockholders generally, the voting power of our outstanding Class A common stock would be diluted, while the voting power of our Class F common stock would remain fixed at an aggregate of 50.1% of the total voting power of our outstanding shares of capital stock as of the applicable record date with respect to such matters. The issuance of preferred stock, while providing flexibility in connection with possible acquisitions and other corporate purposes, could, among other things, have the effect of delaying, deferring or preventing a change in control of our company and might adversely affect the market price of our Class A common stock and the voting and other rights of the holders of our Class A common stock. We have no current plan to issue any shares of preferred stock.
