p1912: After the completion of this offering, certain holders of our Class A common stock (including those issuable upon conversion of our Class N common stock) will be entitled to rights with respect to the registration of their shares under the Securities Act. These registration rights are contained in our IRA. We and certain holders of our stock are parties to our IRA. In addition, we are party to separate registration rights agreements with each of Google (the “Google RRA”) and Broadcom (the “Infrastructure Partner RRA”) that we entered into in connection with note purchase agreements with those parties, which provide Google and Broadcom with registration rights separate from the registration rights under our IRA, as described below under “Registration Rights of Google” and “Registration Rights of Broadcom.” The registration rights set forth in our IRA will expire upon the earliest to occur of (i) the second anniversary of the date of completion of this offering, (ii) with respect to any particular holder, when such stockholder is able to sell all of its shares pursuant to Rule 144 of the Securities Act or any similar exemption during any three-month period, or (iii) the termination of our IRA. We will pay the registration expenses (other than underwriting discounts and commissions) of the holders of the shares registered pursuant to the registrations described below. In an underwritten offering, the managing underwriter, if any, has the right, subject to specified conditions, to limit the number of shares such holders may include. The registration rights described in this section do not entitle any holder to notice of, or to include shares in, this offering. The exercise of these registration rights is subject to the lock-up agreements described in the section titled “Shares Eligible for Future Sale—Lock-Up and Market Standoff Agreements.”
p1913: After the completion of this offering, the holders of up to shares of our Class A common stock (including those issuable upon conversion of our Class N common stock) will be entitled to certain demand registration rights. At any time beginning six months after the effective date of this offering, the holders of at least 60% of the shares registrable under our IRA that are entitled to vote can request that we register the offer and sale of their shares. Such a request for registration must cover securities, the anticipated aggregate offering price of which, net of underwriting discounts and commissions, is at least $200,000,000. We are obligated to effect only two such registrations. If we determine that it would be seriously detrimental to us and our stockholders to effect such a demand registration, we have the right to defer such registration, not more than twice in any 12- month period, for a period of up to 120 days. Additionally, we will not be required to effect a demand registration during the period beginning 90 days prior to our good faith estimate of the date of filing of, and ending on a date 90 days following the effective date of, a registration statement relating to an offering by us (or, in the case of this offering, ending on a date 180 days following the effective date of this registration statement), provided that we are actively employing in good faith all reasonable efforts to cause such registration statement to become effective. We are also not obligated to effect a demand registration if the initiating holders propose to dispose of shares that may be immediately registered on Form S-3 pursuant to the Form S-3 registration rights described below.
p1914: After the completion of this offering, if we propose to register the offer and sale of our Class A common stock (including shares issuable upon conversion of our Class N common stock) under the Securities Act, in connection with the public offering of such Class A common stock the holders of up to shares of our Class A common stock will be entitled to certain “piggyback” registration rights allowing the holders to include their shares in such registration, subject to certain marketing and other limitations and the registration rights of lenders under our convertible note agreements, which consist of the Google RRA and the Infrastructure Partner RRA described below. As a result, whenever we propose to file a registration statement under the Securities Act, other than with respect to (i) a registration related to any employee benefit plan or a corporate reorganization or other transaction covered by Rule 145 promulgated under the Securities Act, (ii) a registration on any registration form which does not include substantially the same information as would be required to be included in a registration statement covering the sale of the shares, or (iii) a registration in which the only Class A common stock being registered is Class A common stock issuable upon conversion of debt securities that are also being registered, the holders of these shares are entitled to notice of the registration and have the right, subject to certain limitations and/or cutbacks, to include their shares in the registration. If the underwriters limit the number of shares to be included in an underwritten offering, the number of registrable shares included may not be reduced below 20% of the total securities included in the offering, and shares held by our cofounders may not be included if any registrable shares held by other selling holders are excluded.
p1915: After the completion of this offering, the holders of up to shares of our Class A common stock (including those issuable upon conversion of our Class N common stock) will be entitled to certain Form S-3 registration rights. The holders of at least 60% of the shares registrable under our IRA that are entitled to vote may make a written request that we register the offer and sale of their shares on a registration statement on Form S-3 if we are eligible to file a registration statement on Form S-3 so long as the request covers securities the anticipated aggregate public offering price of which is at least $2,000,000, net of any underwriters’ discounts or commissions. These stockholders may make an unlimited number of requests for registration on Form S-3; however, we will not be required to effect a registration on Form S-3 if we have effected two such registrations within the 12-month period preceding the date of the request. Additionally, if we determine that it would be seriously detrimental to us and our stockholders to effect such a registration, we have the right to defer such registration, not more than once in any 12-month period, for a period of up to 120 days. We are also not required to effect a registration on Form S-3 during the period ending 180 days after the effective date of a registration statement subject to the piggyback registration rights described above.
p1916: We entered into the Google RRA in May 2026 in connection with our Google 2026 NPA, pursuant to which Google may acquire shares of our capital stock. Under the Google RRA, shares of our capital stock held by Google that are not covered by the registration rights under our IRA are registrable, subject to customary exceptions. During the one-year period following the effective date of the registration statement of which this prospectus forms a part, Google may make a single demand that we register the resale of all of its registrable shares that are not then salable pursuant to Rule 144. In addition, once we are eligible to use Form S-3, we are required to register on Form S-3, within 60 days of each quarterly closing under the Google 2026 NPA, the resale of the registrable shares acquired at such closing and of any registrable shares not previously registered, and to keep such registrations effective for so long as Google holds registrable shares. Registrations under the Google RRA are subject to customary deferral and blackout provisions, and Google may not exercise its registration rights under the Google RRA after February 7, 2033 or, if earlier, the date that is 12 months following the final quarterly closing under the Google 2026 NPA.
p1917: We entered into the Infrastructure Partner RRA in June 2026 in connection with the Infrastructure Partner 2026 NPA that may be assigned by Broadcom, subject to our consent (not to be unreasonably withheld), to a designated financial partner, pursuant to which we may issue convertible promissory notes to Broadcom or a designated financial partner. Registrable shares under the Infrastructure Partner RRA generally consist of the shares of our Class A common stock issuable upon conversion of our Class N common stock issued upon conversion of the notes, subject to customary exceptions. Once we are eligible to use Form S-3, we are required to file, within 60 days, a shelf registration statement covering resales of these registrable shares, and to keep it effective and effect takedowns at the request of the holder of these shares for so long as these registrable shares are held. The holder of these registrable shares also has demand registration rights following the listing of our securities, limited to one demand registration for every $5.0 billion of notes issued and subject to a $500,000,000 minimum offering size (unless the holder of these registrable shares is selling all of its remaining registrable shares), and piggyback registration rights subject to exceptions substantially similar to those described above with respect to our IRA. The holder of these registrable shares may effect up to three underwritten offerings, including block trades, in any 12-month period, subject to the same $500,000,000 minimum, and registrations under the Infrastructure Partner RRA are subject to customary deferral and blackout provisions. If the underwriters impose a cutback in an underwritten offering, shares held by our cofounders will not be included if any shares held by the holder of these registrable shares are excluded. If we grant registration rights to other securityholders, or amend their existing registration rights, on terms more favorable than those provided to the holder of these registrable shares, we must offer to amend the rights of the holder of these registrable shares to be at least as favorable, and the holder of these registrable shares is entitled to proportionate treatment if lock-up or similar restrictions are waived for other stockholders in connection with a registration, in each case subject to specified exceptions. The Infrastructure Partner RRA terminates upon the earlier of the date on which the holder of these registrable shares and its permitted transferees no longer hold registrable shares and the date that is nine months after the latest maturity date of any outstanding note issued under the Infrastructure Partner 2026 NPA. As of the date of this prospectus, no notes have been issued under the Infrastructure Partner 2026 NPA and, accordingly, no registrable securities are outstanding under the Infrastructure Partner RRA.
p1918: Certain provisions of Delaware law, our amended and restated certificate of incorporation and our amended and restated bylaws, which will become effective immediately prior to the completion of this offering, which are summarized below, may have the effect of delaying, deferring, or discouraging another person from acquiring control of us. They are also designed, in part, to encourage persons seeking to acquire control of us to negotiate first with our board of directors. We believe that the benefits of increased protection of our potential ability to negotiate with an unsolicited acquirer outweigh the disadvantages of discouraging a proposal to acquire us because negotiation of these proposals could result in an improvement of their terms.
p1919: We have elected not to be governed by the provisions of Section 203 of the DGCL, prior to the later to occur of the Class F Sunset Time and the Class T Sunset Time, but our amended and restated certificate of incorporation will provide that the restrictions contained in Section 203 will apply to us immediately following the later to occur of either the Class F Sunset Time or the Class T Sunset Time. Following the later to occur of the Class F Sunset Time or the Class T Sunset Time, we will thereafter be governed by Section 203, which generally prohibits a public Delaware corporation from engaging in a “business combination” with an “interested stockholder” for a period of three years after the date of the transaction in which the person became an interested stockholder, unless:
p1920: • the business combination or transaction which resulted in the stockholder becoming an interested stockholder was approved by the board of directors prior to the time that the stockholder became an interested stockholder;
p1921: • upon consummation of the transaction which resulted in the stockholder becoming an interested stockholder, the interested stockholder owned at least 85% in voting power of the voting stock of the corporation outstanding at the time the transaction commenced, excluding shares owned by directors who are also officers of the corporation and shares owned by employee stock plans in which employee participants do not have the right to determine confidentially whether shares held subject to the plan will be tendered in a tender or exchange offer; or
p1922: • at or subsequent to the time the stockholder became an interested stockholder, the business combination was approved by the board of directors and authorized at an annual or special meeting of the stockholders, and not by written consent, by the affirmative vote of at least two-thirds of the outstanding voting stock which is not owned by the interested stockholder.
p1923: In general, Section 203 defines a “business combination” to include mergers, asset sales, and other transactions resulting in financial benefit to a stockholder and an “interested stockholder” as a person who, together with affiliates and associates, owns, or is an affiliate or associate of the corporation and within three years did own, 15% or more in voting power of the corporation’s outstanding voting stock.
p1924: Our amended and restated certificate of incorporation and our amended and restated bylaws, which will become effective immediately prior to the completion of this offering, will include a number of provisions that could deter hostile takeovers or delay or prevent changes in control of our board of directors or management team, including but not limited to the following:
p1925: As described above in the section titled “—Common Stock—Voting Rights,” our amended and restated certificate of incorporation provides for a multi-class common stock structure. Under this governance structure, we expect that the LTBT and the Founder LLC will collectively have the ability to elect all members of our board of directors, and the Founder LLC will have the ability to determine the outcome of all matters submitted to a vote of our stockholders generally for the foreseeable future, including the approval by our stockholders of significant corporate transactions such as a merger or other sale of our company or its assets. Such transactions also require approval of our board of directors, a majority of whom are elected by the LTBT. Holders of our Class A common stock generally will not be able to affect the outcome of any matter submitted to a vote of our stockholders or the election of our directors, regardless of how they vote, unless a majority of the Continuing Founders cannot agree on how our Class F common stock will be voted (in which case our Class F common stock will generally be voted proportionately with the votes of our Class A common stock cast on the matter).
p1926: Our amended and restated certificate of incorporation that will become effective immediately prior to the completion of this offering will provide that prior to the Class F Sunset Time, we will not have a classified board of directors, and all directors will be elected for annual terms. Each director’s term will continue until the next annual meeting and until the election and qualification of his or her successor, or his or her earlier death, resignation, or removal.
p1927: Following the Class F Sunset Time, our board of directors will shift to having a classified board of directors consisting of three classes of approximately equal size, each serving staggered three-year terms. At such time, our directors would be assigned by the then-current board of directors to a class. If our Class T common stock remains outstanding, the Class T directors and the remaining directors shall be allocated among the classes so that each class includes a proportionate number of Class T directors and other directors. Upon expiration of the term of a class of directors, directors for that class would each be elected for a three-year term at the annual meeting of stockholders in the year in which that term expires. As a result, only one class of directors would be elected at each annual meeting of our stockholders, with the other classes continuing for the remainder of their respective three-year terms. Each director’s term would continue until the third annual meeting of stockholders following their election and until his or her successor has been elected and qualified, or until his or her earlier death, resignation, or removal. Any increase or decrease in the number of directors would be distributed among the three classes so that, as nearly as practicable, each class would consist of one-third of our directors.
p1928: Our amended and restated certificate of incorporation and amended and restated bylaws will provide that (i) prior to the Class T Sunset Time, only the holder of our Class T common stock can fill vacant directorships of any Class T director, subject to the nomination procedures for the Specified Class T Director; and (ii) prior to the Class F Sunset Time, vacant or newly created directorships for any directors other than our Class T directors can be filled by (a) our board of directors, in accordance with, and following receipt of written notice from, the Founder LLC recommending the person proposed to fill such director seat or (b) the holders of our Class A common stock and Class F common stock, voting together or acting by written consent. Following the Class F Sunset Time, only our board of directors will be permitted to fill vacant or newly created directorships for any directors other than our Class T directors. Prior to the Class T Sunset Time, the number of directors constituting our board of directors will be permitted to be set only with the approval of 80% of authorized members of our board of directors (rounded up or down to the nearest whole number (any exact 0.5 rounding up)); provided that until the earlier to occur of the Class F Sunset Time or the Class T Sunset Time, such total number of authorized directors must be an odd number. Following the Class T Sunset Time, the number of directors constituting our board of directors will be permitted to be set with the approval of a majority of the authorized members of our board of directors. These provisions would prevent a stockholder from increasing the size of our board of directors and then gaining control of our board of directors by filling the resulting vacancies with its own nominees. This will make it more difficult to change the composition of our board of directors.
p1929: Our amended and restated bylaws will provide advance notice procedures for stockholders, other than holders of Class T common stock or Class F common stock nominating directors in accordance with nomination procedures in our certificate of incorporation or the Stockholders’ Agreement, seeking to bring business before our annual meeting of stockholders or to nominate candidates for election as directors at a meeting of stockholders. Our amended and restated bylaws will also specify certain requirements regarding the form and content of a stockholder’s notice. These provisions might preclude our stockholders from bringing matters before our annual meeting of stockholders or from making nominations for directors at a meeting of stockholders if the proper procedures are not followed. In addition, our NGC will also have the right to receive 30 days’ prior written notice of any nomination of persons to serve as a director by the LTBT or the Founder LLC or the proposed removal of such directors, as well as appointments and removals of the Trustees of the LTBT. Our NGC may waive such notice periods in its discretion. We expect that these provisions may also discourage or deter a potential acquirer from conducting a solicitation of proxies to elect the acquirer’s own slate of directors or otherwise attempting to obtain control of our company.
p1930: Our amended and restated certificate of incorporation and amended and restated bylaws will provide that special meetings of stockholders may be called only by (i) our board of directors acting pursuant to a resolution adopted by a majority of the authorized members of our board of directors; (ii) the chairperson of our board of directors; (iii) our Chief Executive Officer; (iv) our President; (v) following the Class F Sunset Time, a majority of the directors who are not Class T directors; (vi) prior to the Class F Sunset Time and only with respect to a special meeting at which holders of our Class E common stock will be asked to vote on a proposal, the secretary of the company; or (vii) prior to the Class F Sunset Time, the Founder LLC as the holder of our Class F common stock.
p1931: The DGCL provides that stockholders are not entitled to cumulate votes in the election of directors unless a corporation’s certificate of incorporation provides otherwise. Our amended and restated certificate of incorporation does not provide for cumulative voting.
p1932: Prior to the Class F Sunset Time and the Class T Sunset Time, stockholders may act by written consent only with respect to (i) any action to nominate, elect, or remove directors or appoint a director to fill any vacancy or newly created directorship; (ii) any action to satisfy certain redemption and protective provisions in our amended and restated certificate of incorporation related to our Class F common stock, Class T common stock, and Class E common stock; and (iii) any matter in which stockholders vote together as a single class if such matter is first approved or requested by our board of directors. From and after the Class T Sunset Time, only the holder of the share of Class F common stock may act by written consent, and from and after the Class F Sunset Time, only the holder of the share of Class T common stock may act by written consent, in each case, only with respect to the actions described above. From and after the occurrence of both the Class F Sunset Time and the Class T Sunset Time, any action required or permitted to be taken by the stockholders must be effected at a duly called annual or special meeting of stockholders and may not be effected by any consent in writing by such stockholders. Notwithstanding the foregoing, any action required or permitted to be taken by the holders of Class E common stock must be effected at a duly called annual or special meeting of stockholders and may not be effected by any consent in writing by such stockholders.
p1933: Prior to the Class F Sunset Time, a majority of the voting power of our Class A common stock and Class F common stock, voting together as a single class, can amend certain provisions in our amended and restated certificate of incorporation and our amended and restated bylaws. Following the Class F Sunset Time, 66 2/3% of the voting power of our Class A common stock can amend certain provisions in our amended and restated certificate of incorporation and our amended and restated bylaws.
p1934: Subject to limitations in our amended and restated certificate of incorporation, which will become effective immediately prior to the completion of this offering, or prescribed by Delaware law, our board of directors will have the authority, if 80% of the authorized members of our board of directors (rounded up or down to the nearest whole number (any exact 0.5 rounding up)) approve, and without further action by our stockholders, to issue up to 30,000,000,000 shares of undesignated preferred stock with rights and preferences, including voting rights, designated from time to time by our board of directors, provided that, prior to the Class F Sunset Time, our board of directors shall not designate or issue any series of preferred stock without the affirmative vote or consent of the Founder LLC. The existence of authorized but unissued shares of preferred stock would enable our board of directors to render more difficult or to discourage an attempt to obtain control of us by means of a merger, tender offer, proxy contest, or other means.
p1935: Our amended and restated bylaws, which will become effective immediately prior to the completion of this offering, will provide that, unless we consent in writing to the selection of an alternative forum, the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware (or, if the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware does not have jurisdiction, another State court in Delaware or the federal district court for the District of Delaware) will, to the fullest extent permitted by law, be the sole and exclusive forum for (i) any derivative action or proceeding brought on our behalf, (ii) any action asserting a claim of breach of a fiduciary duty owed by any of our current or former directors, stockholders, or officers or other employees to us or our stockholders, (iii) any action arising pursuant to any provision of the DGCL or as to which the DGCL confers jurisdiction upon the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware, (iv) any action arising pursuant to or to interpret, apply, enforce or determine the validity of our amended and restated certificate of incorporation, or our amended and restated bylaws, or (v) any action asserting a claim governed by the internal affairs doctrine, except for, in all cases, any claim as to which such court determines that there is an indispensable party not subject to the jurisdiction of such court (and the indispensable party does not consent to the personal jurisdiction of such court within 10 days following such determination).
p1936: Section 22 of the Securities Act establishes concurrent jurisdiction for federal and state courts over Securities Act claims. Accordingly, both state and federal courts have jurisdiction to hear such claims. To prevent having to litigate claims in multiple jurisdictions and the threat of inconsistent or contrary rulings by different courts, among other considerations, our amended and restated bylaws will also provide that, unless we consent in writing to the selection of an alternative forum, the federal district courts of the United States will, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, be the sole and exclusive forum for resolving any complaint asserting a cause or causes of action arising under the Securities Act against any person in connection with any offering of our securities, including, without limitation, any auditor, underwriter, expert, control person, or other defendant. Unless we consent in writing to the selection of an alternative forum, the United States District Court for the District of Delaware will, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, be the sole and exclusive forum for the resolution of any derivative action or proceeding brought to enforce any duty or liability created by the Exchange Act or the rules or regulations thereunder. All other claims arising under the Exchange Act may be brought in any federal court of competent jurisdiction. Any person or entity purchasing, holding, or otherwise acquiring any interest in our securities shall be deemed to have notice of and consented to these provisions. We note that stockholders cannot waive compliance (or consent to non-compliance) with the federal securities laws and the rules and regulations thereunder.
p1937: Our co-founders intend to enter into the Founder LLC Agreement. We expect the Founder LLC Agreement to become effective substantially concurrently with the filing and acceptance of our amended and restated certificate of incorporation with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware.
p1938: Our Class F common stock will be held by the Founder LLC. Our Class F common stock will be voted by the Founder LLC in a manner determined pursuant to the Founder LLC Agreement. Generally, the Founder LLC will vote as determined by a majority of the Continuing Founders. Our seven co-founders will each initially be a Continuing Founder. Upon the incapacity or death of any of our co-founders, a successor member may be admitted to the Founder LLC as a Continuing Founder until the tenth anniversary of the completion of this offering.
p1939: When there have been fewer than three Continuing Founders (not including any successor member who is a “Non-Qualifying Member” as defined in the Founder LLC Agreement) for 90 consecutive calendar days, the 450-day Class F Transition Period will commence. Upon completion of the Class F Transition Period, all of our Class F common stock and Class E common stock then issued and outstanding will be redeemed by us for no consideration and certain other governance changes will take effect.
p1940: Regardless of the length of time that has elapsed since the completion of this offering or the circumstances that resulted in the removal of a Continuing Founder, one or more successor members may be admitted to the Founder LLC during the Class F Transition Period as needed to ensure that there are three Continuing Founders serving until completion of the Class F Transition Period. The admission of any successor member during the Class F Transition Period will not cure the event that commenced the Class F Transition Period or extend the Class F Transition Period.
p1941: A Continuing Founder will be removed from the Founder LLC upon the earliest to occur of (i) such Continuing Founder’s resignation as a member of the Founder LLC; (ii) such Continuing Founder’s death or incapacity; (iii) with respect to each of our seven original co-founders, such original co-founder’s ceasing to hold (together with such original co-founder’s related holders) on any record date for a vote of our stockholders a number of shares of Class A common stock (including shares subject to options, RSUs, and other convertible securities) equal to at least 2% of the shares of Class A common stock held by such original co-founder and their related holders as of the completion of this offering; (iv) such Continuing Founder’s removal for “cause” (as defined in the Founder LLC Agreement), which includes specified competitive activities described in the Founder LLC Agreement; (v) with respect to any successor member admitted to the Founder LLC prior to the commencement of the Class F Transition Period, other than a successor member who is a member during the Class F Transition Period, the tenth anniversary of the completion of this offering; or (vi) with respect to each of our seven original co-founders, the commencement of a leave of absence approved by a Supermajority of the other Continuing Founders, which may not be approved during the Class F Transition Period or if the grant of the leave of absence would itself cause the Class F Transition Period to commence.
p1942: Each Continuing Founder will be entitled to one vote when determining how our Class F common stock will be voted. If a majority of the Continuing Founders cannot agree on how our Class F common stock will be voted, then our Class F common stock will generally be voted proportionately with the votes of our Class A common stock cast on the matter (subject to a quorum of a majority of outstanding Class A common stock). With respect to certain matters, our Class F common stock will be voted “for” the proposal only if a greater threshold of Continuing Founders agree, and if the greater threshold is not met, our Class F common stock will be voted “against” the proposal. See the section titled “—Class F Common Stock Voting Mechanics.”
p1943: The Founder LLC Agreement will not govern the voting of any shares of our Class A common stock held by the co-founders or their related holders. Each co-founder (or their related holders) will be able to vote shares of our Class A common stock held by them in their discretion, regardless of the manner in which the Founder LLC will vote our Class F common stock.

p2014: Distributions on our Class A common stock will constitute dividends for U.S. federal income tax purposes to the extent paid from our current or accumulated earnings and profits, as determined under U.S. federal income tax principles. To the extent those distributions exceed both our current and our accumulated earnings and profits, the excess will constitute a return of capital and will first reduce your basis in our Class A common stock, but not below zero, and then will be treated as gain from the sale or other disposition of stock as described below under the section titled “—Gain on Disposition of Our Class A Common Stock.”
p2015: Except as otherwise described below in the paragraph on effectively connected income and the sections titled “—Backup Withholding and Information Reporting” and “—FATCA,” any dividend paid to you will generally be subject to U.S. federal withholding tax either at a rate of 30% of the gross amount of the dividend or such lower rate as may be specified by an applicable income tax treaty between the United States and your country of residence. Under applicable Treasury regulations, the applicable withholding agent may withhold up to 30% of the gross amount of the entire distribution even if the amount constituting a dividend, as described above, is less than such amount. If we or another withholding agent over-withhold or if you do not timely provide us with the required certification, you may be entitled to a refund or credit of any excess amounts withheld by timely filing an appropriate claim with the Internal Revenue Service (“IRS”).
p2016: In order to receive a reduced treaty rate, you must provide the applicable withholding agent with an IRS Form W-8BEN, IRS Form W-8BEN-E, or other appropriate version of IRS Form W-8, including any required attachments and your taxpayer identification number, certifying qualification for the reduced rate. Additionally, you will be required to update such forms and certifications from time to time as required by law. If you are eligible for a reduced rate of U.S. withholding tax pursuant to an income tax treaty, you may obtain a refund of any excess amounts withheld by timely filing an appropriate claim for refund with the IRS. If you hold our stock through a financial institution or other agent acting on your behalf, you will be required to provide appropriate documentation to the agent, which then will be required to provide certification to us or our paying agent, either directly or through other intermediaries. You should consult your tax advisor regarding entitlement to benefits under any applicable income tax treaties.
p2017: Dividends received by you that are effectively connected with your conduct of a U.S. trade or business (and, if required by an applicable income tax treaty, that are attributable to a permanent establishment or fixed base maintained by you in the United States) are generally exempt from such withholding tax, subject to the discussions below on backup withholding and FATCA (as defined below) withholding. To obtain this exemption, you must provide us with an IRS Form W-8ECI, including any required attachments and your taxpayer identification number, certifying qualification for the exemption. Additionally, you will be required to update such forms and certifications from time to time as required by law. Such effectively connected dividends, although not subject to U.S. federal withholding tax, are includable on your U.S. federal income tax return and taxed to you at the same rates applicable to U.S. persons, net of certain deductions and credits. If you are a corporate non-U.S. holder, dividends you receive that are effectively connected with your conduct of a U.S. trade or business may also be subject to a branch profits tax at a rate of 30% or such lower rate as may be specified by an applicable income tax treaty between the United States and your country of residence. p2022: Generally, a corporation is a USRPHC if the fair market value of its U.S. real property interests equals or exceeds 50% of the sum of the fair market value of its worldwide property interests and its other assets used or held for use in a trade or business (all as determined for U.S. federal income tax purposes). p2028: Sections 1471 through 1474 of the Code, and the Treasury regulations and administrative guidance issued thereunder (collectively, “FATCA”), generally impose a U.S. federal withholding tax at a rate of 30% on dividends on and, subject to certain proposed Treasury regulations discussed below, the gross proceeds from a sale or other disposition of our Class A common stock if paid to a “foreign financial institution” (as defined in the Code), unless otherwise provided by the Treasury Secretary or such institution enters into an agreement with the U.S. government to withhold on certain payments and to collect and provide to the U.S. tax authorities substantial information regarding the U.S. account holders of such institution (which includes certain equity and debt holders of such institution, as well as certain account holders that are non-U.S. entities with U.S. owners) or otherwise establishes an exemption. FATCA also generally imposes a U.S. federal withholding tax of 30% on dividends paid on and, subject to certain proposed Treasury regulations discussed below, the gross proceeds from a sale or other disposition of our Class A common stock if paid to a “non-financial foreign entity” (as defined in the Code) unless otherwise provided by the Treasury Secretary or such entity provides the withholding agent with a certification identifying, and information with respect to certain direct and indirect “substantial United States owners” (as defined in the Code) of the entity, certifies that it does not have any such substantial United States owners or otherwise establishes and certifies to an exemption. The withholding provisions under FATCA generally apply to dividends on our Class A common stock. The Treasury Secretary has issued proposed regulations providing that the withholding provisions under FATCA do not apply with respect to the gross proceeds from a sale or other disposition of our Class A common stock, which may be relied upon by taxpayers until final regulations are issued. An intergovernmental agreement between the United States and your country of tax residence may modify the requirements described in this paragraph. You should consult your own tax advisors regarding the possible implications of FATCA on your investment in our Class A common stock.

p2075: In order to facilitate the offering of our Class A common stock, Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC, acting as stabilization agent on behalf of the underwriters, may engage in transactions that stabilize, maintain, or otherwise affect the price of our Class A common stock. Specifically, the underwriter may sell more shares of Class A common stock than the underwriters are obligated to purchase under the underwriting agreement, creating a short position. A short sale is covered if the short position is no greater than the number of shares available for purchase under the over-allotment option. The underwriter can close out a covered short sale by exercising the over-allotment option or purchasing shares in the open market. In determining the source of shares to close out a covered short sale, the underwriter will consider, among other things, the open market price of our Class A common stock compared to the price available under the over-allotment option. The underwriter may also sell shares of Class A common stock in excess of the over-allotment option, creating a naked short position. The underwriter must close out any naked short position by purchasing shares of Class A common stock in the open market. A naked short position is more likely to be created if the underwriter is concerned that there may be downward pressure on the price of our Class A common stock in the open market after pricing that could adversely affect investors who purchase shares of Class A common stock in this offering.

The underwriter is not required to engage in these activities and may end any of these activities at any time.

p2165: Loss Contingencies Description As further described in Note 13 to the consolidated financial statements, the Company is of the involved in various legal claims, proceedings and other regulatory and administrative Matter proceedings, certain of which may include claims for substantial or indeterminate amounts of damages. The Company’s assessment of loss contingency matters requires significant judgment in determining both the likelihood and estimated amount of potential losses.
p2166: Auditing the Company’s accounting for and disclosure of certain loss contingencies was especially challenging due to the significant judgment required to evaluate management’s assessments of the probability of loss and its estimate of the potential amounts or range of such losses. How We We performed audit procedures that included, among others, obtaining an Addressed understanding of the identification and evaluation of loss contingencies, including the the Matter Company’s assessment of the likelihood that a loss will be incurred and its ability to in Our reasonably estimate the loss or range of possible losses. We read the Company’s board Audit minutes, requested and received legal counsel confirmation letters, met with legal counsel to discuss the nature of certain matters and obtained representations from management on these matters. We also evaluated the appropriateness of the related disclosures included in the consolidated financial statements.
p2167: Fair Value of Convertible Notes Description The Company accounts for its convertible promissory notes at fair value. As discussed in of the Note 4 to the consolidated financial statements, the estimated fair value of convertible Matter promissory notes as of December 31, 2025, was $41.7 billion and the recognized loss for the change in the fair value of the convertible promissory notes for the year ended December 31, 2025, was $34.5 billion. The Company estimated the fair value of the convertible promissory notes using a hybrid approach comprising a contingent claims analysis method and a common stock equivalent method which involved the use of complex and subjective estimates, judgments and assumptions.
p2168: Auditing the Company’s estimated fair value of convertible notes was especially challenging due to the significant judgment required to assess management’s selection of the valuation methodology, determination of the relative weight applied to the contingent claims analysis and the common stock equivalent methods, which involved key judgments and assumptions, including the Company’s stage of development, likelihood of an initial public offering (IPO), need for and terms of financings, and secondary and other market transactions. The estimated fair value of the convertible notes is particularly sensitive to changes in the relative weight applied to the two valuation methods.
p2169: How We We performed audit procedures that included, among others, evaluating the Company’s Addressed selection of the valuation methodology, evaluating the key judgments and assumptions the Matter noted above used by the Company’s valuation specialist, and evaluating the in Our completeness and accuracy of the underlying data supporting the key judgments and Audit assumptions. We involved our valuation specialists to assist with our evaluation of the methodology used by the Company and the key judgments and assumptions. Specifically, we focused on the Company’s determination of the relative weight applied to the contingent claims analysis and common stock equivalent methods and the key judgments and assumptions that affected the weighting. For example, we evaluated the stage of the Company’s development, inspected the Company’s written plans and internal presentations relating to an IPO process, and evaluated secondary and other market transactions during the period and their impact on the relative weight applied to the two valuation methods by the Company.

p2208: Anthropic, PBC (the “Company”) is a public benefit corporation (“PBC”) incorporated under Delaware law in January 2021. The Company develops and maintains advanced artificial intelligence (“AI”) models and provides its intelligence service through its platform and applications to customers. The Company’s public benefit purpose is to responsibly develop and maintain advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity. The Company is headquartered in San Francisco, California.
p2209: The accompanying consolidated financial statements have been prepared in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (“GAAP”). The Company consolidates its wholly owned subsidiaries over which it exercises control, as well as variable interest entities (“VIEs”) where the Company is deemed to be the primary beneficiary. All intercompany balances and transactions between consolidated entities have been eliminated in consolidation.
p2210: Certain amounts reported in the Company’s prior period consolidated financial statements have been reclassified to conform to the current period presentation. During the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company changed its presentation of operating expenses from a functional classification under which cost of revenue, gross profit (loss), research and development, sales and marketing, and general and administrative were presented as separate line items, to a classification based on the nature of expenses. As a result of this change in presentation, cost of revenue, gross profit (loss), research and development, sales and marketing, and general and administrative are no longer presented as separate line items in the consolidated statements of operations.
p2211: Under the new presentation, expenses are presented by major categories, including compute and infrastructure; personnel; sales, marketing, and partnerships; Bartz settlement; and other operating and administrative. In addition, the Company combined certain captions on its consolidated balance sheets and consolidated statements of cash flows. These reclassifications and certain other prior period amounts have been recast for all prior periods presented to conform to the current period presentation. These reclassifications affect presentation only and did not impact total assets, total liabilities, total stockholders’ equity (deficit), total operating loss, net loss, or net cash provided by (used in) operating, investing, or financing activities.
p2212: The accompanying interim consolidated balance sheet as of June 30, 2026 and the interim consolidated statements of operations, comprehensive loss, redeemable convertible preferred stock and stockholders’ deficit, and cash flows for the six months ended June 30, 2025 and 2026 and the related notes to such interim consolidated financial statements are unaudited. p2213: On September 17, 2026, the Company effected a 10-for-1 stock split of its authorized, issued, and outstanding shares of Class A common stock and Class N common stock. The conversion rate of the Company’s redeemable convertible preferred stock was proportionately adjusted to factor in the stock split. On the same date, the Company also effected a 1-for-1,000 reverse stock split of its authorized and issued shares of Class T common stock. All share and per share information has been retroactively adjusted to reflect the stock split and reverse stock split for all periods presented.

p2215: The preparation of consolidated financial statements in conformity with GAAP requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities, revenues and expenses, and related disclosures of contingent assets and liabilities in the consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes. Actual results could differ materially from those estimates. Significant items subject to such estimates and assumptions include the determination of the fair value of common stock, valuation of deferred tax assets and the related valuation allowance, the potential outcome of uncertain tax positions that have been recognized in the consolidated financial statements or tax returns, valuation of the simple agreements for future equity (“SAFEs”), valuation of convertible notes, valuation of goodwill, stock-based compensation, the assessment of useful lives of long-lived assets and intangible assets, contingencies, the valuation of financial instruments, and incremental borrowing rates for operating and finance leases.
p2216: Financial instruments that potentially subject the Company to concentrations of credit risk consist principally of cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash, accounts receivable, and short-term investments. The Company maintains cash with financial institutions of high credit quality and has not experienced any losses on such accounts and does not believe it is exposed to any unusual credit risk beyond the normal credit risk associated with commercial banking relationships. p2235: Fair value is defined as the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. In accordance with Accounting Standards Codification (“ASC”) 820, Fair Value Measurement (“ASC 820”), the Company uses the fair value hierarchy, which prioritizes the inputs used to measure fair value. The hierarchy, as defined below, gives the highest priority to unadjusted quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities and the lowest priority to unobservable inputs. The three levels of the fair value hierarchy are set forth below:
p2236: Level 1: Observable inputs such as quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities.
p2237: Level 2: Observable inputs other than Level 1 prices such as quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities in active markets, quoted prices in markets that are not active or inputs other than the quoted prices that are observable either directly or indirectly for the full term of the assets or liabilities.
p2238: Level 3: Unobservable inputs in which there is little or no market data and that are significant to the fair value of the assets or liabilities.

p2252: Long-lived assets, such as property and equipment, right-of-use (“ROU”) assets, and finite-lived intangible assets subject to amortization, are reviewed for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of an asset or asset group (collectively, the “asset group”) may not be recoverable. Recoverability of asset groups to be held and used is measured by comparing the carrying amount to the estimated undiscounted future cash flows expected to be generated. p2254: Goodwill represents the excess of the purchase price in a business combination over the fair value of net tangible and intangible assets acquired. Goodwill is not subject to amortization but is tested for impairment on an annual basis, performed in the fourth quarter of each year, or whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate the carrying value of the reporting unit may be in excess of the reporting unit’s fair value.
p2255: Goodwill is tested for impairment at the reporting unit level by first assessing the qualitative factors to determine whether it is more likely than not that the fair value of the Company’s single reporting unit is less than its carrying amount. Qualitative indicators assessed include consideration of macroeconomic, industry, and market conditions, the Company’s overall financial performance, and personnel or strategy changes. Based on the qualitative assessment, if the Company determines that it is more likely than not that the Company’s single reporting unit’s fair value is less than its carrying amount, a quantitative analysis is performed by comparing the fair value of the Company’s single reporting unit to its carrying value. If the carrying amount of the reporting unit exceeds its fair value, an impairment loss is recognized in an amount equal to that excess, limited to the total amount of goodwill allocated to the reporting unit. The Company did not recognize any goodwill during the years ended December 31, 2023 and 2024. No impairment losses related to goodwill were recognized during the year ended December 31, 2025 or the six months ended June 30, 2026 (unaudited).

p2280: Stock-based compensation expense is recognized on a straight-line basis over the period during which an employee is required to provide services in exchange for the award (generally the vesting period of the award). p2281: • Fair value of common stock – Until the Company’s common stock is publicly traded, the Company must estimate the fair value of common stock. The Company’s board of directors (the “Board”) considers numerous objective and subjective factors to determine the fair value of the Company’s common stock including: contemporaneous third-party valuations of the Company’s common stock, price paid by investors for the Company’s common and redeemable convertible preferred stock, actual and forecasted operating and financial performance, market conditions, performance of comparable publicly traded companies, developments and milestones within the Company, the rights, preferences, and privileges of the Company’s common and redeemable convertible preferred stock, and the likelihood and timing of achieving a liquidity event, among other factors.
p2282: • Expected volatility – Expected volatility is a measure of the amount by which the stock price is expected to fluctuate. p2283: • Expected term – Expected term represents the period over which the Company anticipates stock-based awards to be outstanding. p2284: • Risk-free interest rate – The risk-free interest rate used is based on the implied yield in effect at the time of grant of U.S. Treasury securities with maturities similar to the expected term of the stock options.
p2285: • Expected dividend yield – The expected dividend yield is zero, as the Company has never declared or paid any dividends and has no current plans to do so.

p2294: The Company uses the asset and liability method to account for income taxes. Current income tax expense or benefit represents the amount of income taxes expected to be payable or refundable for the current year. Under this method, deferred income tax assets and liabilities are determined based on differences between the financial statement reporting and tax bases of assets and liabilities and net operating loss and credit carryforwards. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted tax rates applied to taxable income in the years in which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled. Valuation allowances are established when necessary to reduce deferred tax assets to the amounts that are more-likelythan-not expected to be realized based on the weighting of positive and negative evidence. Future realization of deferred tax assets ultimately depends on the existence of sufficient taxable income of the appropriate character (for example, ordinary income or capital gain) within the carryback or carryforward periods available under the applicable tax law. The Company regularly reviews the deferred tax assets for recoverability based on historical taxable income, projected future taxable income, the expected timing of the reversals of existing temporary differences and tax planning strategies. The Company’s judgment regarding future profitability may change due to many factors, including future market conditions and the ability to successfully execute the business plans and/or tax planning strategies. Should there be a change in the ability to recover deferred tax assets, the Company’s income tax provision would increase or decrease in the period in which the assessment is changed. The Company treats Net CFC Tested Income (formerly referred to as Global Intangible Low-Taxed Income or “GILTI”) as a period cost.
p2295: The Company accounts for uncertain tax positions in accordance with ASC 740-10, Accounting for Uncertainty in Income Taxes. The Company recognizes accrued interest and penalties related to unrecognized tax benefits in the provision for income taxes in the consolidated statements of operations.

p2299: Basic net loss per share is computed by dividing the net loss attributable to common stockholders by the weighted-average number of shares of common stock outstanding during the period, less shares subject to repurchase. The diluted net loss per share is computed by giving effect to all potentially dilutive securities outstanding for the period using the treasury stock method or the if-converted method if the effect is dilutive. For periods in which the Company reports net losses, diluted net loss per share is the same as basic net loss per share, because all potentially dilutive securities are anti-dilutive.
p2300: In November 2023, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (“FASB”) issued Accounting Standards Update (“ASU”) 2023-07, Segment Reporting (Topic 280): Improvements to Reportable Segment Disclosures (“ASU Anthropic, PBC Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (Continued)

p2302: In December 2023, the FASB issued ASU 2023-09, Income Taxes (Topic 740): Improvements to Income Tax Disclosures (“ASU 2023-09”). p2303: In July 2025, the FASB issued ASU 2025-05, Financial Instruments—Credit Losses (Topic 326): Measurement of Credit Losses for Accounts Receivable and Contract Assets (“ASU 2025-05”). ASU 2025-05 provides all entities with a practical expedient when estimating expected credit losses for current accounts receivable and current contract assets arising from transactions accounted for under ASC 606. All entities may elect a practical expedient that assumes that current conditions as of the balance sheet date do not change for the remaining life of the asset. The amendments in this ASU will be effective for annual reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2025, and interim reporting periods within those annual reporting periods. Early adoption is permitted in both interim and annual reporting periods in which financial statements have not yet been issued or made available for issuance. The Company early adopted ASU 2025-05, effective January 1, 2025, electing the practical expedient and applying the guidance prospectively. This ASU did not have a significant impact to the Company’s consolidated financial statements.
p2304: In September 2025, the FASB issued ASU 2025-06, Intangibles—Goodwill and Other—Internal-Use Software (Subtopic 350-40): Targeted Improvements to the Accounting for Internal-Use Software (“ASU 2025-06”). ASU 2025-06 modernizes the guidance for costs incurred in connection with internal-use software by removing references to prescriptive development stages. Under ASU 2025-06, an entity may begin capitalizing internaluse software costs when (a) management, with the relevant authority, implicitly or explicitly authorizes and commits to funding a computer software project and (b) it is probable that the project will be completed and the software will be used to perform the function intended (the “probable-to-complete recognition threshold”). ASU 2025-06 is effective for annual reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2027, and interim periods within those annual reporting periods; early adoption is permitted. The ASU may be adopted prospectively, retrospectively, or via a modified prospective transition. The Company early adopted ASU 2025-06, effective January 1, 2025, applying the guidance on a prospective basis. This ASU did not have a significant impact to the Company’s consolidated financial statements.
p2305: In November 2024, the FASB issued ASU 2024-03, Disaggregation of Income Statement Expenses (Subtopic 220-40) (“ASU 2024-03”), and in January 2025, the FASB issued ASU 2025-01, Income Statement-Reporting Comprehensive Income-Expense Disaggregation Disclosures (Subtopic 220-40): Clarifying the Effective Date (“ASU 2025-01”). p2341: During the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company entered into a contract to receive warrant rights to acquire common shares of a privately-held company as consideration under an agreement entered into but not yet commenced. The warrant rights are freestanding financial instruments that meet the definition of a derivative as they contain a net settlement feature. The warrants have not been designated as hedging instruments and will be granted and recognized as lease incentives upon commencement of the related arrangements and recognized as a reduction of the related ROU assets. The Company estimated the fair value of the warrant rights using a probability-weighted expected return method. In applying this method, the Company utilized Level 3 valuation inputs based on information available, including terms and features of the warrant rights and other outstanding classes of the issuer’s equity securities, observable transactions in the issuer’s securities such as its most recent financing round, estimates of equity volatility, and expected time to a liquidity event. The initial fair value of the warrant rights was recognized as a derivative asset classified within other assets on the consolidated balance sheets, with a corresponding deferred liability classified within other noncurrent liabilities.

p2343: In March 2026 (unaudited), the Company entered into a note purchase agreement (the “Google 2026 NPA”) with Google LLC (“Google”), which included a commitment to sell 38.6 million shares of the Company’s Series G-2 redeemable convertible preferred stock at $259.1364 per share. In April 2026 (unaudited), the Company entered into a note purchase agreement (the “Amazon 2026 NPA”) with Amazon Web Services, Inc. (“Amazon”), which included a commitment to sell 19.3 million shares of the Company’s Series G-2 redeemable convertible preferred stock at $259.1364 per share. Refer to Note 9 and Note 16 for further information. These agreements are marked-to-market each period. Changes in fair value are recognized in other income (expense), net on the consolidated statements of operations. Assets under these note purchase agreements are recorded at fair value within other assets, noncurrent on the consolidated balance sheet.
p2344: The estimated fair value of the note purchase agreements was determined by using a probability-weighted expected return method. The fair value of the Series G-2 redeemable convertible preferred stock was determined by using a hybrid approach comprising a contingent claims analysis (“CCA”) and a common stock equivalent (“CSE”) method. Assumptions included assumed future liquidity and financing events, the terms and features of the agreement, weights applied to each scenario, discount rates, applicable risk free rates, the fair value of the Series G-2 redeemable convertible preferred stock, and a discount for lack of marketability.
p2345: Level 3 liabilities consist of the SAFE liabilities (Note 9), convertible notes (Note 9), derivative liabilities (Note 9), donation matching program liability (Note 10), and a holdback liability for a portion of shares issuable in the acquisition of Codeblog Corp. (“Bun”) (Note 15). There is no current market for these liabilities such that determination of fair value requires significant judgment or estimation. Changes in fair value measurements categorized within Level 3 of the fair value hierarchy are analyzed each period based on changes in estimates or assumptions and recorded as appropriate. The Company recorded a $3 million change in fair value of the holdback liability during the year ended December 31, 2025 in other income (expense), net in the consolidated statements of operations.
p2346: The SAFE liabilities are recorded at fair value, which is determined based on a third-party valuation utilizing a scenario-based analysis and a CCA, that considers specific scenarios that factor in timing, probability, and financing size. This model takes into account the contract terms as well as multiple inputs, such as the Company’s redeemable convertible preferred stock price, risk free interest rates, and expected volatility, some of which the Company could not corroborate with observable market data. The assumptions used in valuing the SAFE liability upon conversion on December 31, 2023 and on January 30, 2024, include volatility, risk free interest rate, and term to liquidity. Changes in the fair value measurement of the SAFE liabilities relate to the conversion scenarios and are recorded as change in fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFEs in the consolidated statements of operations. All SAFEs have been converted as of December 31, 2024.
p2347: The estimated fair value of the convertible notes is determined by using a hybrid approach comprising a CCA and a CSE method. The analysis estimates the fair value of the convertible notes based on the probabilityweighted expected future investment returns, considering possible outcomes available to the note holder, including conversions to redeemable convertible preferred stock, Class N common stock, and maturity. Assumptions include weight applied to the CCA and CSE methods, assumed volatility, time to a liquidity event, need for and terms of financings or expected financings, and the risk free interest rate. Changes in fair value of the convertible notes are recorded as change in fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFEs in the consolidated statements of operations.

p2405: In September 2023, the Company entered into a note purchase agreement (“Google 2023 NPA”) with Google LLC (“Google”), for the issuance of convertible promissory notes in an aggregate principal amount of up to $2.0 billion, issuable in three tranches. The Company issued the first tranche of notes in an aggregate principal amount of $500 million in September 2023, the second tranche of notes in an aggregate principal amount of $750 million in September 2024, and the third tranche of notes in an aggregate principal amount of $750 million in September 2025.
p2406: The notes issued under Google 2023 NPA bore interest at a rate of 10.0% per annum, compounded annually, and payable upon maturity, 48 months after the respective issuance date. The Company also has a commercial agreement with Google for the provision of intelligence service.
p2407: In connection with the Company’s Series E-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock financing in 2025, the first and second tranches of notes issued under Google 2023 NPA converted in full into an aggregate of 12.7 million shares of the Company’s Series E-3 non-voting redeemable convertible preferred stock at a conversion price of $44.8692 per share and an aggregate of 15.3 million shares of Series E-4 non-voting redeemable convertible preferred stock at a conversion price of $50.4779 per share, respectively. The conversion prices reflect the contractual discounts to the Series E-1 original issuance price of $56.0865 per share. As of December 31, 2025, $750 million aggregate principal amount remained outstanding under the third tranche of notes issued under Google 2023 NPA.

p2420: Any conversion of the notes issued under an Amazon NPA is subject to Amazon’s aggregate ownership cap, which is waivable at Amazon’s option. p2434: The Company determined that the SAFEs are not legal form debt (i.e., no creditors’ rights). The monetary settlement amount of the SAFEs is based upon a fixed or determinable amount known at inception, and the number of equity shares received upon conversion is variable. In such circumstances, equity classification is not appropriate because such contracts that are settled based upon a fixed amount do not expose the holder to risks and rewards similar to those of an equity-holder, therefore, the SAFEs would have been classified as marked-tomarket liabilities pursuant to ASC 480.
p2435: As of December 31, 2024 and 2025, as well as June 30, 2026 (unaudited), the Company had no outstanding SAFEs.
p2436: The Company elected to account for the SAFEs and the convertible notes using the fair value option pursuant to ASC 825 and changes in fair value related to the SAFEs and convertible notes are recorded in change in fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFEs in the Company’s consolidated statements of operations (Note 4). The Company elected to account for the convertible notes using the fair value option pursuant to ASC 825 to eliminate the accounting complexity that would otherwise result from separately accounting for the liability and equity components of the convertible notes under the traditional bifurcation model.
p2437: The estimated fair value of the convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFEs is determined by using a scenario-based analysis that estimated the fair value of the convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFEs based on the probability-weighted present value of expected future investment returns, considering possible outcomes available to the SAFE and convertible note holder, including conversions to redeemable convertible preferred stock, Class N common stock and maturity. Issuance costs were expensed as incurred and are reflected in other income (expense), net in the consolidated statements of operations. Changes in fair value of the SAFEs and convertible notes and accrued interest are recorded as change in fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFEs in the consolidated statements of operations.

p2440: On May 14, 2025, the Company entered into a credit agreement (the “Credit Agreement”), by and among the Company, the lenders from time to time party thereto (collectively the “Lenders”), and Morgan Stanley Senior Funding, Inc., as Administrative Agent and Collateral Agent for the Lenders. The Credit Agreement provides for a senior secured revolving credit facility in an aggregate principal amount of $2.5 billion, with a $400 million letter of credit sublimit. The obligations under the Credit Agreement mature on May 14, 2030, subject to an earlier springing maturity date that is contingent upon the outstanding amount of convertible notes issued by the Company on the date that is 91 days prior to the maturity of such notes. The proceeds of the credit facility may be used for working capital, general corporate purposes, and other lawful purposes. p2441: Agreement. Borrowings under the Credit Agreement bear interest at rates based on either the Alternate Base Rate, Term SOFR or other applicable benchmarks, plus an applicable margin.
p2442: The Company is required to pay commitment fees on the unused portion of the credit facility and fees in connection with letters of credit. The obligations under the Credit Agreement are guaranteed by certain subsidiaries of the Company and are secured by substantially all of the assets of the Company and the subsidiary guarantors, subject to certain exceptions and exclusions set forth in the Credit Agreement. The Credit Agreement contains customary affirmative and negative covenants, including, but not limited to, restrictions on additional indebtedness, liens, asset sales, investments, mergers, and restricted payments. The Company is also subject to a financial covenant which requires the Company to maintain liquidity of at least $500 million as of the last day of each fiscal quarter. p2467: The holders of the redeemable convertible preferred stock have no voluntary rights to redeem shares. Therefore, all shares of redeemable convertible preferred stock have been presented outside of permanent equity.
p2468: The Company recorded shares of redeemable convertible preferred stock issued for cash at their respective issuance price less issuance costs on the dates of issuance. The carrying values of the Company’s redeemable convertible preferred stock have not been accreted to their redemption values as the liquidation event is not considered probable of occurring. Subsequent adjustments of the carrying values to redemption values will be made only if and when it becomes probable the convertible preferred stock will become redeemable.

p2470: The Company has one class of capital stock designated “participating common stock” and another class of capital stock designated “Class T common stock.” The class of capital stock designated “participating common stock” is divided into two series, designated “Class A common stock” and “Class N common stock.” The certificate of incorporation, as amended and restated August 27, 2025, authorized the Company to issue up to 8,162.8 million shares of Class A common stock, 5,547.2 million shares of Class N common stock, and 1 share of Class T common stock. p2483: The Company grants RSUs to employees and the RSUs vest upon the satisfaction of both a service condition and a performance condition. The service condition for these awards is generally satisfied over a four-year vesting period. The performance condition is satisfied upon the occurrence of an “initial event” which is defined as either (i) a qualifying change in control of the Company or (ii) a listing of the Company’s equity securities on an established securities market (including through a traditional public offering, direct listing, or business combination with a special purpose acquisition company), in each case, on or before the seventh anniversary of the grant date, as further defined in such RSU agreements. If the performance condition is not satisfied within seven years of the grant date, all unvested RSUs are forfeited.
p2484: As of December 31, 2025 and June 30, 2026 (unaudited), no stock-based compensation expense had been recognized for the RSUs because management determined that it is not probable that the performance condition will be achieved. If management had determined the performance condition was probable of achievement as of December 31, 2025 and June 30, 2026 (unaudited), the Company would have recognized $671 million and $2.9 billion, respectively, of cumulative stock-based compensation expense as of the respective dates and would have had $5.2 billion and $23.7 billion, respectively, of unrecognized compensation cost that represents the RSUs that have not satisfied the service condition for vesting. As of June 30, 2026 (unaudited), unrecognized compensation cost is expected to be recognized over a weighted-average period of 2.1 years.

p2541: The Company is involved from time to time in claims, proceedings, and litigation, including the following:
p2542: In August 2024, various authors filed suit against the Company alleging infringement of copyrighted books in the case of Bartz, et al. v. The complaint alleged, among other things, copyright infringement related to the use of literary works used in the training of the Company’s large language models. p2543: In October 2023, Concord Music Group et al. filed a complaint against the Company in the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Tennessee (“Concord I”).
